name: Ship the source, skip the companion record the diff owes
one_line: A change lands whose derived artifact, ledger row, or index link is owed in the same PR and is not in it — the committed binary, the derived queue, the CHANGELOG, the outbox block, the read-path link — because nothing computes the obligation from the diff.
trigger: PR open / pre-push, when `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD` intersects a path whose companion path is absent from the same diff
why_it_happens: Every one of these obligations is a true statement written in a README or plan and nowhere computable. The agent can see its own diff but has no table that says what that diff owes, so the debt is carried in memory and lost at the moment of PR open. Where a checker did exist it ran in a lane the diff had already routed around (docs-only fast path, `--check-only`, control-only fast lane).

proposed_fix: one checker, `check_companion_debt.py`, driven by a repo-local `.substrate/companions.json` of `{owes_when: <path glob or content regex>, owes: <path>, mode: present|regen}` rows — e.g. `games/*/src/** → dist/<game>.gba (regen)`, `docs/publishing/vetting/*.md → docs/publishing/OWNER-QUEUE.md (regen)`, `src/**|bench/*.py → CHANGELOG.md#[Unreleased] (present)`, `sb/spec/** → manifest.snapshot.json (regen)`, `.sessions/*.md matching '## 💡' → docs/ideas/*.md (present)`, `.sessions/*.md matching an owner-question block → docs/owner-questions.md (present)`, `docs/planning/** → a read-path link (present)`, `sims/verdict-NNN-* → control/outbox.md '## VERDICT NNN' (present)`. Predicate: for each row whose `owes_when` intersects `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD`, mode `present` fails when `owes` is absent from the same diff; mode `regen` runs the named generator and fails on a non-empty `git diff` (byte-idempotence). No generic diff→owed-companion table exists, so the pattern itself is "new"; the fix must not re-implement those four.

name: Act on the handoff's stated state instead of re-resolving it at HEAD
one_line: A baton, dispatch brief, wake prompt or pinned SHA states what is true; hours to weeks pass before it is read, and the session builds on a world that has moved.
trigger: Session boot / first tool call, on a prompt containing a PR number, a SHA, a version string, or a named next task.
why_it_happens: A handoff reads as authority rather than as a dated observation, and it is the first thing a cold session sees — before it has any tree knowledge to contradict it. TRAP-001 exists and is stated, but nothing delivers it at the moment the prompt is read.

proposed_fix: Chain: skill `prompt-preflight` -> hook `.claude/hooks/handoff_reresolve.py`. Hook half fires on `SessionStart` and `UserPromptSubmit`; it scans the incoming prompt for `#(\d+)`, `\b[0-9a-f]{7,40}\b`, `v\d+\.\d+\.\d+`, and `origin/main`, and prints a resolved table before the first tool call — each PR's live `state`/`merged_at` from the direct-PAT path, each SHA's `git merge-base --is-ancestor <sha> origin/main` result, each version against the tree's version homes, plus `git rev-parse origin/main` vs any SHA the prompt calls HEAD. Silent when the prompt names nothing resolvable; never blocks. Skill half: `prompt-preflight` gains a mandatory step 0 on the WRITE side — 'every #N, SHA, version and named next-task in the prompt you are about to write must be resolved at HEAD in this session and stamped with the resolution time, or replaced by a pointer to the live surface' — so the class is attacked at both the write and the read end. name: State N measured of M total, or don't write the count
one_line: A count, ratio or universal quantifier is published over a population larger than the set actually enumerated — the sample reads as a census.
trigger: Edit/Write adding a line containing a cardinal count, an 'N of M' ratio, or a universal/superlative scope word (every, all, none, only, full, app-wide, never, the only) over a population noun.
why_it_happens: Writing 'every' costs one word; enumerating costs a sweep. The measured set is in working memory and the unmeasured remainder is not, so the sentence is composed over what the session can see rather than over what it names.

name: Perform the session-card ceremony half-way
one_line: A PR lands with no session card at all, or with a card authored from memory whose mandated fields are missing or off-taxonomy — and the gate only grades a sampled window, so the drift ages out silently.
trigger: two moments, both hook-firable: (a) writing/editing a `.sessions/<date>-<slug>.md` file, and (b) opening a PR whose diff adds no `.sessions/*.md` on the full (non-control) lane
why_it_happens: The card is the one artifact every session must author and the only one authored free-hand from recall. The grammar lives in a README one hop from the template; the checker that grades it is advisory and windowed (10 newest cards / the mtime-picked card), so a violation is either not blocking or not seen. Card-less PRs escape entirely because the born-red gate is written to engage only when a PR *adds* a card — absence is its blind spot, stated verbatim in the superbot and superbot-next cites.

name: Run the command, then write the number
one_line: A figure is written into a card, PR body, retro or owner-facing message from memory, arithmetic-in-prose, or a tool's convenience summary line — never from the command that measures it — and it is wrong.
trigger: an Edit/Write whose added lines put a digits token (or a `~N` hedge) into `.sessions/*.md`, `docs/**/*.md`, a PR body, or an owner reply, with no measuring command in the same paragraph
why_it_happens: The number is a by-product of work the session already did, so it feels remembered rather than claimed. Estimating costs zero seconds and the counting command costs one; nothing at write time distinguishes a recalled figure from a measured one, and once written it is indistinguishable to every later reader. Under load the drift is systematically low (chat-side '~50' against 102, '~1,900' against 1,815), so the errors are not noise — they are a habit.

name: Write a verdict, closure or root cause without re-reading the artifact
one_line: 'Fixed', 'weak', 'every seam', 'PRIVATE', 'the cause is X' are written from memory, a doc badge, a truncated grep, a docstring or a secondhand pin — when one command against the live artifact would have settled it, and repeatedly did not agree.

name: Land a guard, test or checker that has never been seen red
one_line: A new assertion, fixture, checker predicate or verifier is written, run once green, and cited as proof — with no run in which it fails, so guards that are structurally incapable of failing ship as safety.
trigger: Edit/Write that adds a test, assert, fixture, or a check_*.py predicate — and the moment the session writes 'covered / pinned / guarded / verified' about it, before the PR opens.
why_it_happens: Writing the check and proving the check are two different acts, and only the first has a natural stopping point. A green run feels like completion, so the falsification run never gets scheduled. Several instances show the broken code returning the right answer by coincidence (positional fallback, palette-ordered fixture, redundant second mechanism), which no amount of re-reading the test exposes — only mutating the guarded line does.

name: Leave the session's own coordination residue on main at close
one_line: Claim files, spent branches, armed wake triggers and uncommitted telemetry lines survive their session, so the next reader sees a false 'this is claimed / this is next / this is in flight' signal that costs a real investigation to disprove.
trigger: The flip-to-complete commit, after the session's PR has reached merged state.
why_it_happens: The residue is created at session START, when its cleanup is a distant abstraction, and its deletion moment is after the PR merges — past the point the session considers itself finished. TRAP-006 guards the card flip but says nothing about what the session leaves behind.

name: A borrowed figure restated as if measured
one_line: A number that arrived from somewhere else — a dispatch brief, a prior card, a sub-agent row, a bot summary, another repo's heartbeat — is repeated as current fact without being re-derived, and it was already wrong or already stale.
trigger: a UserPromptSubmit or file read whose text contains a figure attributed to another record (`the brief said`, `per the prior card`, `as relayed`, `the summary reports`), immediately followed by that figure appearing in an Edit to a doc or in a reply
why_it_happens: An inbound figure arrives already formatted as a fact, so re-deriving it feels like distrusting a colleague rather than doing the work. The cost asymmetry is invisible: the producing session paid nothing for the estimate, and every downstream reader inherits it at full confidence. Sub-agent and bot output is worst — it looks measured because a tool produced it, but the tool measured something else, or nothing.

name: A written reference that does not resolve
one_line: A path, line number, SHA, quotation or 'filed in X' destination written into a record where the target does not exist, does not contain the claimed content, or was never actually written.
trigger: a Write/Edit adding a backticked repo path, a `path:LINE` cite, a 7–40 char SHA, an attributed quotation, or a destination claim `(filed|captured|routed|recorded|indexed|documented|noted) (in|to|as) <path>` — and equally, the moment an external review reply citing any of those is about to be acted on
why_it_happens: A citation is generated by the same fluency that generates prose, and its shape carries all the authority while none of the verification. Two sub-cases compound it: a 'filed in X' claim is written at the moment of intending to file, and the filing is then batched away or lost in a rebase; and a quotation from an external agent arrives already looking like evidence. `check_baton_resolves` covers exactly one venue (the baton line) in one repo.

name: The only copy lives outside the readable repo
one_line: A fact, evidence pack or recipe the estate needed was produced in a session and left in chat, the scratchpad, a PR body or a transcript, so it evaporated with the container.
trigger: at end of turn / session close, when the session measured something, was denied something, provisioned something, or produced an analysis, and the branch diff adds no committed file carrying it
why_it_happens: Producing the knowledge and committing it are separate acts, and the producing session already has the knowledge — so the value of writing it down is entirely external. Scratchpads and PR bodies feel like storage because they persist for the length of the session that can already see them.

name: A number whose definition was never stated — and was wrong
one_line: The count is arithmetically correct and measures the wrong thing: a mis-set instrument, an inclusion predicate that does not match the claim, a mismatched denominator, a proxy standing in for the quantity, a simulator nobody calibrated — published with the authority of a measurement.
trigger: an Edit/Write adding a percentage, rate (`/s`, `per`), coverage fraction, ranking, `N of M`, or a certainty label (`MEASURED`) to a findings doc, card, or owner-facing artifact

name: Accept a clean result from an instrument never shown able to report the failure

proposed_fix: New PostToolUse hook `.claude/hooks/retraction_sweep.py`, firing on Edit/Write. name: The merge lands, the ledger row never does
one_line: A PR ships and the living state doc or program progress ledger is never updated, so the surface a cold session reads third describes a repo several merges — sometimes seventeen slices, sometimes five days — in the past.
trigger: At session close, after the session's PR reaches merged state, before the card is flipped complete.
why_it_happens: The ledger entry is the one piece of work whose natural moment is after the PR merges — i.e. after the session believes it is done, and often after auto-merge has landed it asynchronously. Every checklist that names the step runs before that moment.

name: Update one half of a pair of records that state the same fact
one_line: Where two surfaces carry one fact — status header vs body, card badge vs program row, Layer-2 vs Layer-1, src vs dist, directory vs its index — the session trues the one it came for and leaves the other asserting the old state, often inside the same file.
trigger: The commit that edits one member of a known record pair without touching the other.
why_it_happens: The session has a task-shaped view of the tree: it opens the surface its task names and edits the paragraph it came for. The pairing is a convention nobody holds in working memory, and in the within-file cases the stale half is often hundreds of lines below the edited one.

name: Note the finding instead of owning it
one_line: A checker advisory, a WARN, or a recorded 'deferred / disclosed / recommend' item is observed and left standing — the same item re-recorded three, five, seven sessions running, with narration substituting for the fix.
trigger: session close, when the strict run's advisory block is non-empty or the card is about to carry a `deferred|disclosed, not fixed|recommend|next session|carried` line
why_it_happens: An advisory finding names a defect and no owner. The session that reads it can always truthfully say the defect predates its diff, so the cheapest correct-looking act is to record it — which produces a card that reads diligent while the item survives. Disclosure is rewarded by the review ritual; closure is not. Nothing counts repeats, so the third instance costs exactly what the first did.

name: Record a wall after one route failed, never trying the second
one_line: A refusal on the proxied/MCP path is written into a ledger, card or doc as a capability limit while the direct-egress $GITHUB_PAT path (or any second route) is never attempted — the single largest sub-class here, and the estate's own capability matrix contradicts nearly every instance.
trigger: a tool call returns 403/401/denied/RESOURCE_INVALID and the session's NEXT write contains a limitation token (wall, blocked, cannot, owner-only, unavailable, 403) — hook-firable as PostToolUse on the failing call, and again as PreToolUse on the Edit/Write that records it
why_it_happens: A 403 is real evidence, so it does not feel like an assumption — but it is evidence about one path, not about the capability. The estate's own topology (a proxy that 403s where direct egress answers 200/204) makes the wrong inference the natural one, and the guard that exists cannot see any of these nouns.

name: Write a verification claim with no reproducible evidence trail

trigger: Writing a number, digest, exit code or review verdict into a card's Verify/close-out section, a PR body, or an outbox verdict block.
why_it_happens: The evidence existed in the session — a scratch script, a terminal buffer, a sibling PR's page — and the record captures the conclusion rather than the trail, because the trail is bulky and the conclusion is what the reader wants. name: Push without a green strict gate on the exact committed HEAD
one_line: The local gate is skipped, run partially, run against a dirty tree, run without the CI-only flag, or its exit code is swallowed — so CI discovers what one command would have.
trigger: PreToolUse on Bash matching `git push`, and on `create_pull_request`
why_it_happens: The gate is a command the agent must remember to run, in full, at the right moment, and then read honestly. Every failure mode here is a cheaper-looking variant that still returns green text: run the fast subset, run before committing, run without the flag CI adds, or pipe the output somewhere that eats the status. The estate's own doctrine ('one command is the local gate', 'never `$?` after a pipe') is stated in prose at exactly the place prose does not bind — the moment of typing `git push`.

name: Volatile state copied forward instead of re-probed at write time
one_line: PR state, trigger state, repo visibility, deploy state or another lane's progress written into a record from a prior record, a brief or memory — true when it was first written, false by the time it was written again.
trigger: a Write/Edit to a record file (.sessions/*.md, current-state.md, control/status.md, owner-queue.md, a handoff/close-out brief) whose added text contains a volatile token — `#\d+`, `trig_[A-Za-z0-9]+`, `PRIVATE|PUBLIC`, `armed|disarmed|parked|open|merged|blocked|in flight|awaiting|not started`
why_it_happens: A record is the cheapest source and it reads authoritative; the cost of a probe is paid at write time while the cost of staleness is paid by someone else, often hours later. TRAP-001 names the failure and `check_status_current` exists, but it checks that a file was touched, not that the volatile facts inside it were re-read — so a copied-forward line passes every gate the estate runs.

name: Ship enforcement that nothing actually invokes
one_line: A checker, workflow step, hook route or guard is written, merged and recorded as protection, while no invocation, flag, path filter, permission or required-check binding ever lets it run.
trigger: The commit or merge of a PR whose diff adds or edits a `check_*.py`, a `.github/workflows/*.yml` step, a hook route, or a doc badge saying 'implemented / enforced / gated' — before the PR body claims protection.
why_it_happens: The artifact's existence is the visible deliverable and the wiring is invisible: a script's body, a workflow file, a route entry all look complete on their own. Every failure here is one hop away from the thing that was checked — the flag argparse rejects, the `paths:` filter the test's input falls outside, the `permissions:` block the gh call needs, the ruleset row that makes a job required, the route already consumed earlier in the session.

name: A time value composed instead of read from the clock
one_line: A timestamp or date is written from the session's sense of when it is — pre-written before the work, rounded, hand-typed after a failed edit, computed in the head, or simply the wrong day — into fields other systems parse and other sessions trust.
trigger: an Edit/Write whose added lines contain an ISO-8601 stamp, a `YYYY-MM-DD` date, or a filename date segment, in a card, heartbeat/status file, provenance line, or planning doc
why_it_happens: A stamp is written at the start of a record and the record is finished later, so the honest value is unknowable at the moment the field is filled; rounding to the next minute or hour feels like tidiness rather than invention. Machine-parsed fields make it worse — the field must be filled to commit, so a placeholder or a guess goes in and nothing at write time compares it to `date -u`. When the correct date is one keystroke from the wrong one, a whole session's records inherit the error at once.

name: A citation that resolves to nothing
one_line: A precise-looking reference — a PR number written before the PR exists, a SHA that no longer resolves after squash-merge, a file:line that moved, a filename that was never the one committed — is published as provenance, and a later reader cannot follow it anywhere.
trigger: an Edit/Write adding a `#\d+` reference, a 7–40 char hex SHA, a `path:line` citation, or a bare path inside an Outcome/Evidence block, in a card, heartbeat, ORDER or findings doc
why_it_happens: The citation is written at the moment the session knows what it means and never re-read at the moment someone else needs it. Predicted PR numbers are the sharp case: the number is needed in the card before the PR exists, so it is guessed. Squash-merge and refactors quietly invalidate references that were true when written — the citation degrades without anyone touching it, and the more precise it looks the less anyone re-checks it.

name: Hand-write a machine-parsed record instead of using its verb
one_line: A control-plane record — heartbeat, claim, model line, append-log row, allowlist YAML, inbox entry — is typed by hand without reading its grammar; the parser then silently drops it or the gate rejects it.

name: Contradicted by an artifact in the same change

name: Say what the instrument asserts, not what you wanted it to prove
one_line: A checker, pin, test, digest or scan is described in prose that covers more than its own assertion — coverage restated as fidelity, filename sets as content, a matched digest as identity.

name: Act on a working tree you never pinned
one_line: A git or file mutation runs against whatever the ambient cwd resolves to — a checkout shared with a live sibling session, a second clone reached by `cd ~`, or the shared parent instead of the session's own worktree.
trigger: any mutating git/file command issued without an explicit `git -C <absolute worktree>` or an absolute cwd, in a container that holds more than one checkout or more than one live session
why_it_happens: cwd is invisible state. Nothing in the transcript shows which tree a Bash call resolved to, so the session's mental model of 'my branch' and the checkout's actual HEAD drift silently, and the divergence only surfaces as a clobbered branch or a dangling commit.

name: Counts and enumerations typed from memory
one_line: A number, tally or 'for each of' list written into a record by recall or by copying an inherited table, when it is mechanically derivable from the tree and disagrees with it.
trigger: a Write/Edit adding a digit adjacent to a countable noun (repos|cards|PRs|adopters|files|patches|checks|arcs|ORDERs|incidents), a 'for each / all N' universal, or an auto-drafted file list about to be committed
why_it_happens: There is no generator, so every count is hand-typed, and a count is the one claim that ages with the tree while sitting still in the doc. name: Absence asserted without the search that settles it
one_line: A 'there is no X / nothing does X / X is missing at HEAD' claim written from not-having-seen-it, when one grep or one list call would have found it.
trigger: a Write/Edit adding a negation next to a countable noun — `no|nothing|zero|never|none of` within ~60 chars of `exists|runs|executes|references|covers|implements|tags|releases|tests|in CI` — or `missing|absent at HEAD`
why_it_happens: Not finding something and it not existing are the same subjective experience, and an absence claim is the one kind that cannot be falsified by re-reading what you already read — it can only be falsified by a search you did not run. The `absence-claim` doc route exists but only delivers TRAP-003 as reading material at hub sessions; nothing blocks the write, and nothing runs in the satellite repos where 6 of these 10 landed.

one_line: 'PR #N did X' written from the number, title or commit subject, when the actual diff did something narrower — usually only filing the order text that the title names.
trigger: a Write/Edit adding `#\d+` or a 7–40 char SHA within ~5 tokens of an action verb (did / landed / shipped / upgraded / withdrew / built / executed / fixed / closed)
why_it_happens: A PR title is written to describe intent and is read as a description of outcome, and the two diverge exactly where it matters most — an order-filing commit is titled with the order it files. Nothing in the estate connects a `#N` in prose to that PR's file list, so the cheapest available evidence is also the most misleading.

name: Finish the work and never drive it to a terminal state
one_line: The session ends with its output stranded one call short — a green PR unmerged or parked as a draft, a pushed branch with no PR, a card pushed born-red and never flipped — with the merge intent left in session memory.
trigger: end of turn (Stop hook), for every branch pushed or PR opened during this session
why_it_happens: The session's own sense of completion arrives when the work is pushed and green — the remaining step is one API call whose absence produces no error, no red, and no signal anywhere the session looks. A skipped arming job is silent by design; a draft PR looks like a decision; a deferred merge lives only in the memory of a session that is about to end. Nothing wakes anyone to say a PR went green (subscribe_pr_activity does not deliver CI-success), so the stranded state is discoverable only by a deliberate poll that no one is obliged to run.

name: Describe a file you never opened
one_line: A sentence stating what a named file, symbol, workflow, skill or issue does, written from its filename, docstring, one-line description or someone else's characterisation rather than from its body.
trigger: a Write/Edit whose added text names a repo path, symbol or issue number next to a describing verb (does / reads / lacks / runs / builds / is a), where that path was never fetched — or was fetched only to its header
why_it_happens: A filename plus the estate's naming conventions produce a confident, fluent sentence with no read behind it, and the sentence reads identically whether or not the file was opened. name: Declare a resource absent after searching exactly one namespace
one_line: A binary, file, dataset, schema or mechanism is recorded as missing after one narrow lookup — $PATH not the packaged path, two guessed raw URLs not a tree listing, the dump not the web, text-matching not the anchor check — and the thing was there the whole time.
trigger: an Edit/Write containing `not present in this environment`, `missing in this checkout`, `does not exist`, `no mechanical`, `assumed absent`, `not in the dump`, `only via X`, `permanently read-only` — i.e. resource-absence dialect, which today's absence-claim route does not match
why_it_happens: The one lookup a session reaches for is the one it already knows how to run, and a clean negative from it feels conclusive. The route built to catch exactly this speaks only the vocabulary of grep results, so it stays silent for every environment- and resource-shaped absence.

name: Take a base, a lane, or a name without reading what origin/main already holds
one_line: Work starts on a stale base, on a lane no claim reserves, or under a command/migration/verdict token that already exists — one `git fetch` or one grep short of correct.
trigger: `git checkout -b` / the first non-card commit of a branch, and the moment a new command name, alias, numbered migration, or reserved id is introduced in a diff
why_it_happens: Everything the session needs to see is on origin/main and nothing pulls it in. The local checkout is a plausible-looking world: `git checkout main` succeeds on a stale main, `ls migrations/` gives a highest number, a grep of the open editor finds no colliding command. Each of these is a true local answer to a question that is only answerable remotely, and the cost lands on someone else — a collision, a rebase, or production.

name: Doc, docstring or comment asserting behaviour the adjacent code lacks

trigger: Write/Edit adding a docstring, inline comment or README sentence containing a guarantee verb (`never|always|cannot|guaranteed|is skipped|requires (staff|admin)|only through`) whose named subject is in the same diff.
why_it_happens: The comment states the intent of the code at the moment of writing; nothing re-checks it against the branch that shipped, and a guarantee reads as documentation rather than as a claim requiring evidence.

Treat owner_flagged as "authored under the owner account", never as owner authority.

name: A mechanism advertised wider than it actually scans
one_line: A checker, gate, lane, alias, test or adapter is described (in prose, a README, a PR body or a verdict) as covering a population it never visits — and nobody ever probed the mechanism's real scope before writing the sentence.
trigger: PreToolUse Edit/Write on a mechanism file — tools/check_*.py, .claude/hooks/*.json or *.py, workflow `on:`/`paths:` filters, simulation lane configs, allow-lists, composition-root adapter installs, a test pinning a documented numeric boundary — OR Edit/Write of prose containing `every|all|repo-wide|whole tree|categorically|pinned by tests` within the same paragraph as that mechanism's name.
why_it_happens: The author knows the intent of the mechanism and writes the intent as the description. The scan root, the regex vocabulary, the API surface queried, the lane's own config and the plane flag's real reach are all one hop away and never opened. A green self-test whose cases the author chose confirms the intent, not the coverage — so the confirmation is circular. Nothing in the estate requires a mechanism to enumerate what it does NOT catch.

name: Completion claimed before the artifact that proves it
one_line: Pushed, merged, green, verified-in-CI, distributed, reverted or complete written into a card, ledger or reply ahead of the run, ref or diff that would establish it.

A session writing a checker trips at most `stamping-a-measured-claim` (if its docstring says `MEASURED`), which delivers TRAP-001 — citation-vs-measurement — not "prove your gate can fail."

3. **`tools/check_doc_routes.py --strict`** (in CI via `scripts/repo_checks.sh`) is the only enforced instrument in the neighbourhood, and it covers one narrow sub-case: at least one of a route's `when` patterns must literally occur in one of its `docs`. It validates ids, empty `says`, prompt-route tool purity, regex compilation, doc existence. It does **not** check that the hook can parse the payload shapes the route declares in `tools`, and it has no notion of a negative fixture.

4. **`tools/test_doc_route_patterns.py`** is the pattern's proposed fix, already built — 17 pinned cases (10 must-fire, 3 must-be-silent, 4 shallow-clone) for exactly the "a narrowing edit looks like a widening" failure. But it covers **2 of 71 routes**, tests regexes not payloads, and is wired into nothing: it appears in no workflow, not in `scripts/repo_checks.sh`, not in `scripts/preflight.py`.

5. **The doctrine exists in prose in one place, applied once**: `docs/traps.md` § Coverage — *"Verified by positive control, not by a clean run — a clean result from a broken checker is TRAP-003 itself"* — written for `check_pipe_exit_code.py`'s 8 fixtures. It is a paragraph about one checker, not a rule with a trigger. `.claude/CLAUDE.md`'s *"A firing instrument is information; a quiet one is no evidence at all"* is likewise unenforced at write time.

6. **Kit side**: `check_folded_gate` is about mtime-vs-diff card selection, unrelated. `docs/findings/2026-08-28-substrate-kit-genesis-dig.md:220` names the general gap in its own words — *"friction→guard | law + tooling; **nothing checks a guard was created**"* — and its enforcement table records the same shape inside the kit (`check_card_residue` advisory-only/self-declared UNVERIFIED/never graduated; marker needles "merge-blocking **presence only**"). name: Success returned for a path that did nothing

name: An invented constant promoted to law or shipped as data
one_line: A threshold, price, cap or limit nobody measured is written into a checker, a BINDING rule, a capabilities ledger or product data — where its hedge is dropped on the first read and it binds every repo that inherits it.

name: Card born complete — the born-red merge hold never arms
one_line: The session card is written or flipped to `complete` before (or in) the first push, so the born-red hold that opens the review window never exists and the lander takes the PR within seconds — sometimes empty, sometimes dropping the very commit the session came to make.
trigger: `git push` (or `create_pull_request`) on a branch whose in-diff `.sessions/*.md` card already reads `Status: complete`, when the branch has no prior push

name: Stamp the cutoff and re-query before publishing a negative
one_line: A single point-in-time read published as a permanent "never happened", with no observation cutoff and no re-query at write time — then inherited by later documents.

proposed_fix: `check_absence_stamp.py`, run in `scripts/preflight.py` and required in `substrate-gate`. Predicate: any added line matching `\b(NO ACK|never (delivered|answered|acked|ran|happened)|no (run|heartbeat|reply|ack)\b|missed (the )?(slot|window)|went dark|\bidle\b|not installed|still unanswered)\b` must carry, on the same line or the one below, BOTH (i) an ISO-8601 `as of YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MMZ` observation cutoff and (ii) `re-queried at write: <command|endpoint>`. name: The repair is the new defect — fixing a review finding regresses a passing case
one_line: A fix authored in response to a reviewer finding widens or rewrites a predicate and breaks the mirror case, so the next round's finding is caused by the previous round's fix.
trigger: PreToolUse Edit on a file already touched by this branch, where the branch has an unresolved PR review comment — i.e. any second-or-later edit to the same predicate/function in one PR.
why_it_happens: The fix is validated against the one case the reviewer named. No before/after corpus exists, so 'the finding is gone' is mistaken for 'nothing else moved' — the repair's claim is wider than the case that produced it.

name: Displayed value never reconciled with the value it describes
one_line: A user-facing string — a computed delta, an arithmetic identity, an effect label, a PR link — is emitted next to the source it claims to explain without either being derived from or checked against it.
trigger: Write/Edit that builds a user-facing string embedding a computed number, an a−b=c identity, an effect-scope label, or an externally returned identifier/URL.
why_it_happens: The display layer is written from the intent of the change, not from the function that computes it; the two are never made to meet, so the copy describes what the author meant rather than what shipped.

proposed_fix: Per-surface property tests, each decidable: displayed delta == delta recomputed by the canonical rate function for every purchase/effect; an arithmetic identity string is emitted only when round(a-b,2)==c, else suppressed; a rendered external identifier may only read a field written by the verification step, with create/reuse mismatch failing closed; each declared effect scope must equal the exact set of rate fields the modifier touches (table test binding label → source field).

why_it_happens: Cards note 'this pattern still isn't routed' and then flip complete; routing is nobody's slice. name: Arm or land a merge on a stale read of the PR's state
one_line: Auto-merge is armed, a PR opened, or a commit pushed against a picture of the PR taken earlier — a webhook payload, a base from before origin/main moved, a head from before the heartbeat commit, or a branch already merged.
trigger: at `enable_pr_auto_merge` / `create_pull_request` / any `git push` or commit onto a branch that has a PR
why_it_happens: GitHub's PR state is asynchronous and the estate has measured ~25 min MCP staleness. A payload or a listing read minutes ago still looks authoritative, and every one of these calls succeeds against the stale picture.

name: "Merged and green" mistaken for delivered
one_line: Work is judged complete at merge-plus-CI-green when the real deliverable is a live service, an installable build, a committed binary or a reachable UI path — so a finished feature sits dark, uninstallable, or undownloadable behind a green ledger.
trigger: session close, when the diff touches a path the repo declares as feeding a delivery surface (deployable service, build identity file, `dist/`, an owner-action row naming an artifact)
why_it_happens: CI green is the only completion signal that arrives on its own. Every other delivery surface has to be gone and looked at, and the session's mental model of "done" is shaped by the signal that pushes itself.
instances: [spider-swing] .sessions/2026-08-02-build-034-speed-cap.md:62 — "the work was judged complete at *merged and green*, when the actual deliverable is *the owner can play it and tell it apart*"; no build cut, so the fix was uninstallable in practice

(1) A committed `docs/delivery-surface.md` per repo declaring, per delivered path glob, how delivery is observed — a version endpoint URL, a `dist/<name>.<ext>` artifact, a build identity file, or `none (library)`. (2) `check_delivery_reaches_surface.py` in `scripts/preflight.py`: if the session diff touches any declared glob, assert the surface is current — fetch the version endpoint and require it to report the merge SHA, or require the named `dist/` artifact to exist AND its hash to differ from the previous commit's. name: New checker shipped without being run against a clean tree or a non-default config
one_line: A checker is added and only exercised against the dirty case it was written for, so it hardcodes paths the config already carries, false-reds a healthy tree, or crashes the whole local gate on an ordinary input.
trigger: PreToolUse Edit adding a function to `bootstrap.py`'s checker scope, or any new `tools/check_*.py` / `tools/*_activity.py` — specifically a literal `"docs"` path join inside a function that receives `config`, an unguarded `read_text(`, or `.replace()`/`.strip()` on an API response field.
why_it_happens: The checker is validated by watching it catch the thing it was written to catch. Nobody runs it on a pristine generated tree, an adopter with a different `docs_root`, an empty repo, or twice in a row — so false red, false green and hard crash all ship together.
instances: gba-homebrew #215 r3778219014 — new checker scans `target/docs` while adopters set `docs_root`; measurement documents are silently skipped and the provenance advisory false-greens
venture-lab #289 r3778256269 — identical hardcoded `docs` with the `config` object already in hand and every sibling checker resolving `config.docs_root`

idea-engine #899 r3778313754 — the boot-path loop treats every extracted token as mandatory although the template marks `HANDOFF.md` 'when present', emitting `boot-path-unresolved` for a healthy generated agreement

websites #499 r3778139391 — unguarded `read_text` in a new advisory checker turns an unreadable file into a crash of the entire `bootstrap.py check`
fleet-manager #947 r3864873056 — `pushed_at: null` on a new empty repo raises `AttributeError` and aborts the whole estate refresh instead of classifying one repo
fleet-manager #963 r3883064474 — the advertised regression suite leaks hook state, so a second run against the same TMPDIR fails on a clean tree
proposed_fix: A `checker-selftest` lane in `scripts/preflight.py` that every checker must pass: (a) run against a pristine generated tree → zero findings; (b) run against the same tree with `docs_root` renamed → identical findings; (c) run twice in the same TMPDIR → identical exit codes; (d) run with one target file made unreadable and one API fixture field null → a finding, never an exception. Plus three decidable lints: literal `'docs'` path join in a function whose signature takes `config` and never references `config.docs_root`; bare `read_text(`/`open(` in `bootstrap.py` checker scope not wrapped in try/except; existence check on a path string containing `#`.
maps_to_existing_trap: new — nearest TRAP-003 (a quiet checker read as evidence of cleanliness)
already_covered_by: Genuinely new; the pattern's own "nearest TRAP-003" self-assessment is accurate. docs/traps.md:96 defines TRAP-003 as "Absence of evidence recorded as evidence of absence", which covers reading a quiet checker as cleanliness — adjacent to the false-green half of this pattern but not to the false-red-on-a-pristine-tree or hard-crash halves, and TRAP-003 is about interpreting a checker's output rather than about validating a newly authored checker. No existing trap covers "new checker exercised only against the dirty case it was written for". Note docs/traps.md:378 records TRAP-003 as "1 route / not yet" enforced, so it would not have caught any of these either.

Nothing. scripts/preflight.py's six lanes (added-card, doc routes, false walls, pipe exit code, owner-comment contract, owner-comment regression) contain no checker-selftest lane, and no lane runs any checker against a generated tree. docs/traps.md's coverage table marks TRAP-003 'not yet' for a deterministic checker. The only precedent is prose about a single checker — TRAP-002's check_pipe_exit_code.py was 'verified by positive control, not by a clean run' with 8 fixtures — which is this pattern applied once by hand, not a lane any new checker must pass.
owner_flagged_premise: VOID — the lane that set this assumed every menno420-authored review comment was the owner speaking. The identity-collision finding (docs/findings/2026-08-29-estate-agent-error-audit.md §1) establishes that agents post under the owner PAT, so no GitHub text is attributable to him. name: Read an exit code after a pipe or a background wrapper
one_line: The gate is run through `| tail`, `| grep` or a backgrounded wrapper and `$?` is read — so the reported exit code belongs to the last stage and every 'gate exit 0' from that shape was never a measurement.
trigger: The Bash call itself: a command line containing a pipe (or `&`/`nohup`) whose status is then read with `$?`, `echo "X=$?"`, or `&&`.
why_it_happens: Piping to `tail` is how a long gate is made readable, and the pipe is added for display reasons at the exact moment the exit code becomes load-bearing. The failure is silent and inverted — it always reports success — so nothing in the output invites a second look. The estate has restated this in 26 of 389 cards and it still fired on 2026-08-22.
instances: [shiftlife] .sessions/2026-07-26-plan-conformance.md:78 — `check --strict | tail -3; echo GATE=$?`; every prior 'gate exit 0' from that shape was unfounded
[couch-legend] .sessions/2026-08-22-android-signing-identity.md:63 — `$?` after a grep reported a false 0 and had to be re-measured
product-forge · .sessions/2026-08-20-phone-controller-slice22-foldables.md:69 — an in-session $?-after-a-pipe misread, disclosed and re-run with real exit codes
websites · .sessions/2026-07-11-fastlane-control-gates.md:35 — the check printed its finding and reported exit 0 because `$?` came from `tail`; unpiped re-run gave exit 1
[superbot] .sessions/2026-06-09-mining-descent-persistent-depth.md:40 — `check_quality.py --full | tail -40` reported tail's 0 while pytest had failed; a regression hid under it
superbot · .sessions/2026-06-24-setup-spine-build.md:23 — a backgrounded pytest/check_quality reported 0 while 13 tests failed
date_span: 2026-06-09 → 2026-08-22 (5 repos, 2.5 months — recurring after the route existed)
proposed_fix: Promote `exit-code-after-a-pipe` from an advisory doc-route to a DENYING PreToolUse hook — the estate's second denying hook after `trigger_tools_guard.py`, justified on the same grounds (no judgement in the rule). New `.claude/hooks/pipe_exit_guard.py` registered on PreToolUse:Bash; deny when the command matches `\|[^\n]{0,400}\$\?` (pipeline then `$?`), or `(?m)^[^|\n]*&\s*$[\s\S]{0,400}\$\?` / `\bnohup\b[\s\S]{0,400}\$\?` (backgrounded status read), UNLESS the same line contains `PIPESTATUS` or `set -o pipefail`. Deny message names the two allowed forms verbatim: `cmd > /tmp/out 2>&1; echo $?` and `cmd | tee /tmp/out; echo ${PIPESTATUS[0]}`. Two amendments the current route lacks: drop the once-per-session consumption for this id so it fires on every offending command rather than being spent by the first, and widen the pattern beyond pipes to the background/`nohup` form that bit superbot #setup-spine-build. Chain: `session-close`'s 'read its real exit code' step → this hook, so the gate command a closing session runs cannot be piped at all.

name: Overwriting the status file drops the flag it was carrying
one_line: A wholesale rewrite of status.md, a heartbeat or a regenerated report silently deleted a flag, self-review or open item that only lived there.
trigger: about to write a full-file overwrite of control/status.md, a heartbeat file, or a regenerated upgrade/round report
why_it_happens: Overwrite-in-place is the cheapest way to write a status file and the ritual says 'write status', not 'merge status'. The loss produces no error, no conflict and no diff a reviewer reads — pokemon-mod-lab's ORDER 005 self-review survived only on a dangling commit, and was found by a retro, not by a gate.

superbot-games · .sessions/2026-07-11-kit-upgrade-v1.12.1.md:60

date_span: 2026-07-11 → 2026-07-18 (5 repos in one week; the destruction is silent so the true span is unknown)
proposed_fix: `check_overwrite_carry.py`, run in the preflight lane. Reads: for every file in the diff whose change is a full-body replacement (>60% of HEAD lines removed), fetch the HEAD body and diff line sets. Predicate — red if any HEAD line matching `⚑|\bFLAG\b|\bowed\b|\bawaiting\b|\bself-review\b|\bunresolved\b|\]\(\.{0,2}/?docs/` is absent from the new body and its distinctive token appears nowhere else in the same diff (i.e. it was dropped, not relocated). Add a second leg for regenerated reports: count how many consecutive cards repeat the same unconsumed baton item and red at N=3, which catches the websites 'seat-digest stale' flag that rode the note without ever being consumed.
already_covered_by: The estate's standing '⟲ Previous-session review' card convention (which caught both real incidents in-flight, at superbot-games/.sessions/2026-07-11-kit-upgrade-v1.12.1.md:67-73 and pokemon-mod-lab/docs/retro/2026-07-11-self-review.md:86), plus the existing 'Next-2 baton' advisory family on the same control/status.md surface (check_baton_resolves, check_baton_freshness) which already occupies the proposed fix's second leg. The pokemon retro's adopted convention — durable content lives in docs/, status carries links not archives — is the implemented root fix.

name: Every wall, denial and coverage row carries evidence a reader can re-derive
one_line: A record satisfies the required form — a wall row, a model line, a coverage ledger, a self-test citation — while carrying nothing anyone can re-check, so the check passes on an empty claim.
trigger: writing a WALLED/DENIED ledger row, a model-attribution field, a coverage-ledger row asserting a file was read, or a PR body citing a self-test
why_it_happens: Checkers written to catch missing fields test presence, and a placeholder is present.

proposed_fix: Upgrade three existing checkers from presence to content. (a) `check_dateless_walls.py` / `check_wall_ledger_agreement.py`: a WALLED/DENIED row must carry a fenced verbatim response ≥20 chars, a surface token (host/endpoint/tool name), and an ISO date — reject the row otherwise, so "no API surface" with no probe cannot be appended at all. (b) `check_model_line.py`: replace marker-presence with a value predicate — reject `withheld|unknown|n/a|redacted|unspecified|\(.*not.*\)` in the model field. (c) `check_claim_provenance.py`: any doc citing a self-test, fingerprint, probe or measurement must reference a repo-relative committed path that RESOLVES at HEAD (fails on scratchpad paths and on absent values), and a coverage row asserting "read" must store the returned fingerprint value, not merely assert the read happened.
maps_to_existing_trap: new — TRAP-010 candidate: "a record that satisfies its own form while carrying no re-derivable evidence." Adjacent to TRAP-003 but the failure is a present claim with hollow backing, not an absence claim; every one of these passed the checker that existed.
already_covered_by: nothing — TRAP-003 (absence-as-evidence) and TRAP-001 (dated doc read as current state) are adjacent but distinct; the `recording-a-wall` doc-route does not require verbatim/surface/date in the row, and `check_no_false_walls.py` exempts a line for merely carrying a date or quote marks (presence, not content)

name: Read the state back — a call's success is not the state it was meant to produce
one_line: An exit 0, a green workflow run, a conflict-free merge or an MCP success is cited as proof of a property the call never tested; no-op successes and zero-check-run PRs look identical to real ones.
trigger: immediately after a mutation or build command returns success, before writing "X is now armed / off / merged / tested / correct"
why_it_happens: Success is the same shape whether the call changed anything or not, and the API returns 200 for a no-op.

proposed_fix: Chain: PostToolUse hook `.claude/hooks/mutation_readback.py` → `session-close` / `quality-gate` step. The hook fires on `mcp__github__(enable|disable)_pr_auto_merge|merge_pull_request|actions_run_trigger|update_pull_request_branch` and on Bash matching `\bgit merge\b|\bgit rebase\b`, and prints the REQUIRED read-back for that specific mutation — auto-merge → `pull_request_read` and assert `auto_merge` is non-null/null as claimed; any merge → `mergeable_state != dirty` AND a full local suite run before push (git merged identical text silently in the spider-swing case, so the diff is not the evidence); CI claim → `commits/{sha}/check-runs` with `total_count > 0` and every run `completed`, plus the run's test count from the log tail, not the check conclusion; build/export → an assertion targeting the claimed property (resolve the emitted links) rather than the process exit. Enforceable half in `check_claim_provenance.py`: a card line matching `\b(is now|now (armed|off|enabled|merged|tested|green))\b` must cite a field read (`auto_merge=`, `mergeable_state=`, `total_count=`, `exit=` of an assertion), not a tool name.

name: Ordering: the value is recorded or consumed before the step that determines it
one_line: State is written, cleared or read one step too early — telemetry posture before promotion, findings after the allowlist pass, a registry cleared before the fallible commit, a bucket marked seen before the restore.
trigger: PreToolUse Edit that mutates a findings/telemetry/state collection at a point later in the function than the call that consumes it, or that clears shared state before a fallible call rather than after its success check.
why_it_happens: Each statement is individually correct; only their order is wrong, and order is the one property a diff review reads past. The failure is invisible on the success path — the telemetry still writes, the feature still renders, the entry still clears.
instances: gba-homebrew #215 r3778219023 — every call site writes the finding to `guard-fires.jsonl` with `posture="advisory"` before the `--strict` promotion makes it exit-affecting, corrupting the estate's own guard telemetry

venture-lab #289 r3778256286 — promoted gate-ready findings are appended after the allowlist/exception pass has run, so a documented exception cannot suppress the finding that now fails the required check

product-forge #53 r3824857516 — `onCreate` loads the global `PREF_SELECTION` and marks the bucket seen, then `buildUi()` overwrites the remembered per-screen layout, so the advertised per-screen memory never survives process death
superbot-next #373 r3569779116 — the pending-cast registry entry is removed before the commit workflow runs, so any failure silently destroys a cast the player already paid for, with no retry path
fleet-manager #952 r3872549046 — the commit marker is mutated before durability, so rollback crashes and a mutation that reported failure stays applied
proposed_fix: Partly decidable, partly procedural. Lint: within one function, flag a mutation of a collection that occurs textually after the call that consumes it (`apply_allowlist(`, `record_fire(`, `emit(`), and flag deletion of a shared-state key that precedes a fallible call with no restore in `except`/`finally`. Procedural, as a step in `implementation-prompt` and the review skill: for every derived or recorded value, name in one line the step that determines it and assert that step runs first — a value recorded before its determinant is a defect even when the happy path is green. Fix shape validated in-estate: clear or commit shared state only after the success check, restore on non-success.
already_covered_by: none — no existing estate convention or checker covers ordering/commit-before-durability (docs/conventions/ has no such doc; tools/check_*.py covers claims, doc routes, EAP figures, false walls, pipe exit codes). Internal overlap risk only: the superbot-next #373 and fleet-manager #952 instances would be absorbed by any atomicity/rollback or TOCTOU pattern in the other class.

name: The verifier that cannot fail
one_line: A checker, guard or verification predicate is landed and declared working without ever being run against an input it is supposed to reject.
trigger: Edit/Write of `tools/check_*.py`, `**/*guard*.py`, `**/*verify*.py`, a `--selftest` block, or any function returning a LANDED/VERIFIED/PASS-class status.
why_it_happens: Writing the checker and testing the checker feel like one act. A clean first run is read as proof the instrument works, when it is equally consistent with an instrument that can never fire — and the four cheap falsifiers (empty, missing, duplicated, swapped input) are exactly the ones nobody runs.

websites #523 r3876480364 — replay verifier branches on the active state only; the consumed state (the normal downstream outcome) is unvalidated

proposed_fix: `tools/check_verifier_controls.py`, wired into `scripts/preflight.py`. Plus four AST predicates, each of which decides an instance above: (a) an assertion whose expected and actual derive from the same file/object [couch-legend #14]; (b) a missing/absent required input returning pass instead of a finding [fm #878]; (c) `re.search` / `startswith` / count-only comparison backing a uniqueness, equality or identity claim when a canonical id or a richer field set is in scope [fm #946, websites #523 ×3]; (d) a return of a LANDED/PASS-class status not dominated by a read of the artefact it names [websites #523]. name: An inference wearing a measurement badge
one_line: A mechanism, cause, consequence or interpretation that was reasoned, correlated or read from a document, published under MEASURED, a `measured` provenance label, or the flat declarative voice reserved for observation.
trigger: a Write/Edit adding `MEASURED`, `verified live`, `provenance: measured`, or a causal/consequential clause (`because|so that|which means|therefore|would have`) attached to a finding — and any claim sourced from a ratio, a correlation, or another system's internals
why_it_happens: The certainty legend is applied at the headline and inherited by everything under it, so supporting sentences, causal clauses and consequences ride a badge earned by one measurement. An inference that *explains* a real finding feels like part of the finding. And the badge is self-sealing: `measured` is precisely the label that tells the next reader not to check, so a wrong one is more durable than an unlabelled claim.

name: Name the control before naming the cause
one_line: A causal or comparative conclusion is drawn from two uncontrolled aggregates, separately-optimised arms, a simulation, or a proxy metric — and stated as a finding.

name: Guard fails open — the enforcement mechanism exempts exactly what it exists to catch
one_line: Gate/checker logic (fences, diff modes, bypass conditions) is written so a malformed or adversarial input silently disables the check while `check --strict` and the required status check stay green.
trigger: PreToolUse Edit/Write on `bootstrap.py`, `tools/check_*.py`, or `.github/workflows/*gate*.yml` where the diff adds an exemption/skip/fence/early-`continue` in a scanning loop.
why_it_happens: The author tests the gate on the shape they imagined (a well-formed file, a normal diff) and reads green as evidence of cleanliness — TRAP-003's failure mode applied to enforcement rather than to search. Nothing in the estate requires a gate to prove it still fires.

name: Green suite, wrong path
one_line: A change is declared verified because a suite is green, when the suite never executes the path that changed.
trigger: Edit/Write of a test, golden, fixture or CI job, OR writing 'verified by / covered by / proven by <test>' into a session card or PR body.
why_it_happens: Green is read as a property of the change rather than of the suite. Nothing in the close ritual asks which code the evidence actually touched, so a suite pinned to a recorded shape, an import-time snapshot, a manufactured environment, or a skipped collection all read identically to a real pass.
instances: superbot-next #157 r3563531654 — presenter used edit_original_response instead of a webhook followup; the golden pinned only the recorded shape, so live drifted while the gate stayed green (OWNER flagged: 'exactly as you said')

superbot #1110 r3442962628 — new CI job's target tests all skip on a missing httpx; the green job was treated as closing the bot-site coverage gap
couch-legend #1 r3826287990 — balance simulator never consults PROPOSED_STAGE_GATES, yet its numbers were reported as validating the stage system
couch-legend #1 r3826287999 — replay tests bypass the simulator entirely and only re-exercise shared engine functions, so the required validation gate never ran
proposed_fix: Three links. (1) Route `evidence-path-check` on Edit/Write of `tests/**`, `**/test_*.py`, `goldens/**`, `.github/workflows/*.yml` and on card/PR text matching `\b(verified|covered|proven|validated) (by|via|with)\b`: 'name the symbol you changed and the test that CALLS it; a golden pins a recorded shape, not a live send path.' (2) session-close / quality-gate skill step — mutation control: break the changed line, re-run the named test, record it going RED; a suite that stays green under mutation is not evidence. (3) Checker: fail any CI job whose pytest collection reports 0 non-skipped tests in the path it claims to cover, and flag module-level `importorskip` for a dependency the job's install step does not install.
already_covered_by: Not covered by an existing trap — 'new (proposed TRAP-008)' holds. Neither fires on 'verified by <test>'. Worth registering explicitly as TRAP-003's inverse — TRAP-003 asks a null to prove the query works; this asks a pass to prove the test can fail — and reusing that register's route/checker machinery and vocabulary rather than inventing a parallel one.

name: Flip complete while the verdict on the current head is still outstanding

name: Merging a PR while its requested review is unanswered
one_line: A session asks for a review, then lands the PR before any verdict exists on the head SHA — usually on a waiting window it chose itself.
trigger: about to call merge on a PR (mcp__github__merge_pull_request, `gh pr merge`, or `PUT /pulls/{n}/merge`) for which a review was requested and no review or inline comment exists on the current head SHA
why_it_happens: The rule is written in three places (CLAUDE.md's 'never merge a PR you have asked Codex to review before it answers', TRAP-007, the kit conventions) and nothing reads PR state at the merge call. The session's own waiting window is the only gate, and a session under close-out pressure always chooses a window shorter than 335 s. TRAP-007's register entry explicitly declined a checker on the ground that review state is PR state, not tree state — true for a checker, and precisely why this belongs in a hook that can call the API.

proposed_fix: New denying PreToolUse hook `.claude/hooks/merge_review_guard.py` — the estate's second denying hook, justified on the same ground as trigger_tools_guard.py (no judgement in the rule). Matches tool name `mcp__github__merge_pull_request` / `mcp__github__enable_pr_auto_merge`, and Bash commands matching `gh pr merge|pulls/\d+/merge`. Predicate, over direct egress with $GITHUB_PAT: extract owner/repo/N; read `GET /pulls/{N}` for head.sha, `GET /pulls/{N}/requested_reviewers`, `GET /pulls/{N}/reviews`, `GET /pulls/{N}/comments`, `GET /issues/{N}/comments`. Deny message names the measured 335 s Codex latency and the inline-comments endpoint (findings arrive there, not in the review body). Fail-open with a loud stderr note if the API is unreachable, so a proxy quirk never blocks work.

name: Two actors mint the same identifier
one_line: Parallel workers or successive sessions each minted an id into a shared namespace with no atomic claim, producing collisions, mid-flight renumbers and one clobbered session log.
trigger: at id creation — writing a new ORDER/proposal/intake number, a session-card slug, an amendment id, or a claim filename
why_it_happens: Minting an id is a local decision made against a local read, and every parallel worker's read is correct at the instant it happens. Nothing in the write path is atomic, so eleven agents each choosing 'the next free number' all choose the same one.

name: A guard, route or matcher changed without re-running its controls
one_line: An allowlist token, a hook matcher, a copied branch-prefix list or an automation's subject-selection is edited and immediately trusted; the guard then silently stops catching what it exists to catch, or fires on the wrong subject.
trigger: an edit that touches a checker, a hook matcher, `doc-routes.json`, an ALLOW*/allowlist literal, or a workflow's match list
why_it_happens: An allowlist entry is added to stop a false positive that is in front of you; the true positive it also silences is not in front of you. Nothing distinguishes 'the guard is quiet because the code is clean' from 'the guard is quiet because I blinded it'.

name: Numbers frozen into a pre-registration before anything ran
one_line: A registration, fixture or proposal pins numerals that were derived by hand, rounded from another representation, or set as thresholds that no honest run could satisfy — and the run then contradicts the document that was supposed to bind it.
trigger: a Write/Edit committing a registration block, `fixtures.json`, or a proposal's gate/exhibit section containing decimal literals or a `tolerance` paired with a sample size, before the runner has executed
why_it_happens: Pre-registration exists to stop the numbers being chosen after the fact, so it demands them before any run can produce them — and closed-form intuition, asymptotic scaling and mental arithmetic rush in to fill the gap. They look identical to run output once committed. Threshold miscalibration is subtler still: the numeral is not wrong, it is unsatisfiable, so a perfect simulation fails and the verdict is decided by a harness artifact rather than by the science — which is why it recurred three times after being 'fixed' once.

proposed_fix: `check_registration_numerals.py`, run at proposal-merge (the moment the registration becomes binding, before any runner exists) — two legs. LEG 1, literals: every numeric literal inside a `## REGISTRATION` block or `fixtures.json` must carry a per-literal `prov:` tag — `RAN cell=<id>` (and the checker asserts the literal appears verbatim in the committed script's recorded stdout, which is hash-pinned) or `DERIVED from=<single-line expression>` (and the checker `eval`s the expression under a restricted namespace and asserts equality to the stated value, catching the 419/375 argmin slip, the 30/150/900 unordered-pairs slip, the 10+12.5 sum, the hex→decimal render, and the 3.7×10⁻¹¹ exponent). A registration containing an untagged literal does not merge. LEG 2, power: for every pinned `tolerance` + sample-size pair, compute the predicted SE from the registration's own stated model and FAIL unless `tolerance / SE ≥ k` AND the expected familywise breach count over the declared number of point-gates is ≪ 1 — this is exactly what V027 discovered, V031 mis-applied per-point, and V067 hit a third time, so the check must be familywise, not per-point. Same leg rejects a PROMOTED/FINDING label on a result whose effect size is inside its own standard error. Chain it: the proposal-drafting path (`scope-backlog-item` → the lab's registration step) gains one line — "run the gate battery once against the real object before freezing any threshold" — and this checker is the gate that makes that line real.

name: A tally that contradicts the list it sits beside

one_line: A session's own reading, design choice, or invented constraint is committed as an owner directive, an ANSWERED owner-queue item, or an owner-verbatim quote — and the inverse, a decision already made or already the session's is stamped 'waiting on you'.
trigger: About to write or flip a record that speaks with the owner's authority: an OD-table row, an OQ- status flip to ANSWERED/RESOLVED/✅, a blockquote attributed to him, a `Constraint:`/`Directive:` line in a handoff prompt, or an ⚑ owner-action block.
why_it_happens: The estate already has the vocabulary — intake's provenance separation, the OWNER/REASONED/DERIVED certainty legend in findings/2026-08-05-foundation-continuation.md — and nothing reads it at write time. A session that has just done real work on a question feels entitled to the conclusion, and the record has no field forcing it to say whose conclusion it is. Both directions come from the same missing boundary: nothing checks where the owner's authority actually sits before the sentence is committed.

name: Phantom deliverable in the record
one_line: A card, ledger entry or handoff names a file, script, brief or ID as existing when the tree at that head contains no such thing, poisoning the state the next session reads.
trigger: Write/Edit to `.sessions/*.md`, `docs/current-state.md`, `control/claims/*`, an owner queue or any ledger, where the added text contains a repo-relative path, a `scripts/…` name, a `D-/Q-/OQ-/ORDER` id, or the phrase 'recorded in <file>'.
why_it_happens: The card is written from the plan while the code is still intended, and nothing between writing and pushing compares the nouns in the record against the tree.

proposed_fix: `tools/check_claimed_artifacts.py`, run in substrate-gate and as a PostToolUse hook on ledger/card writes: from added lines extract (a) paths matching `[\w./-]+\.(py|ts|tsx|md|json|ya?ml)` and (b) ids matching `\b(?:D|Q|OQ|TRAP)-[A-Z0-9-]+\b|ORDER \d+`; fail when a path is not in `git ls-files` at HEAD ∪ diff, or an id has no defining heading in the tree. Add the superbot #1091 predicate: if the changed-file set is entirely under `.sessions/` while the card or commit message claims a code deliverable, fail.
already_covered_by: Nothing delivers this. The trigger moment is OCCUPIED but by different content, and every existence-check in the estate is scoped to a surface this pattern does not live on: (1) `.claude/hooks/read_before_write.py` — PreToolUse Write/Edit, fires at the exact moment, but checks read-set membership, never tree existence; (2) doc-route `card-status-write` (+ `card-flip-to-complete`) — fires on `.sessions/*.md` Edit/Write, says card-status/merge-control only; (3) kit `check_links` (bootstrap.py:2201) — markdown-link form, `docs/` only; (4) kit `check_baton_resolves` (bootstrap.py:3966) — resolves cited repo-relative paths, but only inside `control/status*.md` § "Next-2 baton", advisory, NOT in STRICT_SUBCHECKS, and `control/` is seat-era historical in fleet-manager so it covers zero live surface; (5) `scripts/check_docs_links.py` — advisory, standalone (not in `bootstrap.py check`), and `EXCLUDE_DIRS` explicitly contains `.sessions`; (6) `scripts/check_estate_index.py` / `tools/check_doc_routes.py` — existence checks for ESTATE rows and route targets only; (7) `scripts/check_owner_queue.py` — checks cited PR state in the queue, not OQ-/D-/Q- id resolution anywhere else; (8) `check_session_log` is marker-presence only (no `exists()` call in its whole body); `check_card_residue` catches stripped fill-slots, not phantom nouns. TRAP-001..007 contain no entry for it.

Partially covered today by `/home/user/fleet-manager/.claude/hooks/read_before_write.py` — a PreToolUse hook that fires on Write/Edit when prose names a path the session never read. A phantom path is necessarily an unread path, so the path half of this pattern already raises an advisory at exactly the trigger the pattern names (Write/Edit to a card/ledger). Coverage is partial: it says nothing about ids (`D-/Q-/OQ-`), and it is keyed to session-transcript reads rather than tree membership, so a path read once and then miscited still passes. owner_flagged_premise: VOID — the lane that set this assumed every menno420-authored review comment was the owner speaking. The identity-collision finding (docs/findings/2026-08-29-estate-agent-error-audit.md §1) establishes that agents post under the owner PAT, so no GitHub text is attributable to him. name: Telling the owner something one command would settle
one_line: A confident factual assertion made to the owner in chat — about a deploy, a credential, an issue's scope, a repo setting, a game string, a play report — that no tool call backed and that he then corrected.
trigger: the Stop hook's review of an outgoing reply containing a declarative claim about this estate's live state, or a contradiction of something the owner has just reported
why_it_happens: These failures land in the chat reply, which is the one surface no checker reads — the gate runs over the diff, not over what was said. name: A registered claim never evaluated against its own pins
one_line: A pre-registered gate value, tolerance, theorem, novelty attribution or numeric target committed as established, when the constants, source revision or shipped content pinned in the same document contradict it.
trigger: the commit of a fixtures/idea/decision file containing a registered assertion — a regime anchor, a monotonicity or closed-form claim, a 'derived, not quoted' attribution, or a numeric threshold — before any run has evaluated it
why_it_happens: Pre-registration exists to stop post-hoc fitting, and it works — but it moves the whole claim to a moment *before* any evaluation is possible, and nothing runs between writing the anchor and running the sim that would test it. The pins that falsify these claims are sitting in the same file; they are simply never applied to the sentences beside them. The cost is asymmetric and severe: an unevaluated registration sinks the entire cycle rather than producing a wrong-but-informative result.

proposed_fix: `scripts/check_registration.py`, run at fixture/idea-file commit time (pre-run, in the born-red PR's gate), with four predicates evaluated against the document's own pins: (1) every regime assertion is evaluated as a predicate over the pinned constants — for 'round-robin is harmless at load ρ', assert `max_d(λ_d)·ρ < 1/N` and red on contradiction, which alone closes the P085/V098 pair; (2) every registered theorem or monotonicity claim is evaluated numerically on the fixture's own pinned grid before it can be a gate conjunct; (3) every hand-worked example is run through the pinned predicate and its recorded label diffed against the computed one; (4) every value tagged 'derived, not quoted' is greped in the pinned source revision (oldid/blob bytes) and reds on a hit — both directions, so quoted-labelled derivations are caught too. name: Headline count contradicted by the list directly beneath it
one_line: A summary sentence states a total, and the rows, bullets or enumerated dispositions in the same document add up to something else.
trigger: Edit/Write of a `.md` file where a numeral or number-word (`four edits`, `all 28 findings`, `13 closed`, `8 of 8`, `7 records`, `nine mappings`) sits within the same section as a Markdown table, numbered list, or YAML/JSONL block whose entries the numeral purports to count.
why_it_happens: The headline is written once and the list keeps moving — usually inside the very same edit, and disproportionately inside edits whose stated purpose is to fix a stale summary (#833, #943, #961). The number is cheap to state and expensive to re-derive, and nothing in the loop re-derives it; review catches it every time, which proves it is mechanically decidable and simply unowned.

Predicate: within each `##`/`###` section of a changed `docs/**.md`, `.sessions/**.md` or generated artifact, extract (a) numerals and number-words bound to a countable noun and (b) the cardinality of every adjacent structure — Markdown table body rows, list items, numbered items, YAML top-level sequence entries, JSONL lines added by the diff. name: The live next-action pointer left aimed at work this PR just finished or superseded
one_line: Work lands but the NOW pointer, live queue, Active-claims row, task ledger, handoff block or route summary that tells the next session what to do still names the completed or abandoned step — the cheapest way this estate manufactures duplicate work.
trigger: Session close, and any Edit/Write of docs/current-state.md, control/status.md, the program's NOW heading, control/claims/**, or a doc-routes `says` summary — plus any PR that adds docs/planning/*.md.
why_it_happens: The pointer is written by a previous session and read by the next one; the session in the middle is the only one that never reads it. Nothing in the landing path asks 'does the queue still describe what is next?'
instances: substrate-kit PR #580 r3728126243 — plan's build order changed, the duplicated order in current-state.md still sends sessions to the old first step
substrate-kit PR #588 r3881241100 — reconciliation completed, its own task row still advertises the work as open
superbot PR #1036 r3432312907 — plan delivered, live queue still says the next action is to synthesize the plan
superbot PR #1147 r3444623105 — completed rollout left under Active claims, so later sessions route around finished work
superbot PR #2008 r3565112924 — new 8-seat structure recorded, handoff still points at the superseded 7-seat kit
superbot PR #1098 r3441663592 — reconciliation marker reset, the file's own '▶ Next action' callout still links the superseded pass
superbot PR #2312 r3703725085 — threshold updated in one place, the '▶ Next' section still names the threshold this pass completed
fleet-manager PR #870 r3825849258 — handoff re-threaded after an owner directive, the route summary still injects the superseded work order
fleet-manager PR #954 r3876595302 — owner's global GO hold recorded in one paragraph while the same file's next-action pointer and the packet's paste-ready execute instruction stay ungated
proposed_fix: Add a mandatory link to the session-close chain, backed by a decidable checker: parse the live pointer's target (PR number, band threshold, doc path, task id, claim branch) from docs/current-state.md / control/status.md / the NOW heading / control/claims/, and fail the gate when the same PR satisfies that target while the pointer line is unchanged in the diff — i.e. 'no Active claim may name a branch whose PR merges in this commit', 'a PR adding docs/planning/*.md must modify the live-queue next-action line', 'a task row citing file:line whose content changed here must be updated'. Second predicate for holds: if a routed doc says execution is held, every paste-ready execute instruction in routed docs must carry the GO precondition.
already_covered_by: Not covered. Nearest existing instruments and why each misses: kit `check_baton_freshness` (bootstrap.py:4160 — same idea, but input-gated to `control/status*.md` `## Next-2 baton` which fleet-manager does not have, resolves only `check_<name>`/`--<flag>` tokens, and is advisory-never-exit-affecting); `check_baton_resolves` (path existence only); `check_status_current` (heartbeat timestamp age); `check_claims` (72h date horizon + duplicates, advisory); `change_guard.py` check C (needs a removed string — the pointer is never edited); `tools/check_doc_routes.py` (validates trigger coverage, never `says` freshness); `.claude/skills/session-close/SKILL.md:118-121` step 6b (stated instruction only — no route, no checker). doc-routes.json: 0 of 71 routes fire on any of the seven trigger strings, tested directly.

No trap covers it; nearest is TRAP-001 ("a dated document read as current state"), which is the reader-side of the same decay — this pattern is the writer-side, so `maps_to_existing_trap: new` stands. name: The summary its own document refutes
one_line: An absolute or 'N of N' summary sentence is written into the same file — often the same paragraph — as the table, caveat or exception list that contradicts it, and the two are never read against each other.
trigger: PreToolUse Edit/Write on any .md whose added text contains an absolute quantifier (`all|every|none|never|no <noun>|entire|categorically|N of N|read in full`) while the file already contains an exception marker (`unrated|except|out of scope|not covered|sampled|head/tail|honest null|UNKNOWN|caveat|only its successor`).
why_it_happens: The summary is written last, from the author's memory of the intent of the work, not from a re-read of the artifact. The table below it was assembled hours earlier. In this estate the summary is also the surface that travels — the ledger row, the NOW pointer, the heading — so the refuting detail stays put and the wrong sentence is what gets read.
instances: fleet-manager #940 r3843065363 — 'all 17 are judged' beside 'five unrated repos' in one sentence, landed in current-state and the NOW pointer

couch-legend #7 r3833315227 — 'never slower', bounded to 12%, above a table listing three regressions
couch-legend #15 r3835962250 — 'all 15 builds' when the same card records four runs using an unpinned checker

(1) Exception-marker predicate: for every sentence containing an absolute quantifier or an `N of N` form, if the same file contains an exception marker (regex list above) that the summary sentence does not itself name, fail and print both lines with their line numbers. This alone catches #940, #906, #960, #512, #840. (2) Table-recompute predicate: when a directional or bounded summary (`never slower|no worse than N%|improved|all faster`) sits within 10 lines of a markdown table, parse the table's signed numeric column, recompute min/max, and fail when a value falls outside the stated bound or carries the opposite sign — this is exactly the couch-legend #7 pair and needs no judgment. name: A plan, spec or owner option that contradicts itself or cannot be satisfied
one_line: The written plan carries constraints its own acceptance criteria violate — file-disjoint units with a hidden import, a least-privilege role the write path cannot use, a never-edit path it instructs a write to, a 'data preserved' option backed by an expiring artifact.
trigger: UserPromptSubmit or Write on `docs/planning/**`, a generated session/handoff prompt, or an owner-decision options block — before the file is written.
why_it_happens: Plans are reviewed section by section for plausibility. The constraints (owned files, DB role, never-edit path, delivery moment, backup durability) are stated in one section and the acceptance criteria in another, and nothing ever cross-multiplies them. A contradiction reads as two reasonable sentences.

proposed_fix: A mandatory SELF-CONSISTENCY PASS step added to `implementation-prompt`, `scope-backlog-item` and `prep-owner-steps`: extract every declared constraint into a list (owned files · privileges · never-edit paths · delivery moment · durability promise · target-platform capability), then walk each acceptance criterion and name which constraints it touches and why it is satisfiable under all of them — an unnameable criterion is unimplementable and must be rewritten before the prompt ships.
