name: Provenance stamp that does not describe the bytes it labels
one_line: A SHA, date, era banner or 'final snapshot' label is attached to an artifact built from something else — the merge revision, the working tree, a later snapshot, a mutable blob/main link, a PR that was born green.
trigger: Write/Edit of code or prose that stamps an artifact with a commit SHA, a generation date, an era window, or a 'snapshot/final/born-red' assertion.
why_it_happens: The label is written where it is convenient (the workflow's env, today's date, the SHA in hand) rather than derived from the ref the bytes came from, and provenance is exactly the claim nobody re-checks because it looks mechanical.
instances: couch-legend #11 r3833952508 — APK built from the merge revision, labelled with the PR head SHA
fleet-manager #934 r3839362655 — publisher reads mutable working-tree bytes while stamping them '@ sha'

websites #512 r3838131684 — 'the final registry snapshot' resolving to a blob/main generator source
websites #512 r3838178907 — provenance notice rendered unconditionally on the snapshot-unavailable path, with a blank date

fleet-manager #950 r3866342634 — card records born-red verification for a PR opened after the card was flipped complete
proposed_fix: Generators must read blobs from the resolved commit or require a clean tree before stamping, and must not embed a literal current date in output templates. In CI: the artifact-name expression must derive from the same ref as the checkout step; a banner asserting a date window fails if the snapshot's `generated_at` or max activity date falls outside it; link text asserting 'snapshot/final' may not resolve to an unpinned `blob/main/` path; and the card's born-red and shipped-SHA assertions are re-derived from the PR's first commit status and the merge commit's parent (TRAP-006's verification made mechanical).

TRAP-001 ("A dated document read as current state") is the inverse operation — mis-reading a stamp, not mis-writing one — and TRAP-004 ("A claim wider than the sample that produced it") is the nearest neighbour for the websites #512 era banner but does not reach the SHA/date/link-target cases. name: Under-reading tool publishing a completeness claim
one_line: A collector or summary reads less than the question needs — default branch only, a capped listing, a rolling window, 'any open card' — and then reports the gap it missed as an absence.
trigger: Write/Edit of a collector/report generator (listing calls, window filters, suppression predicates) or of a summary line asserting coverage ('all', 'none', 'no unconsumed', 'complete', 'recently shipped').
why_it_happens: The happy-path read is written first and works on the author's example; the case the tool was built for is the edge case, and an empty result reads as good news rather than as an unproven query (TRAP-003 in tool form).
instances: fleet-manager #947 r3864685645 — Contents requests omit `ref`, so in-progress cards on PR branches — the coordination case — are invisible
fleet-manager #947 r3864685685 — Contents directory listing capped at 1,000 with superbot already at 970, output still claims complete card coverage

fleet-manager #947 r3864873044 — 'any open card exists' used as proof the latest push is accounted for, hiding uncarded pushes
superbot #1114 r3443043438 — reconciliation marker advanced past merge #1096, which is absent from the ledger and now permanently skipped

superbot-next #606 r3776588099 — provenance-stamping step whose cross-workflow ordering means it never fires for the newly armed merges it exists for
proposed_fix: Every listing call paginates or uses the Trees API and passes the ref the data actually lives on; every coordination/reporting tool ships a test exercising the exact case it exists for (a card that exists only on a PR branch; an old carded PR plus a newer uncarded push on main; a repo whose adoption card predates the window) — the positive control TRAP-003 already mandates for queries, applied to tools. Summary predicates: a 'no outstanding X' line fails while any X carries status `new`; a 'Recently shipped #N' entry fails unless PR N is merged at HEAD; a marker advance fails unless every first-parent merge below the new marker appears in the ledger.

name: Generated artifact built before its own inputs, or only half its outputs refreshed
one_line: The exporter runs mid-session, then the session adds the card, telemetry row or idea file it was supposed to summarise — so the committed dashboard, console, site or digest describes a tree that no longer exists, and drift checks that exempt volatile feeds pass anyway.
trigger: Bash `git add`/`git commit`/`git push` in a commit that touches both a generated artifact (**/dashboard.json, **/console.json, **/site.json, docs/SKILLS.md digests) and any source directory it derives from (.sessions/, docs/ideas/, telemetry/, .claude/skills/).
why_it_happens: Regeneration is done at the point the session thinks about the dashboard, not at the last commit; and a producer with two outputs is remembered as having one. The check that would catch it was written to tolerate exactly the files that move.

Drive it from a producers manifest that lists each script with ALL of its outputs (export_dashboard_data.py → dashboard/data/dashboard.json AND botsite/data/site.json), so a partial refresh is a hard failure. Add set-comparison for derived indexes: every entry in a digest must exist in the source table it names, and vice versa. name: A claim wider than the sample it was taken from
one_line: A number, rate, universal or superlative is published over a population the session never measured — a partial probe set, one version, a short burst, a purposive subset, a partial billing cycle — with the sample size nowhere in the sentence.
trigger: PreToolUse Edit/Write whose added text matches census/population forms — `\bonly \d+ of \d+|\b\d+ of (the )?\d+ \w+|estate-wide|repo-wide|every (repo|repository|day|run|file)|since it was introduced|full month|dominant|most common|across all \d+` — the existing `claim-beyond-the-sample` route, extended to superlatives and time-window words.
why_it_happens: Measuring the remainder costs one more API call and feels redundant once the pattern is visible in the sample. The sentence then reads as a census because English has no cheap way to say 'and I did not look at the rest'. The route for this trap exists and still lost every incident below, because it matches phrasing and nothing checks the phrasing against the evidence actually recorded in the same document.
instances: websites #511 r3836178278 — OWNER: a workflow health rate taken from the repo-wide Actions feed, shipped into the PR body; re-measurement showed the opposite

name: Born-red card never flipped — the record and the gate disagree at PR head
one_line: A session writes a full close-out, then leaves the machine-read Status field at in-progress, so the required check stays red and the permanent ledger claims unfinished work the same card says is finished.
trigger: Stop hook on the final reply, and PreToolUse on `gh pr ready` / `update_pull_request` / any 'PR is ready' declaration: if any in-diff .sessions/*.md card has Status: in-progress while its body contains a filled close-out/verification section, block once.
why_it_happens: The card is born red on purpose, so 'in-progress' looks correct right up to the moment it is not, and the flip is the one step with no artifact to produce — it leaves no trace when omitted. Sessions treat the close-out prose as the completion event; the machinery reads only the Status field.

proposed_fix: Two halves. (a) A Stop-hook predicate (not a new checker — the checkers already decide this) that runs the repo's own gate on the in-diff cards and refuses a reply containing 'ready for review' / 'close-out' / 'merge' while it exits non-zero, quoting its output. (b) session-close SKILL.md gains an explicit terminal step order: request review → verdict on current head → flip Status → push the flip as the last commit → confirm gate green. The gap is not knowledge: every one of these eight had a checker that already said no. It is that nothing reads that checker between writing the close-out prose and declaring the PR ready.
maps_to_existing_trap: new — the exact mirror of TRAP-006 (flipped too early, defeating the hold); TRAP-006 and TRAP-007 both cover premature flips and nothing covers never flipping, which is 8 of 39 incidents in this class
already_covered_by: The session-close skill already carries the exact terminal ordering the fix proposes ("born-red card first, READY PR, batched work, close-out docs, flip complete last; land on green"), and CLAUDE.md's kit-discipline bullet restates it ("born-red session card, session close updates the program's progress ledger, and one command is the local gate — python3 bootstrap.py check --strict"). The enforcement half already exists and works: substrate-gate / kit-quality / check_session_gate.py are required checks that hold an in-progress card, which is why all eight PRs flipped before merging. This is also the exact mirror-image of TRAP-006 (flipping too early defeats the hold) — the proposed hook would push sessions back toward that trap.

Nearest neighbours, all measured non-covering: (1) doc-route `card-flip-before-push` (Bash, `repeat: true`, so never spent) fires on every `git push` and its `says` literally opens "TRAP-006 — before this push: does the in-diff .sessions/*.md card still say in-progress?" — the question is asked, but its whole payload teaches the inverse failure (already-complete = auto-merge race), and it never fires on `gh pr ready` or on a final reply; (2) `card-flip-to-complete` (`Status:\**\s*`?complete`?`) and `card-status-write` are structurally unable to fire on this pattern — the first needs the flip that never happens, the second is spent writing the born-red card; (3) no route in `.claude/hooks/doc-routes.json` matches `gh pr ready` (the `github-api` route needs `gh api` / `api.github.com` / `GITHUB_PAT` / `uploads.github.com`); (4) fleet-manager's only Stop hook is `.claude/hooks/owner_review.py`, which is content-independent and tree-blind — it blocks once with a fixed provenance question and never reads a card, a gate or a PR; (5) TRAP-006 and TRAP-007 both cover premature flips, as the pattern says, and `docs/traps.md`'s own coverage table plus its closing "coverage boundary" section concede routes fire on tool calls, not on chat replies. name: Status token asserted ahead of the state it reports
one_line: DONE / complete / live / closed / ported written into a ledger, current-state doc or manifest while the row's own dependents are open, unmerged, placeholder or unmapped.
trigger: Edit/Write that inserts a completion token (`DONE`, `Status: complete`, `live`, `deployed`, `closed`, `ported`) into a program ledger, current-state doc, owner-queue, reconciliation marker or parity manifest.
why_it_happens: The status flip is the cheapest edit in the session and the one that makes the work look finished, and the dependents live in the same row or one file away rather than in the agent's head. Downstream readers then use the token as truth — which is precisely why the wrong flip is expensive: the next session skips the remainder it can no longer see.

name: Decline in-scope work on a fence you never checked
one_line: Available work is deferred citing a scope fence, phase gate, blast-radius risk or feasibility doubt that the session never tested — several times while the very measurement that would settle it sat unrun in the tree.
trigger: writing a deferral line — `↪ Next`, 'left undone', 'parked', 'out of scope for this pass', 'needs X first' — whose stated reason is a fence, a risk or feasibility rather than a measured result
why_it_happens: A fence-shaped reason sounds like discipline rather than avoidance, and it reads well in a card, so it is never challenged. Deferrals are also the last thing written in a session, when the appetite for one more probe is lowest.

name: The start-of-session scan expires and is never re-run
one_line: A session scans open PRs, claims and main once at boot, then starts its second or third slice hours later — or pushes a long-running branch — against a snapshot that has since gone stale, and collides with work that landed in between.
trigger: Creating the Nth branch/slice of a multi-slice session, resuming after a long pause, or `git push` on a branch older than the last fetch.
why_it_happens: The scan feels like a boot ritual rather than a perishable fact. Sessions correctly record 'I scanned at start' and treat that as covering the whole session; the estate's own cards measure the half-life in hours ('its §5 claim scan was stale within hours'). Warm containers compound it — one coordinator's clone was seven merged PRs behind origin at its first turn.

It keeps a per-session timestamp under `/tmp/claude-scan-state/<session-id>.json` written whenever the session runs `git fetch`, `gh pr list` or `list_pull_requests`. Predicate at fire time: run `git fetch -q origin` then `git rev-list --count HEAD..origin/main`; inject when the recorded scan is older than 30 minutes OR origin/main has moved by >0 commits since it, printing 'origin/main moved N commits since your last scan' plus `gh pr list --state open --json number,title,files` filtered to the paths in the current diff. name: A number or an absence taken from an instrument with no positive control
one_line: A search index, an unauthenticated CDN read, a bare name grep, a remote status field or a delegated model's citation is used as ground truth without first proving the instrument can see the thing it is being asked about.
trigger: about to turn a value from a search/index API, a raw CDN fetch, a name-only grep, a remote status field, or a delegated answer into a written claim or a decision
why_it_happens: A query that returns cleanly feels like a measurement. Index blindness, stale caches and name collisions all produce well-formed, plausible answers, so nothing in the response itself signals that the instrument was pointed at the wrong thing.

name: The tractable proxy answered instead of the owner's actual ask, and 'done' judged by the agent's standard
one_line: A qualitative complaint is replaced by whatever was measurable, or an ordered plan by whatever document was freshest, and completeness is declared against a technical contract the owner does not use to judge the thing.
trigger: About to flip a feature or card to complete, or to send a reply reporting a measurement, a recommendation, or a next-actions block, when the ask that started the work was qualitative or the deliverable is owner-facing.
why_it_happens: The owner's ask is usually qualitative and the session's tools are quantitative, so there is always a nearby question that IS measurable — answering it feels like progress and produces a clean report. Symmetrically, an agent's definition of done (tests green, contract satisfied, docs written) is fully available inside the session while the owner's (he opens the app and taps a button; he reads the plain-language layer; he directs rather than reviews) lives in docs/owner-profile.md and docs/intent.md, which nothing puts in front of a completion flip or a recommendation.

name: Automation whose trigger, credential or predicate means it never runs — or runs on the wrong thing
one_line: Workflows are wired to events GitHub suppresses, to events no workflow subscribes to, to jq expressions that never test empty, or to refs and diffs that let them merge the wrong commits in a loop.
trigger: PreToolUse Edit/Write on `.github/workflows/*.yml` adding an `on:` trigger, a `--jq` emptiness test, `workflow_dispatch` on an auto-merging workflow, or a regeneration/commit step.
why_it_happens: Workflow chains are validated by reading the YAML, not by running the chain end to end once. Every one of these is invisible in a single manual test — the suppression, the missing subscriber, the empty-list branch and the squash all only appear on the path nobody exercised.
instances: websites #509 r3825959240 — GitHub suppresses runs caused by `GITHUB_TOKEN`, so the `push` trigger never publishes the freshly committed `review/data/**` and the Pages site stays stale
superbot-next #606 r3776588091 — the release emits an `unlabeled` event no workflow subscribes to, so a successfully held PR is never re-armed and the happy path deadlocks

superbot #1045 r3435347448 — `.[0].number` on an empty list evaluates to `null` not empty string, so `[ -z "$existing" ]` is false and the first/no-open-PR run skips `gh pr create` then tries to merge a PR that does not exist
superbot #1045 r3435347465 — `workflow_dispatch` with an unpinned checkout ref makes a manual run from a non-main branch merge all that branch's commits into main under a generated-data title

superbot #1165 r3446246517 — a metadata-only diff (`meta.generated_at`/`meta.build`) feeds an any-diff auto-merge loop, guaranteeing the next scheduled export sees another diff — self-sustaining PR and deploy churn
superbot #2072 r3571228217 — the conflict-resolution helper regenerates exports from a tree that may still contain conflict markers, baking corrupt or stale data into committed artifacts
superbot #2344 r3723779054 — generated artifacts stamped with a build commit that will not survive squash-merge, so the provenance badge points at an unreachable object
proposed_fix: A `workflow-lint` checker with six decidable predicates: (1) a workflow that commits with the default checkout credential paired with another relying on `on: push` for that path → fail; (2) label removal used as a re-trigger with no workflow listing `unlabeled` in `on:` → fail; (3) `--jq` used in a `-z`/`-n` emptiness test must end in `// empty`; (4) an auto-merging workflow with `workflow_dispatch` must pin `ref:` or guard `refs/heads/main`; (5) any regeneration step must be preceded by a refusal when `git diff --name-only --diff-filter=U` is non-empty, and must skip when the diff touches only volatile metadata keys; (6) an embedded build sha must satisfy `git merge-base --is-ancestor <sha> <PR head>`.

name: Composed UI/runtime state never exercised — the feature is broken exactly where it ships
one_line: Timers, overlays, list-level attributes, clamps, hit rectangles and index maths are each correct alone and wrong together, so the feature is invisible or unusable on the target device or at the population size it will reach.
trigger: PreToolUse Write/Edit adding a duration constant, a global key listener, an `aria-live`/`role=status` attribute, a line-clamp, hard-coded widget coordinates, or a UI index derived from a collection size.
why_it_happens: Each component is exercised in isolation at the size and width the author happened to open. The composed state — cinematic over toast, cinematic under modal, longest string at narrowest width, full registry, legacy rows — is never in the harness, and on the owner's phone the composed state is the only state.
instances: couch-legend #7 r3833172094 — a 5,200 ms cinematic hide over a 4,800 ms toast expiry, so queued toasts expire unseen behind the cinematic
couch-legend #7 r3833338148 — a one-shot chapter cinematic runs, burns its pending stage and binds Escape while a modal is open, so the player never sees it and Escape hits two handlers
couch-legend #17 r3838157657 — `aria-live` on every shop row, so a single state change makes every row announce at once
couch-legend #17 r3838201018 — the impact paragraph clamped at phone and `sm` widths, hiding the very effects the feature exists to show, on the owner's own target device
product-forge #50 r3788541865 — preset widget rectangles overlap at `x=0.24..0.29`, `y=0.56..0.70`, so D-pad touches in the intersection drive the analog stick
superbot #1160 r3445385264 — a Discord row index derived from unbounded registry size reaches `row=5` and raises `ValueError` once enough worlds register
superbot #1039 r3432534246 — the species catalog shrunk without migrating existing log rows, so `!fishlog` can display 23/21
proposed_fix: Harness contract enforced in the gate: the visual/state harness must include the maximum-length string, the maximum collection size, the narrowest target width, and each declared overlay/modal combination — a component added without its worst case in the harness fails. Five decidable lints alongside it: (a) pairwise rectangle intersection over interactive widgets in every preset; (b) `aria-live`/`role=status` inside a component rendered in a `map`/list; (c) line-clamp applied to the element rendering the feature's primary content; (d) a UI index derived from `len(collection)` with no clamp to the platform's declared range; (e) a displayed numerator and denominator computed from different filtered sets. Plus a duration-constant registry: named timers in one store that overlap are reported for a human decision.

name: Retirement applied to the visible surface only
one_line: A service, cron, workflow or duplicate is deleted and the change is made where a human would look, while redirects, machine-readable inventories, parallel registries, probe rows and runbooks keep advertising the dead thing as live.
trigger: Edit/Write whose diff removes a `schedule:`/cron block, deletes a workflow file, or adds retirement vocabulary (`retired|deleted|decommissioned|taken offline|no longer runs`) next to a named identifier (hostname, service id, workflow filename).
why_it_happens: Retirement is felt as a single act, but the identifier is replicated across data files, templates, redirects and ops docs that were written by different sessions; nothing enumerates the identifier's occurrences at the moment the retirement is declared.

name: The proof that was never re-run
one_line: A command, count or exit code is recorded as evidence but does not reproduce on the committed tree — never run, run against an earlier artifact, or unrunnable anywhere else.
trigger: Edit/Write of `.sessions/**` or `docs/**` containing a fenced command adjacent to a recorded exit code, count, or a 'Check it' recipe.
why_it_happens: The command is written at the moment of intent and the tree keeps moving underneath it — later commits, a later edit to the artifact, a flag that never existed. Recording the command feels like running it, and nothing ever re-executes what was written down.
instances: fleet-manager #845 r3756178179 — closure command claimed 'no hits'; at that head it matches three paths and exits 0
fleet-manager #846 r3757269308 — recorded `grep -c` proofs print 0 and exit 1 while the target text is present, contradicting the pass's own claim that every proving command ran

superbot #2344 r3723779058 — card's commands-run block names `export_dashboard_data.py --drift`; the script exposes `--check` and no `--drift`
fleet-manager #946 r3852236666 — browser-render verification (27/12/9) left standing as send-day evidence after the copy block changed; the proof describes a different artifact
websites #510 r3826544414 — absolute self-link double-prefixed by the exporter's own rewrite in every generated page; the exported output was never opened
proposed_fix: `tools/check_proof_commands.py` in `scripts/preflight.py`: parse every fenced command in changed `.sessions/**` and `docs/**` that sits adjacent to a recorded exit code, count or `Check it` label; execute it in the committed checkout and diff exit code AND output against the record. Three cheap sub-predicates catch the rest without execution: absolute session-container paths (`/home/user/`, `/workspace/`) in a committed recipe; a flag absent from the named script's argparse; a verification record whose stored artifact sha256/word-count no longer matches the artifact in the diff (kills stale browser/render evidence and forces a re-run when the artifact changes). For generated output, the evidence must cite the generated file, not the template.

name: Private, owner-gated or credential-bearing content reaches a public surface
one_line: Machine paths, gated identifiers, whole runner environments and secret-bearing URLs are written into public repos, CI uploads, logs and user-visible errors, with a born-red gate or a reversible encoding mistaken for protection.
trigger: PreToolUse Bash on `git push` / `gh pr create`, or Edit/Write of a file under a public-published tree, where the content contains an absolute host path (`/home/`, `/Users/`, `C:\`), a `pending OWNER … ruling` marker, an env dump piped to an outbound command, or a log call interpolating `*_URL`/`*_TOKEN`.
why_it_happens: Publication is treated as the merge, not the push — so a born-red gate reads as a hold. And redaction is treated as a string operation rather than a property: `replace()` and base64 both look like they do something to a reader skimming the diff.
instances: fleet-manager #360 r3610512197 — a CI workflow base64s every process environment variable and posts it off-repository while describing the upload as anonymous timing-only data

fleet-manager #833 r3743454117 — pushing the branch already published thread subjects, message IDs, timestamps and vendor identity to a public repo; the open owner ruling and born-red gate were treated as mitigation
fleet-manager #954 r3876630614 (OWNER) — exact hub filesystem paths written into a packet bound for a shared surface, where the content rule keeps machine paths in the hub's private records

fleet-manager #954 r3876571693 (OWNER) — a hook spec that never enumerates where each class of session record lands, leaving it ambiguous whether machine/personal detail reaches the public estate pages
superbot #2058 r3580682268 — the full secret-bearing relay URL logged verbatim at boot and again in `push_snapshot` failure logs, leaking the ingest credential
websites #523 r3872055338 — token redaction implemented as a literal string replace applied after `str()`, so the escaped form of the credential survives into user-visible error text
proposed_fix: A denying PreToolUse guard on `git push`/`gh pr create` (same class as `trigger_tools_guard.py`, the estate's one no-judgement rule) that scans the outgoing diff for: absolute host paths, user-named home directories, any file carrying a `pending OWNER … ruling`/confidentiality marker, and workflow steps piping `env`/`printenv` into an outbound command. name: Written in one place, unswept at the surfaces that get read
one_line: A constraint, hold, or restructure lands at its authoritative site while the pointers, summaries and first-read maps that sessions actually execute from keep telling the old, thinner, or ungated story.
trigger: Edit/Write whose diff touches an authority surface — the consolidation program's OD table, `docs/current-state.md`, `docs/owner-queue.md`, `docs/intent.md`, `docs/ESTATE.md`, or any normative `##`/`§` heading being renumbered or retitled — or whose added text matches `(paste[- ]ready|first[- ]sitting|start here|NOW pointer|§\s*\d+[a-z]?\s+(rules?|steps?)\s+\d|recommended source|owner vocabulary)`. One route id per direction so it is not spent on the authority write: `authority-doc-write` (Edit/Write, `repeat: true`) + `pointer-surface-write`.
why_it_happens: The estate's records are deliberately redundant — the same constraint is stated at an authority site, a summary site and an executable pointer. A session edits the one it opened, and nothing in the tree links the dependents, so correctness at the site being edited is indistinguishable from correctness overall.
instances: fm #954 r3876630750 — OD-23's owner GO hold recorded once; current-state's first-sitting line, the packets' §6 rule and §7's paste-ready line still told a future session to start work ungated (OWNER-voiced concession)

(2) VOCABULARY COVERAGE — parse the owner-vocabulary column of `docs/ESTATE.md`, assert each term resolves to a route in `.claude/hooks/doc-routes.json` via the same matcher `route_docs.py` uses; fail listing unrouted terms (extend `tools/check_doc_routes.py`, mirror `tools/test_doc_route_patterns.py`'s must-fire/must-be-silent fixtures so a widening cannot silently narrow). (3) REFERENCE RESOLUTION — resolve every intra-document `§ N`, `rules N–M`, `§ Nb` reference against that document's actual headings/enumerations; unresolved → fail. (4) SUMMARY FIDELITY — for entries declared first-read (`docs/intent.md` map rows), assert each constraint id's row contains every keyword the full statement marks binding, or carries `SUMMARY — see <path>` explicitly. Plus the two routes above so the sweep is asked for at the edit, and a `session-close` step: "you changed an authority; run the propagation sweep and paste its exit code."

name: The record landed somewhere unreachable from main
one_line: Work was committed, but on a dangling commit, a post-squash branch tip or a PR closed unmerged — so the only copy of a record left the main line entirely.
trigger: about to push to a branch whose PR is already merged, about to close a PR unmerged, and at session close after any squash-merge
why_it_happens: Committing feels like durability — the work is in git, and git does not lose things. But reachability from main is what makes a commit findable, and nothing in the push or close path checks it; the branch tip and the squash commit look identical from inside the session that made both.

proposed_fix: `check_offmain_records.py`, two legs, run at close-out. Leg 1 (reachability sweep): for every `refs/remotes/origin/claude/*` branch whose PR is merged or closed, assert `git merge-base --is-ancestor <tip> origin/main`; report any tip that is not, with `git diff --name-only origin/main...<tip>` so the stranded files are named — this is precisely the venture-lab telemetry append that missed the squash window and survived only as a hand-written ADVISORY line. Leg 2 (close-unmerged guard): before `gh pr close` without merge, run `git diff --name-only origin/main...<branch>` and refuse if the branch uniquely adds files under `docs/` or `.sessions/` — gba-homebrew's whole ordered night report, including its verbatim denial ledger, exists only on dangling commits `a84933b`/`b57221a` because of this. Leg 3 (cheap, same file): before opening or merging a PR touching shared docs paths, list open PRs and diff their changed-file sets against this branch's, which is how fm #838's work was stranded by #840.

Covers legs 1 and 2 as prose procedure; nothing enforces it mechanically, and no checker in fleet-manager/tools/ does a reachability sweep.

.claude/hooks/git_state_guard.py — `squash_stack_warning()` + `force_push_report()`, wired as a PreToolUse hook in .claude/settings.json (matcher `Bash|WebFetch|Read|Glob|Grep|Edit|Write|MultiEdit`). name: Destructive git run without reading the tree first
one_line: `git reset --hard`, `git checkout --`, `git restore` or `--amend` is issued to tidy or sync, against a tree that still holds uncommitted work or a branch whose PR has not merged, and the work is gone.
trigger: a Bash command matching a history- or worktree-destroying git verb, before it runs
why_it_happens: These commands are the standard idiom for 'get clean and sync', reached for during cleanup when attention has already moved to the next task. The tree's state is exactly the thing the session has stopped looking at.

proposed_fix: `check_destructive_git.py` as a PreToolUse Bash deny. Predicate: command matches `git\s+(reset\s+--hard|checkout\s+(--|-f)\b|restore\b|clean\s+-[a-zA-Z]*f|commit\s+--amend)` AND either (i) the hook's own `git status --porcelain` (unpiped, real exit code) is non-empty, or (ii) `gh pr list --head $(git branch --show-current) --state open` is non-empty. Deny, printing the porcelain lines that would be destroyed and the two safe forms: `git stash -u` first, or `git checkout -B <branch> origin/main` — never a bare reset on a feature branch, which rewinds that branch's ref and strands its commits.

name: Edit a file that is regenerated, kit-owned or already applied
one_line: A change is made in place to a generated workflow, a generated artifact in a conflict, or a migration already applied on main — so the edit is overwritten on the next regeneration, or never runs at all.
trigger: an Edit/Write whose target carries a generated/kit-owned banner, sits under `migrations/` at a version already on origin/main, or is a generated artifact being conflict-resolved
why_it_happens: The file is right there, the fix is one line, and the banner is above the fold of what the session actually read. The failure is deferred to a later upgrade or deploy, so nothing in the session contradicts it.

proposed_fix: `immutable_paths.py`, PreToolUse on Edit/Write/NotebookEdit. Deny when any holds: (1) the target's first 20 lines match `(DO NOT EDIT|generated by|regenerat|kit-owned|hand edits.*overwritten)`; (2) the path matches `migrations/(\d+)_` and that version already exists on `origin/main` (runner skips by version, so the change would never apply); (3) the path is listed as a generated artifact and the working tree is mid-rebase/merge. The deny message names the source file to edit instead and the regeneration command. Companion for the inverse direction — a regeneration silently dropping host customizations for five consecutive hops — the `upgrade-distribution` carve-out scan must diff whole files, not named steps, and red when a regenerated file loses ANY line the previous version had.

name: The session ends with its own PR in a non-terminal state
one_line: A session comes to rest with the PR it opened still `dirty`, still open, or with its branch never pushed at all — so the document or fix the session exists to deliver is not on main, and successive sessions re-flag the hole as out of scope rather than driving it home.
trigger: session close / the Stop hook, with a branch created this session
why_it_happens: Opening the PR feels like the delivery. Nothing in the loop closes back on it, and a `dirty` state is silent — no failure fires, no notification arrives, and the estate's own wake mechanism explicitly never wakes a session to say a PR went green.
instances: [fleet-manager] .sessions/2026-08-08-index-layer2-spider-swing.md:18 — #817 left `dirty`; the document declared to supersede anything conflicting was never on main and a fresh session walking the read path could not reach it

[sim-lab] .sessions/2026-07-18-verdict-128-compounding-reward-inequality.md:29 — V126's PR #200 never landed, `sims/` jumps 125 → 127, and five-plus later verdicts merged over the gap while each session re-flagged it as out of scope

[fleet-manager] findings/ultracode-verification-2026-07-10.md:170 — `mergeable_state: dirty` against #1911/#1914 which merged after it opened, card already flipped
proposed_fix: Chain: `session-close` → `stop_check.py`. Add to `session-close` a final step 8 "terminal-state roll call" that records, in the card, every branch the session pushed and every PR number it opened. Then have the Stop hook (`src/engine/hooks/stop_check.py`, the estate's existing reply-review gate) read that block and **block once** unless, for each entry: `git rev-parse --verify origin/<branch>` succeeds (the branch actually reached origin), and `GET /pulls/{n}` returns `merged == true` or `state == closed`, or the reply names the PR with an explicit stated reason for parking it. A refused push and a conflicted PR are both fine outcomes; leaving the turn without saying so is not.

TRAP-006/TRAP-007 in docs/traps.md cover the OPPOSITE failure (flipping complete too EARLY) and do not cover this one.

[D-0017] (docs/decisions.md:267-292, decided 2026-08-14) + .claude/skills/session-close/SKILL.md steps 3 and 7b and its "Report format" terminal-state line — doctrine, NOT delivery: no docs/traps.md entry, no doc-routes.json route and no checker fires at this pattern's trigger moment.

name: A design shipped on an unstated fork that was the owner's to settle
one_line: The home, shape, or user-facing interaction model of a new thing is chosen by assumption rather than named as a choice, and the owner reverses it — usually the same day.
trigger: About to draft a design doc or founding package, or to merge a PR that fixes a user-facing interaction model, where the artifact's home, shape, or flow was picked without being written down as a decision with alternatives.
why_it_happens: A fork only looks like a fork if you stop to name it; from inside the drafting, the first plausible home or flow reads as the design, not as option A. Two of these repos had an OPEN question register (Q-0254, Q-0175) already holding the very fork being assumed, and nothing made checking it a precondition of drafting. The cost is asymmetric and known: one AskUserQuestion before the merge versus a same-day owner reversal of shipped work.

name: A record finalized while its own review line still says pending
one_line: The card, verdict or close-out is written as complete with a `reply: pending` / `review: pending` line inside it, and nobody ever comes back — 'pending' becomes the terminal disposition.
trigger: writing a `Status: complete` / `status: finalized` line into a record whose same block contains a review or codex line reading pending, awaiting, or no reply
why_it_happens: 'Pending' feels honest — it is not a false claim, it is a true one about a moment that has passed. TRAP-007's own coverage note declares no checker possible because review state is PR state; that is right about the PR and wrong about the record, and the wrongness has cost five verdicts in one sim-lab shard alone. The record contradicts itself in a single diff, and nothing reads it.
instances: [sim-lab] control/outbox-archive-2026-07.md:52 — verdict ledgered `status: finalized` with `reply: pending (OA-002 open ... fold in when it lands)`; recurs across VERDICTs 004/007/010/011/013 in one shard

[superbot] .sessions/2026-06-19-settle-decisions-codex.md:57 — closed without checking whether Codex had reviewed its recent PRs; the owner had to prompt about the reply
date_span: 2026-06-19 → 2026-07-10 (3 weeks, 3 repos); the sim-lab shard repeats it across five numbered verdicts
proposed_fix: New `src/engine/checks/check_review_pending.py`, wired into `scripts/preflight.py` so it runs under `python3 bootstrap.py check --strict`. This is the half of TRAP-007 that IS tree state, which the register wrongly wrote off. Reads every file matching `.sessions/*.md`, `control/outbox*.md`, `docs/retro/*.md` and any block containing a `status:` or `Status:` line. Predicate: within one record block (delimited by the next `^## ` heading), FAIL when a line matches `(?i)^\s*\**(status|Status)\**:?\s*`?(complete|finalized)` AND another line in the same block matches `(?i)^\s*(codex|review|reply|verdict-review)\s*:.*\b(pending|awaiting|no reply|not yet|when it lands)\b`. Escape hatch: the block passes if the same line carries an explicit `re-polled <ISO8601>` stamp plus a terminal word (`quota-blocked`, `declined`, `will-not-answer`), which turns a silent carry-forward into a dated fact. Scans prose deliberately — unlike the pipe-exit checker, this trap lives in prose.

name: A reviewer's transient refusal recorded as a standing suspension
one_line: One quota refusal is generalised into 'the review step is suspended' and then cited as precedent by later sessions, permanently deleting a review step the estate's own rule says is retry-later.
trigger: writing a codex/review line that reads `none`, `suspended`, or `skipped`, or recording any reviewer refusal as a property of the tool rather than a dated event
why_it_happens: A refusal arrives as a real message with a real reason, which makes it feel like a measurement rather than a moment. The precedent then compounds: once one record says suspended, the next session cites the record instead of retrying, and by V073 nobody is testing the claim at all. The estate's false-wall guard already exists and already runs in CI — it simply has no pattern for a reviewer.
instances: sim-lab · control/outbox.md:320 — 'codex: none this cycle — @codex step suspended per the outbox codex-line escalation (quota precedent, carried from V071–V073)': one refusal turned into a three-verdict standing precedent
[sim-lab] .sessions/2026-07-12-verdict-016-review-authenticity.md:67 — the verdict PR skipped its @codex step as 'suspended' and landed without it

idea-engine · docs/audits/eap-project-audit-2026-07-14.md:76 — the @codex verdict-review step recorded 'quota-capped → suspended' at the program level (dual-cited with P6: the same row also names the three fabrication incidents)
[fleet-manager] .sessions/2026-08-07-codex-caught-four.md:72 — 'recorded my impatience as a property of the tool' (dual-cited with P1: the merge is P1's instance, the recording is this one)
date_span: 2026-07-12 → 2026-08-07 (1 month, 3 repos); the sim-lab precedent chain itself spans V071–V073 plus V016
proposed_fix: Two small additions, both to machinery that already exists. (1) A `doc-routes.json` route `reviewer-refusal`, `repeat: true`, on UserPromptSubmit + PreToolUse Edit/Write, triggers `['(?i)\b(quota|usage)[- ]cap', '(?i)reached usage limits', '(?i)\b(codex|review)[- ]step (suspended|skipped|unavailable)', '(?i)codex\s*:\s*none', '(?i)quota precedent', '(?i)carried from V\d+']`, delivering CLAUDE.md's 'Quota refusals are retry-later, never a property of the tool' bullet plus `docs/CAPABILITIES.md` § THE DISCOVERY RULE step 0. (2) Extend `tools/check_no_false_walls.py` — already a required status check via substrate-gate — with the same patterns, so the sentence fails the merge rather than decorating it. The wall guard's current regexes hunt for API/service walls and do not recognise a reviewer wall, which is exactly how 'the @codex step is suspended' passed a gate designed to stop that sentence.

name: A review finding dispositioned by reflex or by symptom
one_line: The finding is answered without a countable disposition — conceded wholesale, rejected wholesale on a method flaw, over-graded, or fixed exactly as narrowly as it was worded — and each failure mode is invisible in the record.
trigger: about to write the disposition of a review finding — the moment a review round is declared resolved, or an objection is answered
why_it_happens: Conceding is cheap and reads as humility; rejecting on a method flaw reads as rigour; fixing the exact words of the finding reads as responsiveness. All three feel like good behaviour in the moment and none leaves a countable trace, so no reviewer of the review can tell deference from judgement. The estate already discovered the fix — three literal tags — and then shipped it as prose, which is the one delivery mechanism `docs/intent.md` § 4 says does not work.
instances: substrate-kit · .sessions/2026-08-06-provenance-mandate-plan.md:14 — three objections raised, three conceded, presented as rigour; the owner flagged it as equally consistent with deference, which is what created the [survived]/[conceded]/[partial] vocabulary

[spider-swing] .sessions/2026-08-01-bot-model-v3.md:81 — the upgrade audit's 'the Reel meter never empties' premise was called circular, implying the conclusion false; the premise in fact holds (never below 73%, median 100%). Right about the method, wrong about the disposition

substrate-kit · docs/reviews/2026-08-06-provenance-mandate-review-record.md:180 — four Codex rounds, each fixing only the symptom named and re-reading the result; the same defect survived all four. Codex: 'Updating the heading grammar fixed the round-3 symptom, but did not verify the record against the complete rule set'

[fleet-manager] findings/2026-08-13-intent-map-fresh-scorer.md:120 — a row graded 'the worst defect in the run'; the severity call did not survive blind re-scoring, re-graded as an attribution imprecision at most
date_span: 2026-08-01 → 2026-08-13 (2 weeks, 3 repos) — tight in time because the convention that names it was written 2026-08-06; earlier instances are undetectable for want of the vocabulary
proposed_fix: The convention (`docs/conventions/adversarial-review.md`) and the route (`adversarial-review`) both exist; only enforcement is missing. New `src/engine/checks/check_review_disposition.py` in preflight. Reads any file under `docs/reviews/`, `.sessions/`, or matching `*review*.md`. Predicate: count finding rows (table rows or `^\s*[-|]\s*(P[0-9]|F[0-9]|finding)` lines) and count literal `[survived]` / `[conceded]` / `[partial]` tags. FAIL when (a) tag count < finding count — an undispositioned finding; (b) every tag in the file is `[conceded]` and count >= 3 — the deference tell the owner named verbatim; (c) a `[survived]` carries no following line stating why, or a `[conceded]` carries no line stating what changed. Paired skill step, into `review` and `session-close`: after the last finding in a round is dispositioned, re-run the finding against the COMPLETE rule set before declaring the round resolved — the round-4 lesson, stated as an action rather than a caution.

name: Canonical predicate re-implemented instead of called
one_line: A simulator, preview, or generated index computes availability / rates / the command surface with its own copy of a predicate the production layer owns, and then publishes the divergence as fact.
trigger: Write/Edit of a module under sim/, analysis/, preview or index-builder paths that defines its own unlock/availability/alias-expansion/rate logic instead of importing the exported one.
why_it_happens: Reimplementing the rule inline is faster than threading the real one into an analysis or export path, and the divergence is invisible until someone compares the artifact against the live oracle.
instances: superbot-next #154 r3563531208 (OWNER) — both indexers registered discord.py group aliases verbatim, publishing a `!open` that never existed and a `create` shadowing a shipped op

proposed_fix: AST/grep check: modules in sim/analysis/preview/index roles may not define a local `*Unlocked` / `compute*` / alias-expansion function — they must import the exported canonical one. Plus an oracle test per generated index: every emitted dispatch key must round-trip through the live dispatcher, no two keys may collide, and no emitted top-level key may shadow a shipped command.

name: A stale literal in code, comment or scaffold contradicting the migrated reality
one_line: Committed code carries a template package id, a legacy directory path, a superseded version pin or a comment that still calls a now-live dataset frozen — latent debt that fails or destroys data the first time someone actually runs it.
trigger: Edit/Write of a source, config or installer file whose diff introduces or leaves a known-stale literal — scaffold ids (`com.getcapacitor.myapp`, `com.example.`), legacy paths (`claims/` not prefixed `control/`), a version pin that also appears in docs, or a freshness/frozen assertion next to a command that writes.
why_it_happens: Generator output is committed unread, and pins and paths are duplicated between code, its own comments and the docs that describe them, so a change made in one is invisible in the others.
instances: gba-homebrew PR #216 r3781391259 — toolchain pin and mirror bumped in the installer; docs/BUILDING.md, current-state.md and a comment in the same script still name 1.21.1 and say no mirror is needed

name: A verdict standing where the measurement belongs

name: Wrote into a machine-owned record without running the program that owns it
one_line: Hand-edited a generated block, an append-only ledger, a parsed field, or a schema whose committed fixtures were left unmigrated — the consumer was never run against the result.
trigger: Edit/Write to a path with a registered producer or consumer: content inside generated fences, a dated ledger entry header, a machine-parsed marker line, or a schema whose fixtures are committed.
why_it_happens: These files read as prose — a markdown ledger, a digest, a run-report header, a JSON fixture — so the agent edits them with the same confidence it edits a paragraph, and the diff looks right to a human eye. The owning program is elsewhere and is never invoked, so every one of these landed green: the generator would have overwritten it, the parser would have dropped it, the analyzer would have printed nonsense — none of them ran. Highest-frequency class in this lane and the only one spanning three repos.
instances: fleet-manager PR #846 — https://github.com/menno420/fleet-manager/pull/846#discussion_r3757343229? — hand-edited three entries inside a block generated from `docs/CAPABILITIES.md`; `bootstrap.py seat-digest` replaces all three and `check --strict` reports `seat-digest-stale` + `seat-digest-over-budget` (discussion_r3757343229 is PR #845; this instance is fleet-manager PR #846 discussion_r3757343229's sibling id r3757343229 as cited in the source record)

fleet-manager PR #859 — https://github.com/menno420/fleet-manager/pull/859#discussion_r3782972999 — inserting a capability row replaced the existing `- 2026-08-13 … remote-container egress layer` header instead of preceding it, destroying a dated record and merging two unrelated claims

couch-legend PR #1 — https://github.com/menno420/couch-legend/pull/1#discussion_r3826502318 — added an analyzer-required field without migrating committed baseline fixtures, so the documented analyze command reports an `Infinity%` displayed-rate floor instead of failing

superbot PR #2092 — https://github.com/menno420/superbot/pull/2092#discussion_r3576774437 — introduced an `owner-live` token in the machine-parsed `**Run type:**` field, which `parse_updates()` only classifies as `routine`/`manual`, silently exporting an empty `run_type`
proposed_fix: Registry + PostToolUse hook + checker. (1) `tools/record_consumers.json`: path glob → validator command (e.g. `docs/CAPABILITIES-*.md` fences → `python3 bootstrap.py seat-digest --check`; run-report headers → `parse_updates.py --validate`; fixture globs → the documented analyze command). (2) `.claude/hooks/validate_record_write.py` on `PostToolUse` (Edit|Write|MultiEdit): if the path matches the registry, run the mapped validator immediately and print its real exit code and diff — non-blocking, but the failure lands in the same turn as the edit, which is the only moment the agent can still act on it. (3) `tools/check_record_writes.py` in `check --strict`, three decidable predicates: fail a diff touching lines inside generated fences with no corresponding source-file change; fail a diff to an append-only ledger that REMOVES an existing dated entry header; fail a schema/field addition with no fixture change in the same commit. (4) Route id `machine-owned-record-write` pointing at the registry so the agent learns which program owns the file before it writes.
already_covered_by: none — no existing trap or checker covers this. `bootstrap.py check --strict` emits `seat-digest-stale`/`seat-digest-over-budget` and superbot ships `scripts/check_reconcile_marker.py --strict`, but those are post-hoc gates for two specific paths, not a registry. `/home/user/fleet-manager/tools/check_claim_propagation.py` is adjacent in spirit ("you corrected one copy and left the other standing") but matches retracted-claim *wordings* in prose, not writes into producer-owned records; it would not have caught any of the four instances. No `tools/record_consumers.json` and no `PostToolUse` write-validator exist in the tree.

Nearest architectural sibling: `.claude/hooks/change_guard.py` check A (path-keyed "the kit copy loop owns this file"), scoped to `.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md` only. Nearest predicate precedent: `check_inbox_append` (pure-append vs merge-base), scoped to `control/inbox.md` only. No trap entry, no doc-route, no blocking checker.

Partly covered, and that is the point: `check_seat_digest` (bootstrap.py:22704-22800) already implements the exact detection for instance 1 by byte-compare, emitting `seat-digest-stale` and `seat-digest-over-budget` — but it is registered `ADVISORY_HEURISTIC` in `guards.ADVISORY_CENSUS` ("digest_advisories") and is contractually never exit-affecting, so it fires today (verified) and gates nothing. `tools/check_no_false_walls.py` already parses the same `substrate-kit:*digest BEGIN/END` fence grammar for its exemption, so the fence-boundary parser exists. `scripts/check_capabilities_grammar.py` lints the CAPABILITIES append-log grammar but explicitly does not check for removed entries. `.claude/hooks/change_guard.py` already occupies `PostToolUse` on `Edit|MultiEdit` (lane C, "un-propagated edit") and is the natural home for the proposed hook rather than a new file. Nothing existing covers instances 2, 3 or 4.
owner_flagged_premise: VOID — the lane that set this assumed every menno420-authored review comment was the owner speaking. The identity-collision finding (docs/findings/2026-08-29-estate-agent-error-audit.md §1) establishes that agents post under the owner PAT, so no GitHub text is attributable to him. name: Duplicate detected and still not stopped
one_line: The collision is seen — a sibling PR on the same paths, a stand-down message sent — and the losing lane keeps going or its auto-merge wins the race, so detection buys nothing and someone still reconciles by hand.
trigger: The moment a duplicate is identified: a sibling PR on the same work is found, or a stand-down comment is about to be posted.
why_it_happens: The stop is attempted through a channel the other session may never read in time (a PR comment) while auto-merge is a machine acting immediately — a message racing a robot. And a session that sees the collision itself has already paid the build cost, which makes 'proceed and let someone close one' feel cheaper than stopping.
instances: substrate-kit · .sessions/2026-07-09-coordinator-review.md:45 — 'Stand-down raced auto-merge and lost': duplicate ORDER 005 PR #51 merged at ~17:24Z before the stop message took effect, leaving a residual conflict on open #50

Substrate-kit-app · .sessions/2026-07-09-project-review.md:32 — saw the sibling PR targeting the same two paths and proceeded anyway: 'whichever PR lands second conflicts; the manager/owner should close one'
superbot · .sessions/2026-06-21-reaction-roles-pr3-5.md:90 — the parallel duplicate #1221 was not noticed and 'then sat open and conflicted'
date_span: 2026-06-21 → 2026-07-09 (3 weeks; two of the three cites are the same #50/#51 lane seen from two repos)
proposed_fix: SKILL — insert a step into `session-close` (and mirror it in `review`), placed before any stand-down or FYI comment is written: 'DUPLICATE FOUND — act on the machine before the message.' Ordered: (1) `mcp__github__disable_pr_auto_merge` on the losing PR — a comment cannot outrun a queued auto-merge, and this is the only step that stops the clock; (2) convert the losing PR to draft (`update_pull_request`); (3) only then post the stand-down naming the winning PR and the work id; (4) record the arbitration on the surviving card, not just in the comment thread. And the rule the Substrate-kit-app card violated, stated as a hard step: when a sibling PR already touches your target paths for the same work id, you STOP and close yours — 'the owner should close one' is not a disposition a session may choose for someone else.
already_covered_by: substrate-kit PR #365 — `bootstrap claim --order NNN` (refuse-unless-`--force` when another live claim on a different branch names the order) + the `claims-order-collision` cross-branch advisory in `check_claims`; and PR #398 — the re-verify-then-stand-down clause, verbatim in the lab-loop prompt at HEAD (recorded in /home/user/fleet-manager/findings/2026-08-28-kit-tree-truth-pass.md:445)

name: A completion sentence wider than the diff that earned it
one_line: The close-out prose asserts an outcome — a thread closed end-to-end, a region with its own identity, a round complete — that is true of part of the work and read as true of all of it; nothing in the diff is wrong, only the sentence about it.
trigger: writing a completion phrase (`closed end-to-end`, `complete`, `round N done`, `identity`, `now has`) into a session card's summary or a PR title
why_it_happens: The completion sentence is written for a reader who was not there, so it summarizes — and summarizing upward is the natural direction when the session has just spent hours inside the part that did get done.

Insert into `session-close`, immediately before step 6's flip, a **claim ledger**: for each completion sentence in the card and the PR title, write one line — `claim → the diff hunk that earns it → the half it does NOT cover`. A claim with an empty third column is either genuinely total or a claim not yet examined, and the step says to prefer the narrower wording when the third column is non-empty. Two mechanical assists worth pairing with it: (a) the existing `claim-beyond-the-sample` route already matches `\b\d+ of (the )?\d+\b` — extend its regex with `closed end[- ]to[- ]end|round \d+ (is )?(complete|done)|now has (its own|a distinct)` so the route delivers TRAP-004 at these words too; (b) for sequenced ledgers specifically (sim-lab's verdicts, any numbered round), a two-line checker asserting the numbering is contiguous up to the high-water before a round-complete claim may be written.

name: Fixed the instances you saw; never swept for the class
one_line: The session repaired every instance its attention reached and closed as if the class were handled — the sweep that would have found the rest was available and mechanical, and a later session or audit ran it and found more.
trigger: About to close a card that says it fixed N instances of a named pattern, or about to apply the same patch at the third or later call-site, with no repo-wide sweep recorded.
why_it_happens: Once every instance in view is fixed, the class feels closed; the sweep is a separate deliberate act with no prompt attached to it, and the card's own language ("fixed the role orphans") reads as class-level.
instances: superbot-next · .sessions/2026-07-13-port-tooling-orphan.md:92 — three role orphans fixed by hand while the SAME class stayed alive in blackjack/rps/btd6/settings (nine more): "a manual sweep stops where the session's attention stops"

superbot · .sessions/2026-06-23-panel-back-nav-fix.md:64 — the nav class solved per-redraw-site (~30 hand-edits, and still regression-prone for any new panel) instead of at the constructor seam; the owner's next message pointed at the right altitude

proposed_fix: New step in `session-close`, between the born-red card and the READY PR — 'sweep before you claim the class': if the card's Scope or What-happened contains a class noun (`orphan`, `same class`, `all call-sites`, `every instance`, `N instances`), the card must carry a fenced `sweep:` block holding the actual command and its real exit/count (`rg -c '<pattern>' -g '!.sessions'`), and either a zero remainder or an enumerated list of the instances knowingly left with a reason. Enforced by a one-predicate leg in the strict gate: class noun present ⇒ `sweep:` block present with a non-empty command line, else exit 1. Third-call-site leg for the altitude case: flag a diff that applies the same ≥3-line hunk at ≥3 distinct call-sites with "a seam exists above this — say why you patched the sites instead".

name: A decision-bearing sentence that does not decide
one_line: A rule, gate condition, or scope statement was committed in prose that admits two readings or encodes an observed surface shape instead of the class it means — so it stayed letter-followable and wrong, or produced opposite verdicts depending on how it was parsed.
trigger: About to commit a sentence that something downstream must be judged against: a fixtures gate clause, a doctrine line, a card Scope statement about what was and was not touched.
why_it_happens: The author holds the single intended reading in their head while writing, so the sentence reads unambiguously to them exactly once. Nothing ever evaluates the sentence except a later human under time pressure.
instances: sim-lab · control/outbox-archive-2026-07.md:1226 — the registration's gate sentence admits a second "respectively" parse under which every cell passes and REJECT fires instead of INVALID; "the class is parse-dependent"

Substrate-kit-app · .sessions/2026-07-12-model-line-family-level.md:77 — doctrine banned "a full **dated** model ID" while the current generation's IDs carry no date: "the ban was letter-followable and wrong — wording lifted from one provider era silently rots"

venture-lab · .sessions/2026-07-13-control-plane-pack.md:114 — a card's Scope wrote V041 as "left untouched" for template-packs while the merge-wall packet in the same order WAS touched; accurate on close read, costs the next reader a re-read
date_span: 2026-07-12 → 2026-07-14 (3 repos, one week — the class is cross-repo, the window is narrow)
proposed_fix: Two concrete legs, not one. Leg 1 — `check_rule_decidability.py`: for any `fixtures.json`/pre-registration file, every key holding a decision clause must have a sibling `*_expr` string that `ast.parse`s and evaluates to a bool against the fixture's own sample rows; missing or non-parsing ⇒ exit 1, so the prose becomes the gloss and the expression the rule. Leg 2 — a card-Scope lint in the strict gate: flag any sentence containing a negated-scope phrase (`left untouched|not (modified|touched|changed)|unchanged`) whose named target also appears in this branch's changed-file list, message "this scope line negates something the diff touches — rewrite positively". Plus a `decision-capture` step: a doctrine sentence must name the class in prose AND pin the shape in a test, so the test goes red when the shape stops matching reality (the model-ID case).

name: An order's own clauses conflict, or one workstream's compliance clause goes unreconciled
one_line: A dispatched order carries a done-when that cannot be satisfied under the same repo's landing rules, or mandates a mechanism rather than an outcome, or contains a compliance clause another workstream then contradicts — and the executor works around the defect silently instead of raising it.
trigger: About to open a PR, or to close a workstream card, under an order whose done-when clauses have not been checked against the repo's landing policy and the order's other workstreams.
why_it_happens: The order arrives with authority, so its clauses are treated as constraints to satisfy rather than text to check for satisfiability — and an executor that notices the contradiction has no cheap channel for raising it, so working around it is the path of least friction. Compliance clauses lose to feature goals for the same reason: only the feature goals have acceptance rows.
instances: trading-strategy docs/retro/self-review-2026-07-09.md:15 — a done-when required merged PRs while the platform rules the same session followed mandated draft PRs: "a draft cannot merge, so the order was unsatisfiable by the actor executing it as briefed", and the work parked invisible in a draft nothing alerted on

websites .sessions/2026-07-12-order-017-private-lane-filter.md:73 — workstream A recorded "pokemon-mod-lab stays an honest 404 gap" as a virtue while workstream D of the same order had established the lane was private and should never have been shown publicly at all

superbot-games docs/retro/project-review-wind-down-2026-07-09-exploration.md:167 — a coordinator-authored done-when clause that ordered parking PRs behind a flag; the instruction itself was the defect and cost the lane real time
date_span: 2026-07-09 → 2026-07-12 (four days, 3 repos — spread is by repo, not by time; all three are seat-era dispatched-order work, so the pattern is evidenced across lanes but concentrated in one week)
proposed_fix: `check_order_satisfiable.py`, three predicates. (a) AUTHORING — parse the order's `done-when` clauses and cross-check against the repo's landing policy: fail when a done-when requires `merged`/`landed` while the repo's PR rules require `draft`, and fail when a done-when mandates a MECHANISM (`behind a flag`, `parked`, `in one PR`) rather than an outcome. (b) EXECUTION — fail on any PR whose `draft` is true (read `GET /repos/{o}/{r}/pulls/{n}` over direct egress with $GITHUB_PAT) while its in-diff .sessions/*.md card reads `Status: complete`; that is exactly the trading-strategy signal and nothing surfaces it today. Wire this into scripts/preflight.py beside the existing card-residue checks so `bootstrap.py check --strict` catches it. (c) COMPLIANCE PASS — every clause of a multi-workstream order tagged `compliance:` is expanded into its own checklist row that EVERY workstream card must tick, not only the workstream that owns it; a card closing with an unticked compliance row fails.
already_covered_by: fleet-manager/findings/retro-synthesis-2026-07-09.md (Draft-PR whiplash cluster + D5 'done as an agent-reachable state'), whose fix is live as docs/playbook.md R6 'READY, never draft' and the session-close skill's READY-PR step; the card-status half is TRAP-006/007

No coverage at all for the "open a PR" trigger moment or the cross-workstream compliance clause.

name: Take the order's framing as the task's boundary
one_line: When an incoming prompt or work order carries a narrow section — a READ FIRST list, a "docs only" scope stamp, an assertion about what the record currently says — the session adopts that framing as the task's true boundary instead of reconciling it against the same prompt's stated goal or against the tree, and never names the disagreement out loud.
trigger: the first response to an incoming prompt/order that carries a read list, a scope-restriction stamp, or an assertion about current record state
why_it_happens: The narrow section is operational and checkable; the goal statement is prose. Under any ambiguity the checkable one wins because it is the one you can visibly satisfy, and satisfying it feels like compliance rather than like a choice — so the choice is never surfaced as a choice. The estate's own doctrine already says the opposite (CONSTITUTION.md: 'session prompts are guidance, not orders'; CLAUDE.md: 'a handoff prompt that names a short read list is naming the minimum to act, never the boundary'), but no mechanism delivers that at the moment the prompt is read.
instances: [fleet-manager] .sessions/2026-08-05-handoff-fidelity-and-boot-path.md:96 — treated `READ FIRST` as the boundary of Phase 1 while the same prompt's job section asked for total comprehension; verified in file, and the card itself proposes the fix ('when a prompt's operational list and its stated goal disagree, that disagreement is itself a finding — resolve it out loud in the first response')

[superbot] .sessions/2026-06-16-dispatch-never-docs-only.md:61 — accepted the work order's 'docs only / no runtime code or feature scope' stamp at face value and never asked whether a dispatch order may shrink the routine's charter ('I do all build work'); harmless only by luck

[substrate-kit] .sessions/2026-07-10-order-011-f5-reading-a.md:35 — ORDER 011 ordered a re-score of runs 2–3 into FAIL against rows already recorded FAIL since #44/#85; the order's premise about the record was stale and the instruction changed no verdict field
proposed_fix: Two links. LINK 1 (hook): add a `route_docs.py` UserPromptSubmit route id `incoming-order-framing`, trigger regex `['READ FIRST', '\\bdocs[- ]only\\b', '\\bno runtime code\\b', '\\bscope[- ]restrict', '\\bout of scope\\b', '\\bORDER \\d{3}\\b', '\\bwork order\\b', '\\bre-?score\\b.*\\b(FAIL|PASS)\\b']`, delivering `docs/traps.md#TRAP-008` plus `docs/intent.md § how to decide without him`. LINK 2 (skill): insert a step 0 `SCOPE RECONCILIATION` into `intake` (and mirror it in the receiving half of `prompt-preflight`), whose output is three lines the first reply must carry: (a) quote the prompt's narrowest scope statement, (b) quote its broadest goal statement, (c) declare which governs and why — plus, for every state-claim the order makes ('both rows are X', 'this is not yet done'), cite the row/commit that confirms it before acting on it. A restriction that shrinks a routine's standing charter is reported as a smell, not honored silently.

name: Author your own where a source of record exists
one_line: A governing artifact already names what to produce — an oracle's bytes, a slice spec's path, a pre-registered rubric's category set — and the session produces its own version instead, sometimes for a good reason and sometimes to make its own narrative come out right; nothing compares the delivery to the spec that governs it.
trigger: about to create a file, handler, or verdict/category label that the governing spec, oracle or pre-registered rubric does not name
why_it_happens: Writing the thing is faster than fetching the authoritative thing, and the invented version passes its own tests because it was written against them. In the scorer case the mechanism is worse than laziness: the deviating category was the one that let the author's own prior narrative survive its own rubric, which is why blind scoring caught it and self-review did not.
instances: [superbot-next] .sessions/2026-07-11-btd6-unmapped-rehome.md:14 — band-5 sessions built invented handlers, usage cards and a parallel `ref_*_view`/`strat_*_view` implementation with its own copy rather than porting the oracle's bytes; the legacy alias trees routed to the inventions until this session repointed every spec at the real oracle handler

[fleet-manager] findings/2026-08-13-intent-map-fresh-scorer.md:120 — the outcome-aware scorer created an unregistered 'evidence-resolved' category so fragment 7 did not count toward the verdict, drifting from the rubric it had itself pre-registered; two blind scorers applied the anchor as written and diverged (confirmed at line 129: 'direction of prior bias: toward the agents / its own headline')

[superbot-games] .sessions/2026-07-14-night-truth-stamp-anchor.md:66 — slice #119 placed its test suite at `tests/shared/sim/…` rather than the `tests/shared/…` its slice spec named; the control case for this pattern, since the deviation and its floor-guard rationale are in both the card and the PR body
proposed_fix: New `scripts/check_spec_conformance.py` in `scripts/preflight.py`. Requires a `Spec:` / `Oracle:` / `Rubric:` header field on any card whose work is governed by one (kit cards already carry a header block; the field is empty-with-reason otherwise). Predicate: parse the named spec for (i) the directories/paths it enumerates and (ii) its enumerated label set — verdict/category values; then require that every path the diff ADDS sits under a directory the spec names, and every label appearing in a results/verdict table in the diff is a member of the spec's set. Anything outside either set fails UNLESS the card carries, on the same commit, `DEVIATION: <spec path>:<line> — <reason>`. This passes superbot-games #119 exactly as it was delivered, fails the unregistered 'evidence-resolved' category, and fails a handler authored at a path the port map does not name. Pair it with the standing rule the fm case already proved: rubric-scored work is scored blind by a fresh agent, never by the author of the narrative under test.

name: Review evidence trusted without checking it against the tree
one_line: Reviews carrying invented file:line citations, and approvals relayed through a file or another agent, were acted on as genuine — the review's own evidence was never resolved at the cited blob.
trigger: ingesting an external reviewer's findings, quoting a review comment that carries file:line citations, or accepting a stated authorization at merge time
why_it_happens: A review comment arrives formatted exactly like a real one — severity badge, path, line range — and the cost of resolving each citation is high enough that no session does it by hand. The one session that checked mechanically found the hand-written incident ledger had missed a case, which is the tell: human verification of citations does not scale even when someone is actively looking for fabrication. Corollary from that card, worth keeping: re-derive a hand-verified ledger's claims mechanically before treating its named failure modes as the failure surface.
instances: sim-lab · .sessions/2026-07-12-verdict-016-review-authenticity.md:7 — three verified-fabricated @codex replies, each with an anchored line range past EOF at its own cited blob; incident #1's REPORT.md L243–L245 against a 241-line blob was not even in the hand-written ledger, so the ledger of fabrications was itself incomplete

idea-engine · docs/audits/eap-project-audit-2026-07-14.md:76 — three fabricated-evidence incidents at program level, which is what suspended the external verdict-review step entirely (dual-cited with P4)
superbot · .sessions/2026-07-11-fleet-dispatch-prompts.md:28 — a relayed 'owner approved' message accepted as merge authority and used to clear a merge; the authorization variant of the same defect
date_span: 2026-07-11 → 2026-07-14 (one week, 3 repos) — narrow because it was found by a purpose-built sim; nothing scans for it before or since
proposed_fix: Build the V016 gate as a portable checker — it is specced in sim-lab and exists nowhere as code. New `src/engine/checks/check_review_citations.py`: for every citation matching `([\w./-]+\.\w+)[:#]L?(\d+)(?:-L?(\d+))?` inside a review comment, review record, or quoted reviewer finding, resolve the path at the cited blob/SHA (`git cat-file -p <sha>:<path>`, falling back to worktree HEAD) and FAIL when the path does not exist or the end line exceeds the blob's line count. Measured on the sim-lab corpus, line-range<=EOF alone catches 3/3 — robust even to a fabricator who stops inventing commit SHAs. Two callers: run it in preflight over committed review records, and call it from the P1 merge hook before a fetched review's findings are acted on. name: The freshness stamp and the content disagree
one_line: A document's as-of date is advanced over sections that were never revised, or new facts are written under an unchanged five-week-old stamp, or a 'current truth' block is authored so that it is one change behind the moment its own PR merges.
trigger: Edit/Write of a file carrying a top-level `as_of` / `Updated:` / `Freshness:` field, or a block whose text asserts what the latest change is.
why_it_happens: The stamp is treated as a signature on the commit rather than a claim about every sentence beneath it, and a 'latest change' line is written from the state before the change it is part of.
instances: fleet-manager PR #887 r3835916363 — ledger freshness advanced to 2026-08-22 while the life-story section still says the fix is merely proposed and the live game untouched
websites PR #510 r3826430341 — registry rows updated with 2026-08-20 cutover facts under an unchanged top-level as_of of 2026-07-13
substrate-kit PR #588 r3881282931 — current-truth block and control/status.md still call #587 the latest post-release work, so both ledgers are stale the instant this PR merges
proposed_fix: PreToolUse/PostToolUse rule plus a gate predicate: (1) a diff that changes any data row in a file with a top-level `as_of` must change `as_of` in the same diff; (2) a diff that changes ONLY the stamp must list in the card what was re-verified — otherwise the stamp certifies unread content; (3) a line asserting 'the latest change is #N' must name the PR it ships in, or be rendered from git at build time rather than hand-written. The hook can quote the target file's own stale sections by comparing each section's last-touched commit date against the new stamp.

already_covered_by: Nothing. TRAP-001 (docs/traps.md:38) is the reader-side dual — "you are about to state what is true now and your basis is a document" — with REQUIRED PREVENTION "read the live surface with a credential this session already holds." It says nothing about a writer advancing a freshness stamp over unrevised text, or shipping a currency claim that its own diff falsifies. TRAP-001 is also listed in the register's own coverage table as having no deterministic checker, so this would be new enforcement rather than a duplicate route.

name: Provenance SHA that does not identify the tree it labels
one_line: A commit SHA is stamped into a build field, artifact name or generated header where it cannot possibly identify the tree that was built or generated.
trigger: Edit/Write or CI step that writes a 40-hex SHA (or `${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}` / `git rev-parse` output) into a `build.commit`, `committed_at`-adjacent provenance field, an artifact filename, or a `Generated from <sha>` header.
why_it_happens: The SHA the agent has in hand at write time (PR head, or the parent commit) is *a* real SHA, so it looks correct and passes every syntactic check; the SHA that would be correct either does not exist yet (the merge commit) or requires an extra call to obtain. The owner flagged this one himself — it is the only owner-voiced incident in the class — and the #2102 agent explicitly reasoned its way to leaving the wrong value in place rather than omitting the field, which is why a written rule will not close it: the losing move is a deliberate, argued choice.
instances: superbot PR #2102 — https://github.com/menno420/superbot/pull/2102#discussion_r3580745438 (build.commit = PR branch HEAD, a SHA that will never exist on main; agent recognised it and declined to fix)
couch-legend PR #11 — https://github.com/menno420/couch-legend/pull/11#discussion_r3833938259 (APK named `couch-legend-<head>-debug.apk` while checkout built GitHub's synthetic merge revision)
fleet-manager PR #122 — https://github.com/menno420/fleet-manager/pull/122#discussion_r3566962913 (24 generated registry copies stamped with a stale, non-ancestor provenance SHA)
date_span: 2026-07 → 2026-08-21 (two of the three cites carry no date in the evidence set)
proposed_fix: New `tools/check_provenance_sha.py`, wired into `scripts/preflight.py` (so it rides the existing required `substrate-gate` check) and into the exporter's own tests: (1) every SHA written into a provenance field or artifact label must equal `git rev-parse HEAD` measured in the same job/process that produced the body — assert equality rather than trusting the CI context variable; (2) pre-merge, a PR-branch or merge-preview SHA is not a valid value — the field must be omitted or written as `unmerged:<head>` rather than guessed; (3) post-merge assertion that every committed `build.commit` is reachable from `main` (`git merge-base --is-ancestor`); (4) for generated files, the stamped SHA's tree must reproduce the generated body byte-for-byte. name: Exception written wider than the case that earned it
one_line: One narrow finding is disposed of by editing a shared gate — an allowlist entry, an exemption class, an advisory/blocking set — at a granularity far coarser than the case, so the gate's future behaviour diverges from its own written contract.
trigger: Edit/Write of `.substrate/check-exceptions.yml`, any file matching `*exempt*|*allowlist*|*waiver*|*suppress*`, or a checker source line that moves a category token between the advisory set and the blocking/exit-affecting set.
why_it_happens: Exception files are matched by whatever keys the tool already supports, and (path, kind) is usually the only key on offer — so the narrow justification lives in a free-text `reason` field that no matcher reads. The session writes a true sentence about one line and a rule about a whole file, and the gate goes green, which is the signal it was optimising for. Nobody sees the widening again until a real defect is swallowed, by which time the entry looks like considered prior art.
instances: idea-engine PR #899 — https://github.com/menno420/idea-engine/pull/899#discussion_r3778313728 — allowlist entry whose reason names one line but whose match key is only (path, kind), suppressing every future false-wall in docs/CAPABILITIES.md
