name: Procedure written to a done state the environment cannot reach
one_line: A journey, worklist or close-out path is specified as complete at a step that is internal, owner-gated or dependent on a mechanism that is not installed — so an executor following it stalls or stops short of the real outcome.
trigger: Writing a done-when criterion, close-out step or end-to-end journey into a plan, worklist or product doc — before the turn ends, resolve each terminal step to the mechanism that produces it and check that mechanism exists and is agent-reachable.
why_it_happens: Planning happens at the altitude of intent, where 'merged', 'deployed' and 'closed' read as single steps; the capability record that says otherwise lives in a different file and is consulted when acting, not when writing. The result is a plan whose failure surfaces only in the continuation session that has to stop mid-slice.
instances: couch-legend #5 — discussion_r3830263339 (close-out doc advertises server-side merge in a repo where the enabler is uninstalled and auto-merge is off; the session ends with the PR open indefinitely)
fleet-manager #868 — discussion_r3824349486 (slice written as fully executable although CAPABILITIES.md records Pages enablement as owner-only; no preflight, no queued owner action)
fleet-manager #882 — discussion_r3833852557 (feedback journey terminates at capture; developer fix, reporter notification, retest and verified closure absent)
proposed_fix: A `done-when resolution` step added to `implementation-prompt`, `scope-backlog-item` and `prep-owner-steps`: every terminal step must name the mechanism that produces it (workflow file, API call, owner action) and be resolved against `docs/CAPABILITIES.md` + `docs/owner-queue.md`; anything the ledger records as owner-gated must ship with an `OQ-` slug queued in the same diff, and the slice must be written to stop cleanly at that boundary. Two decidable backstops: `tools/check_done_when.py` fails a worklist slice whose done-when references an owner-gated capability with no `OQ-` reference; and any doc naming an auto-merge/close-out path must be validated against that repo's real settings (`allow_auto_merge == true` and the enabler workflow present at head) before the path may be written. For journeys, a review-time question with a written answer: name the actor and the observable outcome at the last step — if the last step is a state change inside the system, the journey is not finished.
already_covered_by: Not covered by an existing trap. `docs/traps.md` holds TRAP-001..007; the nearest neighbours are TRAP-006 (card flipped to `complete` before the branch is pushed) and TRAP-007 (card flipped to `complete` while a requested review is unanswered) — same premature-completion family, but both are about a session misreporting its own state, not about a plan specifying a done-state the environment cannot produce. Partial skill-level overlap only: `.claude/skills/scope-backlog-item/SKILL.md` already carries a buildable / owner-gated / dead classification with a six-field owner ask, which covers the item-level half of the proposed fix.

name: Destructive command with its safety check ordered after the damage
one_line: The agent authors or ships a `reset --hard` / `rmtree` step whose guard runs after the data it was meant to protect is already gone.
trigger: Bash execution OR Edit/Write of file content containing `git reset --hard`, `git clean -fd`, `shutil.rmtree(`, `rm -rf` — i.e. any irreversible operation entering a procedure, skill body, or tool.
why_it_happens: The agent reasons about the happy path it is building for (fresh clone, disjoint directories) and writes the destructive step as setup. The guard is added afterwards, as prose, and prose has no ordering enforcement — so 'stop if dirty' lands textually after the command that made it clean. Nothing in the estate reads a procedure as a sequence.
instances: couch-legend PR #5 — https://github.com/menno420/couch-legend/pull/5#discussion_r3830169998 — mandatory first boot step hard-resets the worktree before the 'stop on dirty worktree' inspection that was supposed to protect it

couch-legend PR #5 — https://github.com/menno420/couch-legend/pull/5#discussion_r3830351641 — follow-up fix patched the dirty case but kept `git reset --hard origin/main`, so a clean branch ahead of main still loses its commits at boot

fleet-manager PR #934 — https://github.com/menno420/fleet-manager/pull/934#discussion_r3839362660 — bundler recursively deletes tracked `sources/`, `excluded/`, `notebook-*` in the source checkout when `--out` overlaps `--src`, with no path-overlap validation
date_span: 2026-08-23 (fm #934) plus two undated couch-legend PR #5 comments whose ids sit immediately below the 2026-08-23 fleet-manager ones
proposed_fix: Route + checker. (1) doc-routes.json id `destructive-op-preflight`, tools [Bash, Edit, Write], when: ["git\\s+reset\\s+--hard", "git\\s+clean\\s+-[fdxn]*[fdx]", "shutil\\.rmtree\\(", "rm\\s+-rf\\b"], repeat: true (an ACTION guard must never be spent), says: name the three instances and demand the inspection-before-destruction ordering. (2) `tools/check_destructive_preflight.py` in `scripts/preflight.py` → `check --strict`, three decidable predicates: (a) in any `.md`/skill/procedure file, a destructive git command must be preceded IN THE SAME FILE by an inspection step (`git status`, `git log @{u}..HEAD`, `git stash list`) and an abort clause; (b) `reset --hard <remote-ref>` must be guarded by a `git rev-list --count <remote-ref>..HEAD` == 0 assertion; (c) any `shutil.rmtree(X)` in a tool taking both an input path arg and an output path arg must be preceded by an `os.path.realpath` overlap assertion — reject resolved out == src or out containing src.
already_covered_by: No trap in `docs/traps.md` covers this (TRAP-001..007 are dated-doc-as-current, exit-code-after-pipe, absence-as-evidence, over-wide claim, owner-corrected-from-memory, and the two card-flip traps) — so `maps_to_existing_trap: "new"` is right at the trap-register level. But `gap_class: "absent"` is wrong: `/home/user/fleet-manager/.claude/hooks/git_state_guard.py` already exists and is wired at `PreToolUse` on `Bash|WebFetch|Read|Glob|Grep|Edit|Write|MultiEdit` in `.claude/settings.json`. Correct classification is `partial`.

name: An advertised path the author never executed once
one_line: A command sequence, override, or interpreter invocation is written into a doc, skill, deny message, or settings file and shipped as working without a single execution.
trigger: Edit/Write that adds a fenced command span to a `.md`/skill body, a `command` field in `settings*.json`, or an override instruction inside a hook's deny/warn text.
why_it_happens: Writing a command and running it feel like the same act at authoring time — the sentence is plausible, the flags are the ones the API docs list, and the file lands green because nothing in the gate executes prose. This is TRAP-004's shape with N=0: a universal claim ('this recipe works', 'export this to override') from a sample of zero runs. The couch-legend case is the worst variant because the untested thing was the gate apparatus itself, so its silence read as success.
instances: couch-legend PR #5 — https://github.com/menno420/couch-legend/pull/5#discussion_r3830170001 — every installed hook wired to an absolute interpreter path absent from the target environment; all hooks exit 127 before `bootstrap.py` runs, silently disabling pre-tool, session-start, post-edit and stop gates

couch-legend PR #5 — https://github.com/menno420/couch-legend/pull/5#discussion_r3830351646 — upgrade recipe downloads release assets over files that always exist in the repo root without `--clobber`/`--dir`, so the documented upgrade stops on collision

fleet-manager PR #834 — https://github.com/menno420/fleet-manager/pull/834#discussion_r3744760035 — deny message advertises an env-var bypass that cannot be armed mid-session (a Bash child's export does not mutate the host process; MCP calls carry no per-call env)
proposed_fix: Skill step + checker. (1) `implementation-prompt` / `session-close` gain one step: every command span and every escape hatch shipped in prose carries an execution receipt comment (`# ran 2026-08-28 @<sha>, exit 0`) or is explicitly labelled `UNVERIFIED — never executed`. (2) `tools/check_command_receipts.py` in `check --strict`: extract fenced command spans from changed `.md`/skill files and every `command` field in changed `settings*.json`; for hook commands require the interpreter to resolve (`shutil.which`/`os.path.exists`) AND a smoke invocation returning != 127 — this alone catches the couch-legend hook wipeout deterministically; for doc spans require a receipt or the UNVERIFIED label. (3) doc-routes id `hook-wiring-smoke-test`, tools [Edit, Write], when: ["\"command\"\\s*:\\s*\"/", "hooks/.*\\.py"] — 'you just wired a hook; run it once and paste the exit code'.
maps_to_existing_trap: new (adjacent to TRAP-004 — a claim wider than its sample, where the sample is zero executions)
already_covered_by: Nothing. Closest neighbours in docs/traps.md are TRAP-004 (a claim wider than its sample — but scoped to numeric/census phrasing, and its `claim-beyond-the-sample` route cannot see a command span or a settings `command` field) and TRAP-002 (an exit code read after a pipe — a misread execution, not an absent one). No existing checker in tools/ inspects shipped command spans, hook wiring, or advertised overrides; install_root_hooks.py installs hooks without validating that they run, and test_codex_hooks.py tests hook logic, not wiring resolution.

name: Unknown rendered to the owner as a confirmed zero
one_line: A read that came back incomplete, contradictory or truncated is displayed as a definite finding — 'No owner comments', 'no comments await action', a Cards total — with the incompleteness surviving only in a warnings field or on stderr that never reaches the reader.
trigger: Edit/Write of a rendering or artifact-writing branch containing a definitive zero-state literal (`^(No|Zero|None) [A-Za-z ]+$`, `no \w+ await`, `nothing to (do|action)`) or reading a `truncated|warnings|partial|is_known` field.
why_it_happens: Two-state rendering. The code has present/absent and no third state for 'we could not tell', so every unknown falls into whichever of the two is the fallthrough — always absence, because absence is the quiet one. This is the most owner-facing member of the class: it is the one where a manufactured null is read by a human as a verified fact, and the estate's own generator (estate_activity.py) committed it.
instances: websites #523 r3873968523 — definitive 'no comments await action' rendered from a root count while the detail read had recorded disagreement and incompleteness warnings in the same result object
websites #523 r3874117722 — fallthrough maps a missing root-index row (a contract contradiction) to the 'No owner comments' display instead of an unknown state
fm #947 r3864796292 — GitHub's `truncated` flag warns on stderr only; `refresh` still writes an estate-log.md whose header presents `Cards` as a total and whose docs promise every card
proposed_fix: A rendering contract plus `tools/check_absence_rendering.py`: (1) any definitive-zero literal must be emitted only from a branch guarded by an explicit completeness predicate — red when a definitive-zero branch is reachable while a sibling field named `warnings|errors|truncated|partial` is non-empty, or while `is_known` is False; (2) any generator that reads a `truncated`/`incomplete` flag must write it into its OUTPUT artifact, not only to stderr or a log — the predicate is that the identifier appears inside the template/write path, and a header presenting a count as a total must carry the completeness token beside it; (3) three-state rendering as a stated convention (present / absent / unknown-because-<reason>), added to docs/conventions/ and routed on the zero-state regexes so it fires while the branch is being written.
maps_to_existing_trap: new — TRAP-010 candidate; TRAP-003 crossed into the UI layer, where the reader is the owner rather than a session
already_covered_by: Conceptually split across two existing traps, but covered by neither's route. TRAP-003 (docs/traps.md:96-122, "Absence of evidence recorded as evidence of absence") carries the reasoning for the contradiction-to-zero instances, but its TRIGGER is scoped to writing a prose absence claim on the strength of an empty search, and its `absence-claim` route regexes (verified above) do not match any of the rendering literals in these instances. TRAP-004 (docs/traps.md:125, "A claim wider than the sample that produced it") actually covers the truncated-total half better than TRAP-003 does — its trigger is "you are about to write a fraction, a total, or a universal covering a population larger than the set you actually measured", which is precisely fm #947's `Cards` header and websites #521's unqualified repository total. Both are marked "not yet" for a checker in the register's own table (docs/traps.md:378-379). So the proposal is a merge of TRAP-003 and TRAP-004 translated from the document surface to the code/rendering surface, where the reader is the owner rather than a session — new as a routed, checkable trap, not new as an idea.

name: Derivative outruns its source
one_line: A packet, outbound mail or port is written from an authoritative source, and the derivative drops binding clauses of that source or asserts exactly what the source says it does not establish.
trigger: Edit/Write of a derived artifact — a file whose body cites a source path or names a lettered/ODd step id (`OD-\d+`, `\bW\d\b`, `\b[A-Z]\d\b`), an outbound draft (`*mail*`, `*draft*`, `render_*_mail.py`), or a port diff whose own notes record the original constraint.
why_it_happens: Compression is the job — a packet exists to be shorter than the program, a mail to be shorter than the sweep, a port to be simpler than the original. The source's limiting clauses are the cheapest thing to lose because they are the parts that add words without adding action, and the exclusions section is structurally the last thing read. The derivative then reads as complete and self-consistent, so nothing downstream can tell that a clause is missing; the reviewer had to hold both documents at once to see it.
instances: fleet-manager PR #861 — https://github.com/menno420/fleet-manager/pull/861#discussion_r3783109614 — execution packet compressed OD-8/W1 to stop/watch/delete, dropping name reclamation and reference repointing

fleet-manager PR #943 — https://github.com/menno420/fleet-manager/pull/943#discussion_r3846776981 — send-ready email concluded across the estate exactly what the source sweep's §6 says the work does not establish

superbot-next PR #255 — https://github.com/menno420/superbot-next/pull/255#discussion_r3566364555 — ported command assigned a coarse `audience_tier` mapping to `moderate_members` while its own port notes recorded `manage_messages`
proposed_fix: Chain: skill step -> route -> checker. (1) Add a `source-clause ledger` step to `implementation-prompt`, `prep-owner-steps` and `continuation-prompt`: before any derivative is written, paste the source's binding clauses and its exclusions section into the session card as a two-column ledger — each clause CARRIED or DROPPED-with-reason, each exclusion NOT-ASSERTED — and treat a missing ledger as a gate-worthy defect. (2) Route `deriving-from-a-source` on Edit/Write when the new text names a step id or a `docs/**` source path, quoting: 'Your derivative is only as narrow as its source. Enumerate the source's clauses and its exclusions section before you compress.' (3) `tools/check_derived_scope.py` in `check --strict`: for a file naming a step id, parse the program's definition of that step and fail when the derivative covers fewer clause verbs than the definition contains; for a file citing a source path, extract the source's `does not establish|out of scope|this work does not|§ exclusions` block and fail on any topic noun from that block asserted affirmatively in the derivative; for a port diff, compare the tier's mapped permission against the permission named in the diff notes.
maps_to_existing_trap: TRAP-004 adjacent (it covers a claim wider than the SAMPLE; this is a claim wider than the SOURCE PERMITS) — extend TRAP-004 with a second axis, or open TRAP-009
already_covered_by: TRAP-004 covers instance 2 substantially but not exactly. In the same #943 review round the agent conceded three other findings it grouped as "wider-than-measured claims cut" (round 3: findings 4, 10, 11, 12), which is straight TRAP-004 territory — a claim wider than the sample. What is genuinely new is the second axis the pattern names: the source carried an explicit, structured exclusions section ("§ 6 · What this file does NOT establish"), and the derivative crossed it. That is a sharper and mechanically checkable variant, not a fresh class. Instance 1 (a binding clause of a cited step id dropped in compression) is not covered by TRAP-004 at all. Recommendation: extend TRAP-004 with the source-exclusions axis rather than opening TRAP-009, and drop instance 3 from the class — it belongs with the merge-before-Codex-answers rule and a superbot-next-local tier-mapping check, not here.

name: Half-swept change — siblings left asserting the old value
one_line: A shared default, constant or framing is changed at one call site or one surface, and the sibling sites carrying the same value are left untouched, so the system holds two contradictory states at once and the change defeats its own stated purpose.
trigger: Edit/Write that changes a literal argument at one call site of a shared function, or edits framing/copy in a shared base file (`base.html`, layout/template, settings/constants module) — fire post-edit and require a sweep count of the remaining sites before the session card may flip.
why_it_happens: The edit that fixes the reported symptom is at the site where the symptom was observed, and that edit makes the reported problem go away — so the change verifies as done against the report rather than against the invariant. Sibling sites are invisible from the diff, and metadata (`<title>`, meta description, defaults) is doubly invisible because it never appears in the rendered view the author checks. The result is not a stale corner but an active contradiction, published on the most-visited route.
instances: superbot-next PR #373 — https://github.com/menno420/superbot-next/pull/373#discussion_r3569779093 — regen interval changed at the cast gate, hub renderer left on the old default, two divergent views of the same energy state

websites PR #512 — https://github.com/menno420/websites/pull/512#discussion_r3838178909 — past-tense era notice added to base.html, homepage hero left present-tense, two mutually exclusive era claims on the primary route

websites PR #512 — https://github.com/menno420/websites/pull/512#discussion_r3838205908 — visible copy retired while shared `<title>`/meta defaults still emit the retired present-tense line on every generated page
proposed_fix: Chain, built on apparatus that already exists. (1) Extend `tools/check_claim_propagation.py` — today it sweeps only `docs/` and `.sessions/` for retracted wordings — with a `--swept '<old string>'` mode and scan roots widened to templates (`**/*.html`, `**/*.jinja`), generated output and code, so a retirement commit fails while any occurrence of the retired phrase survives anywhere renderable, metadata included. (2) Add a call-site coherence predicate to the same tool: when a diff changes a literal argument at a call site, enumerate every other call site of that callee passing a different literal and fail unless the diff touches them or the session card names the divergence as intended. (3) Route `partial-sweep` (Edit/Write on `base.html`, `**/templates/**`, `**/constants*.py`, `**/settings*.py`) saying: 'You changed one of N sites. Run the sweep and paste the remaining count — a grep that returns nothing proves your query ran, not that the sweep is complete (TRAP-003): show the positive control.'
maps_to_existing_trap: new (TRAP-003 adjacent — the completeness of a sweep is established by a positive control, not by a clean grep; this pattern is TRAP-003's failure mode applied to code and templates rather than to prose claims)

name: Declared ready without measuring against the governing spec
one_line: A handoff artifact — send-ready copy, a dispatch prompt — is produced and declared ready while violating the form, the numeric bound, or the objective its governing plan states, so a successful execution still fails the goal.
trigger: Edit/Write of a file containing `<!-- COPY -->`/`COPY:`/`PASTE-READY`/`send-ready` markers, of anything under `docs/prompts/`, or of text matching `\b(deliverable|dispatch|hand this to|paste this)\b`. Route id `handoff-artifact-write`; the same trigger is the entry point for `prompt-preflight`.
why_it_happens: Producing the artifact and checking it against the plan are separate reads, and the plan is usually closed by the time the draft is polished. Fluency substitutes for compliance: a well-written 1,700-word draft feels finished, and a report-shaped dispatch feels safe.
instances: fm #943 r3846871620 — a 482-word first-person narrative with personal judgements, thanks and the owner's signature ghost-written into a section the governing plan reserves to the owner and caps at a skeleton of pointers, then labelled a scaffold
fm #943 r3846871619 — Part 2 shipped at ~1,700 words (lines 98–258) against the owner's explicit short, cold-readable one-page bound, never measured against the stated limit

superbot #1998 r3564790355 — the only dispatch routed for a confirmed Rule-6 false-green bug asked Codex for a findings report rather than edit/test/open a fix PR, so a fully successful run would restate the known bug and leave production false-green
proposed_fix: Route → skill step → checker. CHECKER `tools/check_handoff_artifact.py`: for each COPY-marked block, (a) word-count it and assert against the numeric bound parsed from the governing plan it cites (`one page` → the plan's own words-per-page constant, `≤ N words`, `short`→ requires an explicit bound); a block with no citable governing plan fails as unbounded; (b) if the block's section is named in the plan as owner-voiced/owner-reserved, assert it contains no first-person pronouns outside quotes and no signature line — form violation, not a judgement call. SKILL step in `prompt-preflight` (already mandatory for any session/handoff prompt per the boot table): a DELIVERABLE-MATCHES-STATE gate — if the prompt's input names an already-confirmed bug or a known fix, the deliverable verb must be in {edit, test, open PR, merge}; a `report`/`investigate`/`findings` deliverable over a confirmed bug is a lint failure, since such a dispatch can succeed without changing anything. ROUTE `handoff-artifact-write` delivers both at the moment of writing.
maps_to_existing_trap: new — TRAP-010 candidate; distinct from TRAP-007, which guards the review window rather than whether the artifact meets its own spec
already_covered_by: none — docs/traps.md holds TRAP-001..007 and none covers artifact-vs-its-own-spec. TRAP-007 (card flipped to complete while a requested review is unanswered) guards the review window, exactly as the pattern says; TRAP-004 (claim wider than its sample) is the shape of the OTHER two findings in the same fm #943 review (r3846871601, r3846871613), correctly not claimed here. Register currently ends at 007, so this is a TRAP-008 candidate, not TRAP-010, unless a parallel harvest has claimed 008/009.

name: Handoff pointer aimed at a surface the next session cannot reach
one_line: The handoff itself is written correctly, but the thing it points at is not on the surface the receiving session will read — an uncommitted plan file, a repo outside the prompt's declared scope, or a card and owner ask left on a branch the procedure then closes unmerged.
trigger: Edit/Write of a claim, prompt, or procedure file whose added text names a repo-relative doc path, an `owner/repo` outside the file's own scope block, or a step matching `/clos(e|ing) the PR (unmerged|without merging)/i` — plus Bash `gh pr close` in a session whose branch carries an in-diff `.sessions/*.md` card.
why_it_happens: The writing session can see the target — the file is in its working tree, the repo is attached to its container, the branch is checked out — so the pointer resolves for the author and only for the author. Nothing in the tree distinguishes 'exists here' from 'exists on main'.
instances: superbot PR #1079 — discussion_r3441215091 (active claim routes parallel agents to docs/planning/ultracode-fleet-plan-2026-06-19.md, never committed)

name: A missing section is an error, never a zero
one_line: A generated or hand-written report's absent section read as a count of zero — the nulls section says "skipped: none" while a whole dimension was silently dropped.
trigger: about to write, or read, a report's nulls / deviations / carve-outs / skipped section
why_it_happens: Report generators omit empty sections to keep output tidy, which makes "not measured" and "measured, none" render identically.
instances: [superbot-games] .sessions/2026-07-11-kit-upgrade-v1.8.0.md:68 — the v1.7.1 upgrade session concluded zero carve-outs by inference because the report had no carve-out section; v1.8.0's explicit zero-carve-out section (kit #156a) closes exactly that ambiguity

[Substrate-kit-app] .sessions/2026-07-19-gsw-4-pr-latency.md:64 — §4 "Honest deviations & nulls" listed `Skipped repos: none` while open→merge latency had been deliberately dropped from harness scope and never logged
date_span: 2026-07-11 → 2026-07-19 (2 repos; the narrowest window here — kept because the fix is already half-shipped upstream)
proposed_fix: Insert one step into `session-close` (and mirror it in `owner-brief`, which renders the same sections for the owner): the nulls/deviations section must enumerate every dimension the work was SCOPED to produce and mark each `delivered` / `0 — searched <what>` / `dropped — <reason, where deferred>`; a dimension that is absent from the section is a defect, not a zero. Mechanical half, since the skill alone will not bind: `check_zero_sections.py` — for report templates with declared sections (nulls, deviations, carve-outs, skipped), fail when a declared section is missing from a rendered report, and require every generator (`upgrade-distribution`'s carve-out scan, measurement harnesses) to emit an explicit `0 —` line rather than omitting the heading. The kit already did this once for carve-outs in v1.8.0; generalise that shape to every declared section.
already_covered_by: TRAP-003 (docs/traps.md:96, with the live `absence-claim` doc route on Edit/Write) — plus substrate-kit #156a, which already fixed the one verifiable generator: v1.8.0 emits `## Carve-out scan … ran, 0 found` unconditionally.
TRAP-003 (register entry covers the class; its `absence-claim` route does NOT fire on this shape) + the carve-out half already shipped in kit code, vendored here at bootstrap.py:21114-21170

name: Measured and inferred shipped at one confidence
one_line: A findings document or evidence table carried the session's own judgements at the same confidence as its measurements — no per-claim marker at all, or an interpretive clause parked in the documented-record column — which is precisely the separation the estate's certainty legend exists to hold.
trigger: About to commit a findings doc or an evidence/provenance table containing both numbers you measured and conclusions you drew.
why_it_happens: Both sentences are true and checkable, so nothing feels wrong while writing; the provenance distinction costs the author nothing and saves only the reader, and the existing `check_claim_provenance.py` does not reach findings prose or table cells.
instances: [spider-swing] .sessions/2026-08-01-claim-provenance-retrofit.md:17 — the preceding measurement session never marked which sentences were measurements and which were inferences: "exactly the distinction the owner has been correcting all day, roughly fourteen times"

fleet-manager · findings/2026-08-13-intent-map-fresh-scorer/scorer-2.md:336 — agent judgements sat in the ESTABLISHED (documented-record) column rather than DERIVED: "the mildest form of the column-blur the procedure exists to prevent"
proposed_fix: Extend `src/engine/checks/check_claim_provenance.py` with two predicates over `docs/findings/**` and `findings/**`. (a) Every sentence containing a numeral, a percentage, or a comparative (`faster|more|fewer|larger|N of M`) must have one of `MEASURED|MEASURED-PRIOR|OWNER|REASONED|REVIEWED|UNVERIFIED|NOT-VERIFIABLE` in the same paragraph — else exit 1 naming the sentence. Wire it into the `intake` skill's intent-map step so the map is checked at the moment it is authored.

name: The owner absorbed what the session should have resolved
one_line: An owner-facing recommendation shipped without the consequence it carried, or a reversible decision was parked behind an owner flag instead of taken and flagged — in both cases the owner did work the session held everything needed to do.
trigger: Writing an owner-facing recommendation, or placing a ⚑ park / owner-action marker on a decision that has a reversible default.
why_it_happens: Deferring reads as caution and costs the session nothing visible, while stating a consequence requires reasoning past the recommendation itself. A done-when clause that mandates parking inverts the estate's own decide-rather-than-ask standing instruction, and nothing checks a ⚑ for whether a default existed.
instances: superbot · .sessions/2026-07-02-hq-guild-live.md:64 — recommended SuperBot for the HQ guild without flagging the state-pollution angle (a production bot in a management guild writes production settings rows for that guild); the owner spotted it himself

superbot-games · docs/retro/project-review-wind-down-2026-07-09-exploration.md:156 — "⚑-parking mandated by a done-when clause cost two decisions a ~2h park that decide-and-flag would have shipped (D-0006→D-0007)"
date_span: 2026-07-02 → 2026-07-09 (one week, 2 repos — the weakest-spread cluster in this class)
proposed_fix: Two steps in `prep-owner-steps`, both enforceable by one gate leg. Step: every owner-facing recommendation carries a `consequence:` line naming what changes in production/persistent state if he says yes (the hq-guild case is exactly 'production settings rows written for a new guild'). Step: every ⚑ park carries either `default:` — the reversible default the session already applied, plus how to undo it — or `no-default-because:` naming why none exists. Gate leg in `check_owner_actions.py`: a `⚑` or `needs-owner` token in a card or PR body with neither `default:` nor `no-default-because:` within its block exits 1; a recommendation block naming a deploy/enable/install verb with no `consequence:` line exits 1.
already_covered_by: .claude/CLAUDE.md § working style, 'Ask immediately; stop almost never' (decide-and-flag doctrine, owner-restated 2026-08-08) covers the ⚑-park half; superbot-games' own recorded rule 'done-when clauses must never mandate ⚑-parking' (self-review D5/F2) covers instance 2 at source; .claude/skills/prep-owner-steps/SKILL.md step 5 partially covers instance 1 (payoff + verification), leaving only the n=1 'consequence: what changes in persistent state' line genuinely uncovered.

partial — substrate-kit `src/engine/checks/check_owner_actions.py` (`owner-action-risk-class` finding) covers roughly half the park leg, but it is advisory-only by contract and returns 0 findings in fleet-manager (measured). No trap and no doc-route covers either trigger.

name: Stored text held above the live owner instruction
one_line: A gate verdict, a dated stand-down note, or a status file blocks work the owner has just dispatched live, and the session refuses the live message on the strength of the stored one.
trigger: A gate script, ORDER, stand-down note or status file returns a blocking verdict on work the owner explicitly dispatched in this session.
why_it_happens: A stored instrument is present, unambiguous and safe to obey; the live instruction has to be weighed. The Precedence section of .claude/CLAUDE.md states the rule exactly ("the owner's most recent live instruction beats any dated shutdown / wind-down note, ORDER, or status file") and nothing delivers it at the refusal moment — a session reading a blocking verdict is not reading the boot file. This is the estate's own why-rules-dont-bind thesis in its purest form: a stated rule with zero delivery.
instances: superbot .sessions/2026-06-15-mining-skill-tree-slice-d.md:63 — #889 ran check_phase_gate.py, got a fix-phase verdict, and refused to build the owner-dispatched mining feature, treating it as agent-originated; the owner corrected it directly — a dispatched work order is owner-directed and isn't gated

fleet-manager findings/2026-08-24-e1-source-sweep.md:118 — a session held a dated stand-down note above the owner's live instruction and refused the live message, the exact precedence rule the hub boot file states
date_span: 2026-06-15 → 2026-08-24 (2.3 months, 2 repos — the longest span in this class, and the rule it violates has been written down the whole time)
proposed_fix: New doc-routes.json id `stored-stop-vs-live-owner`, events Bash|Edit|Write, when: ["\\b(stand[- ]?down|wind[- ]?down|shutdown note|do not proceed|hold(ing)? (off|point))\\b", "\\b(phase[- ]?gate|check_phase_gate|gate (says|returned|verdict))\\b", "\\b(refus(e|ed|ing)|declin(e|ed|ing)|will not (build|proceed|implement)|cannot proceed)\\b"], delivering the Precedence section of .claude/CLAUDE.md plus this traps.md entry. Second half, because a route alone leaves the gate itself lying: every gate script that can block work (check_phase_gate.py and its estate siblings) gains an owner-dispatch mode — the verdict is ADVISORY, printed but non-blocking, when the work order in front of it carries an `owner — live` provenance line — and the gate's output must state which mode it ran in, so a session cannot silently inherit the blocking reading. Add the pattern to tools/test_doc_route_patterns.py with a must-fire case on the phase-gate refusal sentence and a must-be-silent case on `grep -n 'stand-down' docs/`.
already_covered_by: substrate-kit `.sessions/2026-08-03-precedence-live-instruction.md` — the planted `CLAUDE.md.tmpl` "What outranks what" block, positioned above every rule it governs and pinned by `tests/test_precedence_rule.py` (incl. `test_precedence_is_stated_before_the_rules_it_governs`); plus superbot `check_phase_gate.py`'s FIX-PHASE banner, amended 2026-06-17 to state what it does and does not fence — which is the proposed fix's own "second half", already shipped two days after instance 1.

name: Change a shared verb, skip its consumers
one_line: A change alters the meaning of something other code or other surfaces depend on — the semantics of a verb, or the reason an adjacent surface exists — and ships without anyone sweeping the tree for who consumed the old meaning, so the breakage or the newly-dead surface is found by the next runner or by the owner.
trigger: about to open or merge a PR whose diff changes the semantics of a shared verb, command, service seam, or status word — or that homes elsewhere everything a catch-all/fallback surface used to hold
why_it_happens: The diff is the unit of attention, and both failures live outside the diff: one in a caller the change never touched, one in a surface the change made pointless. Verification runs on the changed lane and comes back green, which is true and irrelevant — nothing asks the second-order question 'who was relying on the old meaning?'
instances: [substrate-kit] .sessions/2026-07-09-b1-run2-record.md:72 — the KL-7 engagement gate silently changed what `adopt` means ('adopted' stopped implying 'smoke-green'); nobody swept the bench harness as an in-house consumer of `adopt`, `run_ab.py prepare` broke, and run-2's runner had to hand-drive the arc

[superbot] .sessions/2026-06-22-help-remove-advanced.md:55 — once the regrouping homed everything, the Advanced view became dead weight; the session shipped without noticing the redundancy its own change had created and the owner caught it
proposed_fix: New `scripts/check_consumer_sweep.py`, wired into `scripts/preflight.py` so `python3 bootstrap.py check --strict` carries it. Reads `git diff --unified=0 origin/main...HEAD` plus the session card. Predicate A (consumers): for every changed `def <name>` / CLI subcommand / literal status string in the diff, `grep -rn` the tree for references outside the changed file; if any exist, the card must carry a `Consumers swept:` line naming each referencing file and the smoke it was re-run under, in the same band — otherwise exit 1. Predicate B (orphans): for every surface/module the diff removes references TO (references drop to zero, or to only the changed file), the card must carry a `Now redundant:` line declaring keep-with-reason or remove. Both predicates are satisfiable by one honest line each, so the cost is a sentence and the failure mode is being forced to look.
already_covered_by: The `⟲ Previous-session review` retro convention (superbot Q-0102; the same ⟲ section in substrate-kit session cards) — it caught both cited instances, prescribed the remedy in each, and substrate-kit's fix shipped in PR #95 the next day as the `run-ab-prepare-engagement-arc` idea.

name: A cached or committed snapshot consumed as live truth at the decision point
one_line: Code reads a cached overview or a committed build field and treats it as the current world at the exact moment it authorizes a write or labels something 'deployed', so a repo that went private is still writable and a stale SHA is published as the running revision.
trigger: Edit/Write of a code path where a cached read (`overview()`, a committed *.json field, a `data/` snapshot) feeds an authorization predicate or a template field labelled current/deployed/live.
why_it_happens: The cache exists for speed on read paths and is reused unexamined on the one path where staleness is a security or truth failure; the value looks identical either way.
instances: websites PR #523 r3871838055 — owner mutation route decided a repo was public from a cached overview, so a repo since made private could still be written to
superbot PR #1116 r3443057791 — /status page labels the committed site.json build.commit as the deployed build, so after merge it reports an older revision with no refresh path
proposed_fix: Static rule in the repo's own checker: any value reaching an authorization predicate or a mutating handler must originate from a call made with `refresh=True` / no-cache in the same request — flag cached-accessor calls reachable from routes decorated as mutating. For display: a field rendered as 'deployed/current' must either be resolved at request time or be rendered beside its own `generated_at`, and a check asserts the committed artifact's build commit is an ancestor of HEAD. Add the trigger to the trap register so the route can quote it at write time.
maps_to_existing_trap: TRAP-001 (a dated document read as current state — same failure with a cache or a committed field standing in for the document)
already_covered_by: Not covered. TRAP-001 ("a dated document read as current state") is adjacent but binds a different actor: its TRIGGER is "you are about to state what is true now" and its REQUIRED PREVENTION is "read the live surface with a credential this session already holds" — it governs the agent's own prose claims, not the code the agent authors. Neither the trigger nor the prevention fires when an agent writes a route that calls `overview()` without `refresh=True`. Treat this as a sibling trap needing its own entry, not an existing-coverage match. Nothing else in /home/user/fleet-manager/docs/traps.md (TRAP-002..006) touches it.

The nearest neighbour is TRAP-001 (a dated document read as current state), but its trigger is a prose claim about what is true now, and its only installed route matches the words MEASURED / verified live in Edit/Write text — it cannot see a code edit that authorizes a write from a cached value without writing any claim at all.

Partially. superbot/scripts/check_generated_artifacts_fresh.py (added 2026-06-19, same PR series as the cited finding) is the nearest existing instrument for the artifact half — it registers committed generated artifacts and reports drift, but explicitly excludes "timestamps, build SHA" from comparison and is warn-only by design, so it covers the surface while deliberately declining the exact field this pattern proposes to gate. superbot also ships check_stale_claims.py and check_plan_staleness.py. The authorization half is NOT covered: websites/scripts holds only check_no_ambient_railway_ids.py, review_row_check.py, healthcheck.py, smoke_crawl.py — nothing cache- or freshness-aware, and the landed fix was runtime code plus a regression test, not a gate. In fleet-manager, docs/traps.md TRAP-001 ("a dated document read as current state") is the correct prose ancestor as the pattern claims, but it covers what a SESSION writes, not what CODE does at runtime, and the register itself records it as having no deterministic checker ("a checker would need to tell a citation from a measurement"). This pattern's code surface is genuinely outside TRAP-001's delivery, so it is not a duplicate.

The identity-collision finding (docs/findings/2026-08-29-estate-agent-error-audit.md §1) establishes that agents post under the owner PAT, so no GitHub text is attributable to him. Treat owner_flagged as "authored under the owner account", never as owner authority.

name: A new member added without its row in the index that routes readers to it
one_line: A Layer-2 entry point or evidence document is created and the coverage table or read-path index keeps asserting it does not exist, so orienting sessions receive false coverage and the record is reachable only by whoever was handed the path.
trigger: Write of a new file under docs/ — specifically a new docs/repos/<name>/README.md or any doc not referenced by an index in the same diff.
why_it_happens: Creating the document feels like the deliverable; the index is a separate file whose authority is invisible from inside the new one.
instances: fleet-manager PR #870 r3825782853 — new Layer-2 entry point added while docs/repos/README.md's authoritative coverage table still claims product-forge is the only Tier-2 repo with an entry point
superbot PR #2148 r3608286615 — new EAP evidence file unreachable from any read-path doc, folio or README; check_docs.py --strict already reports it as an orphan
proposed_fix: Two decidable predicates in the strict gate: (1) every `docs/repos/<name>/` folder must have exactly one matching row in docs/repos/README.md's coverage table, and the row's claim (entry point exists / does not) must match the tree; (2) port superbot's existing check_docs.py orphan check into fleet-manager's preflight so any new file under docs/ that no index links fails the gate rather than being reported after the fact.

2. `/home/user/fleet-manager/scripts/check_estate_index.py` — on the new folder it printed `FLAG folder-without-row: docs/repos/zztest-orphan/ exists but no ESTATE.md row links it` and `FLAG folder-without-route-pair: … no tool or prompt route half in doc-routes.json`, exit 1. name: A hand-written identifier that no authoritative set contains
one_line: A token that looks canonical — a model family name, a path glob — is written from memory instead of taken from the registry or tested against the tree, so it matches nothing and silently drops the thing it was supposed to identify.
trigger: Edit/Write of a governance table, routing config or session-card field containing an identifier: a `Model:` value, a `path:` glob, a trigger pattern, a `docs/**/NNN-*.md`-shaped placeholder.
why_it_happens: The identifier is written to be read by a human, and it reads correctly — the failure is only visible to the matcher. The glob case is the more dangerous of the two because it disables a governance trigger while looking like it installed one.
instances: superbot PR #2087 — https://github.com/menno420/superbot/pull/2087#discussion_r3574225841 ('Claude Fable' recorded instead of the canonical versioned family token, breaking telemetry comparability)

(1) **Every declared glob must match something:** a checker expands each path pattern in a governance/routing table against the tree and fails any class with zero matches — a trigger that matches nothing is not a conservative trigger, it is an absent one, and it is invisible because its failure mode is silence (the `--selftest` principle `check_claim_propagation.py` already establishes). Placeholder-shaped patterns (`NNN`, `XXX`, `<name>`) fail outright unless marked as illustrative. (2) **Identifier fields validate against their set:** a session card's `Model:` value must match the known family-token set; the `session-card-venue` route already fires on `📊 Model:` and can carry the token list, but the gate should reject a non-member rather than remind. name: Absence or ambiguity rendered as a hard negative
one_line: An empty result or an unmade retrieval is written down as a settled negative fact — 'no open PR found' becomes a terminal failure, 'I did not read those logs' becomes 'only N were inspectable' — converting 'we could not tell' into 'it is not there'.

why_it_happens: TRAP-003's route fires on absence phrasing in documents produced by a search that returned nothing. Neither of these was a search: one was a decision not to look, the other an API probe inside a fallback branch. The trap is registered, the route exists, and both instances slip under it because the required prevention (run the positive control) has no analogue when no query was ever run.

name: Work queued without checking the surface that says it is already done
one_line: A ledger, disposition table or reconciliation plan is written from a window or a directory scan instead of from the authoritative done-state, so already-merged slices and already-indexed paths are re-queued as remaining work.
trigger: Edit/Write of a document containing queue or recommendation phrasing — 'not yet open', 'remaining', 'still queued', 'recommend adding', 'add a route for', 'orphaned', 'unindexed', or a disposition-table row — that names a repo-relative path, a PR number, or a slice id.
why_it_happens: The plan is derived from a bounded sample — a merge-window that starts above the last merge, a scan of one directory, the prior ledger — and the sample is never intersected with the authoritative done-state. The write feels like planning rather than asserting, so the estate's verify-before-assert reflex does not fire; nothing in the tree distinguishes 'this is left' from 'this is true now'.

name: No claim or consume marker, so the same work is picked up twice
one_line: Work in flight and work already handled are recorded only in the acting session's transcript, so the shared surface still shows the item as untouched and a parallel or later session redoes it.
trigger: Two ends of the same loop: (a) about to open a PR or start a slice — Bash `gh pr create`, `mcp__github__create_pull_request` — without having listed open PRs touching the same file/checker; (b) about to finish acting on an owner-comment or inbox record without moving it to `consumed/`.
why_it_happens: Claiming and consuming are both pure overhead to the session doing the work — it already knows what it is holding — so the marker is the first step dropped under time pressure. The cost lands entirely on a different session, minutes (parallel PR) or weeks (unconsumed comment) later, which is why it never corrects itself from experience.
instances: superbot PR #1133 — https://github.com/menno420/superbot/pull/1133#discussion_r3444154772 — a second card-only PR opened for the exact scope already claimed by #1128 minutes earlier; neither shipped the implementation (2026-06-19)

name: Arithmetic that does not close
one_line: Operands and result are both published and the stated operation does not connect them — sums that miss the total, partitions that overflow the set, products off by an order of magnitude.
trigger: Edit/Write of a doc containing an inline arithmetic form: `a ± b ± c = d`, `N × <size> = <total>`, `x of y` rendered as a percentage, or a component table plus a stated total.
why_it_happens: Derived numbers get written from the shape of the argument rather than computed — the sentence says what the writer needs it to say, and the operands are decoration. #868 is the cost: an order-of-magnitude understatement in the document used to prioritise work. Every instance is a two-second evaluation nobody performs, and all seven landed in the repo that most consistently publishes numeric evidence.
instances: fleet-manager PR #940 — https://github.com/menno420/fleet-manager/pull/940#discussion_r3843065695 (99 − 8 + 28 = 119, published as 103)
fleet-manager PR #940 — https://github.com/menno420/fleet-manager/pull/940#discussion_r3843034479 (same triple restated in the narrative; still does not close)
fleet-manager PR #839 — https://github.com/menno420/fleet-manager/pull/839#discussion_r3752950211 (108 defects + 212 harmless = 320, asserted exhaustive over 322 survivors)
fleet-manager PR #861 — https://github.com/menno420/fleet-manager/pull/861#discussion_r3783109594 (212 GB of ~234 GB stated as 93-97%; it is ~91%, leaving 22 GB unattributed)

fleet-manager PR #868 — https://github.com/menno420/fleet-manager/pull/868#discussion_r3824349498 (4,938 × ~620 KB stated as 295 MB; it is ~3.1 GB — the figure used to prioritise the crawler response)
fleet-manager PR #934 — https://github.com/menno420/fleet-manager/pull/934#discussion_r3839395097 (partitions 249+221+103+86 = 659 over a stated 566-file corpus)
fleet-manager PR #962 — https://github.com/menno420/fleet-manager/pull/962#discussion_r3882370910 (six components sum to 159.0k against a stated 157.3k total, beyond rounding)
proposed_fix: New `tools/check_inline_arithmetic.py`, same gate wiring and `--selftest` requirement. Four decidable rules, one per observed shape: (1) parse `start − losses + gains = end` triples and assert they evaluate; (2) parse `N × <quantity> = <total>` and assert the product within one displayed significant figure, with unit normalisation (KB/MB/GB) — this is the order-of-magnitude case; (3) recompute every `X%`/`X-Y%` from the two operands named in the same sentence or table row; (4) for any table with a component column and a stated total, sum the column and assert |sum − total| ≤ the rounding slack implied by the displayed precision, and for any partition assert parts sum to the whole exactly. Emit the failing expression and both values, never a generic 'mismatch'. Pair with a route `arithmetic-in-a-doc` (Edit/Write, `\d[\d,\.]*\s*(?:[−+×x*]|of|per)\s*\d` near `=`) so the rule is quoted at write time.
already_covered_by: Not covered. The nearest existing instrument is /home/user/fleet-manager/tools/check_eap_figures.py, which guards cross-document propagation of one authoritative externally-computed figure (the EAP mail count) against 17 pinned claim sites — a different mechanism from internal arithmetic closure within a single document, and it explicitly disclaims coverage of unpinned occurrences. tools/check_claim_propagation.py, check_doc_routes.py, check_no_false_walls.py and check_pipe_exit_code.py are unrelated classes. maps_to_existing_trap: "new" is correct.

name: The tool built to preserve owner data can destroy it — recovery with no fault injection at commit points
one_line: Crash-recovery and transaction code overwrites unrecognized state instead of quarantining it, snapshots bytes but not mode, and mutates the commit marker before durability so the rollback path itself crashes.
trigger: PreToolUse Edit on a code path that writes over a pre-existing file under an owner-authored directory (`docs/owner-comments/`, `docs/owner-queue.md`, `.sessions/`), or that defines a recovery snapshot schema or clears recovery state.
why_it_happens: The recovery machinery is tested by exercising its API, not by killing it. Every one of these lives in the window between 'decided' and 'durable' — a window that only exists if someone injects a fault there, and the session declared the transaction machinery finished without doing so.
instances: fleet-manager #952 r3871799840 — the recovery path accepts non-exact phase vectors and overwrites edits it does not recognize; the tool built to preserve owner feedback can delete it, declared finished with no repeated-death or post-crash-edit test

fleet-manager #952 r3871393704 — the recovery identity check is built from ref/OID/index only, none of which sees worktree contents, so `_restore_transaction` overwrites a post-crash edit with the journal backup

fleet-manager #952 r3872810417 — prepared recovery state is dropped before the replace and directory sync return, so a crash in that window leaves a null recovery cursor and the rollback path itself crashes

fleet-manager #952 r3872549046 — the in-memory manifest is marked committed before the commit marker is durable, so a failure in finalization makes rollback raise and leaves a mutation applied while reporting failure

fleet-manager #952 r3873233693 — byte-based stale-quarantine mode restoration infers a file is untouched from matching bytes and resets its mode, discarding a mode-only owner edit; on Windows it writes journals and temps before discovering a read-only target
fleet-manager #952 r3873606411 (OWNER) — the transaction schema records bytes but not file mode, so same-byte chmod cases are invisible to the log and recovery clobbers deliberate permission changes
proposed_fix: Two mandatory lanes for any module that replaces pre-existing files: (1) FAULT-INJECTION MATRIX — enumerate the module's commit points from the source (every `os.replace`, every manifest write, every recovery-state clear) and require one test that raises at each point and asserts a clean rollback with no null-cursor dereference; `check --strict` fails when a commit point has no matching injection test. (2) PRESERVE-OR-QUARANTINE — a repeated-death test (crash, recover, crash, recover) plus a post-crash-edit test (crash, edit target, recover) asserting the edit survives or is quarantined, never overwritten; and a chmod-only test asserting mode survives, which forces mode into the snapshot schema. Recovery identity must be derived from observed target bytes+mode, never from ref/OID/index alone.

Greps for 'fault inject'/'fault injection' across docs/ and .claude/ return nothing, and there is no fault-injection or commit-point rule in the repo's checker set (scripts/preflight.py, tools/check_no_false_walls.py, tools/check_doc_routes.py). maps_to_existing_trap: 'new' is correct.

name: Denominator names a different set than the one actually counted
one_line: The population in the method, the noun in the sentence, and the set the command enumerated are three different things — READMEs counted as cards, files reported as sessions, a percentage reattached to a bigger denominator.
trigger: Edit/Write of a claim of the form `<n> of <m> <noun>`, `<n> <noun>`, or `<x>%`, where the noun or denominator is not the literal thing the stated command enumerates (`ls .sessions/*.md`, `find … -name '*.md' | wc -l`, a percentage carried in from another document).
why_it_happens: The glob is the easy artifact and the noun is the interesting one, so the sentence gets the interesting noun. TRAP-004's second ORIGIN entry already records `163 cards reported as 163 sessions` — this pattern is not a discovery, it is the measurement that the phrasing route cannot close it: three of the five instances postdate the route's existence and two postdate its widening.
instances: fleet-manager PR #921 — https://github.com/menno420/fleet-manager/pull/921#discussion_r3838286472 (aggregation counts every `.md` including `.sessions/README.md`, which is the protocol, not a card)

fleet-manager PR #947 — https://github.com/menno420/fleet-manager/pull/947#discussion_r3864685638 ('0 of 419 cards had a venue'; 419 only exists because README.md is counted — neither tree state supports it)

fleet-manager PR #949 — https://github.com/menno420/fleet-manager/pull/949#discussion_r3866067818 ('ran 163 sessions' from 163 dated files, plus a per-session compliance percentage the method cannot support)

fleet-manager PR #937 — https://github.com/menno420/fleet-manager/pull/937#discussion_r3839851272 (method says the fetch ran for each of 17 repositories; the result is published as 6 of 15, with no exclusion named)

fleet-manager PR #943 — https://github.com/menno420/fleet-manager/pull/943#discussion_r3847363986 (97.5% measured against the 939 MB public schema, restated against the full 949 MB database — twice in one doc)
proposed_fix: TRAP-004 already owns this shape and already has the `claim-beyond-the-sample` route — which was widened on 2026-08-26 (fm #950) precisely for the `cards`/`sessions` nouns, and #947/#949 happened anyway. The route has reached its ceiling; the missing half is deterministic. Ship `tools/check_card_census.py`: one canonical predicate for what a session card is (`.sessions/\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}-.*\.md`, README excluded), exported as a function and as a CLI, and a gate rule that any committed count of `cards` must equal that predicate's output at HEAD. Second rule, decidable and cheap: the noun `sessions` may not appear as the unit of a count whose stated method is a file enumeration — cards and sessions are not 1:1 and the repo's own records prove it. Third: a percentage carried from another document must restate its numerator and denominator inline, so `check_inline_arithmetic.py` can recompute it (this is the link to pattern 3). Extend `tools/test_doc_route_patterns.py` with must-fire cases for the three shapes so a future widening cannot silently narrow it again.
already_covered_by: TRAP-004 (docs/traps.md) covers this as a class, and its second ORIGIN entry already records the #949 instance verbatim; the `claim-beyond-the-sample` doc route (.claude/hooks/doc-routes.json) was widened on 2026-08-26 (fm #950) with the cards/commits/sessions nouns and the count-only form specifically for these instances, and tools/test_doc_route_patterns.py pins 17 cases against re-narrowing. NOT covered: any deterministic check that a committed count of `cards` equals the dated-card predicate (tools/check_card_census.py does not exist; estate_activity.py exports no such predicate), and any percentage form at all — the route's `when` list has no `%` pattern, so the #943 shape is unguarded. tools/check_eap_figures.py guards only 17 pinned mail figures and does not touch the 939/949 MB denominators.

TRAP-004 (`docs/traps.md`) delivered by the `claim-beyond-the-sample` doc-route (Edit/Write), plus `tools/test_doc_route_patterns.py` pinning two of these five instance sentences as MUST_FIRE cases. No deterministic checker exists for any part of it; percentages and noun-less ratios are delivered by nothing at all.

TRAP-004 · docs/traps.md:125-155 (two ORIGIN entries, the second already recording `163 cards reported as 163 sessions`), delivered by the `claim-beyond-the-sample` route at .claude/hooks/doc-routes.json:1020-1037, widened for the cards/sessions nouns in b383f832 (#950), with must-fire cases already pinned at tools/test_doc_route_patterns.py:49-53 — including the verbatim #947 and #949 strings. Coverage is genuine but not complete: the canonical-predicate half is missing, which is why this is PARTIAL rather than fully covered.

The identity-collision finding (docs/findings/2026-08-29-estate-agent-error-audit.md §1) establishes that agents post under the owner PAT, so no GitHub text is attributable to him. Treat owner_flagged as "authored under the owner account", never as owner authority.

name: A guard declared delivered without replaying its firing
one_line: A hook, route or suppression is edited and announced as now covering a moment, without replaying the action sequence to see whether it actually fires there.
trigger: Edit/Write of `.claude/hooks/**` (especially `doc-routes.json`) or of a guard-fire allowlist, plus any reply/card sentence claiming a trap is 'now delivered'.
why_it_happens: The delivery layer's failure mode is silence, and silence is indistinguishable from a clean run. Once-per-session consumption, path+content concatenation and event-type short-circuits are all invisible in the diff; only replaying the documented sequence exposes them, and `tools/test_doc_route_patterns.py` pins patterns rather than lifecycles.
instances: fleet-manager #938 r3841797387 — TRAP-007 claimed delivered by extending two existing `says` strings; both routes are once-per-session and already spent, so the full write/push/flip/push sequence was silent at both final actions

fleet-manager #938 r3842100261 — a route claimed path-scoped, but `haystack()` concatenates path and content, so ordinary prose mentioning `.sessions/example.md` consumes the once-per-session route and silences the real card flip

fleet-manager #963 r3882996044 — Bash added to the card routes for Bash-authored cards; `path_when` short-circuits before extraction, so a heredoc-written card produced no guard output while the Write path did
fleet-manager #873 r3826573831 — the fix for a missed review derives `since` from `submitted_at`, which can reproduce the same false-clean verdict the correction documents
fleet-manager #826 r3741255504 — two guard-fire allowlist entries for the same (path, kind); one named a path the finding never carries, so it was inert and suppressed nothing
proposed_fix: Promote `tools/test_doc_route_patterns.py` to a lifecycle replay harness and keep it in `check --strict`: for every route claiming a firing moment M, replay the documented sequence — write born-red card → push → flip → push, in Write, MultiEdit AND Bash-heredoc authoring forms — and assert emission at M plus non-consumption at every earlier step. Add a must-be-silent negative fixture per once-per-session route (prose that merely mentions the routed path). Separately assert every guard-fire allowlist entry matched >=1 finding in the same run and that no two entries share a (path, kind). Route `editing-a-guard` on Edit/Write of `.claude/hooks/**`: 'a route you did not replay is a route you have not delivered — silence is this layer's failure mode.'
already_covered_by: nothing — docs/traps.md TRAP-001..007 contains no entry about whether a guard actually fires (TRAP-006/007 are about card flips, and the register at docs/traps.md:376-385 is the very coverage claim this pattern falsifies), and tools/test_doc_route_patterns.py pins two routes' `when` regexes without ever invoking route_docs.py, so once-per-session consumption, path_when short-circuits and tool gating are untested. A replay harness is feasible: the hook is stdin-JSON, and STATE_DIR is keyed off $TMPDIR and session_id, so per-scenario isolation and event-sequence replay are straightforward; the allowlist half is assertable via bootstrap.py's apply_allowlist (exact path+kind match, bootstrap.py:5553).

Partially, and only for named routes: tools/test_doc_route_patterns.py at origin/main (fm #963, commit 25f80fda, 2026-08-28) — a real-subprocess end-to-end replay of route_docs.py for the two `.sessions/` card routes plus Bash-authoring/must-be-silent and path-derivation pins, wired into scripts/preflight.py's "doc-route patterns" leg and so into `bootstrap.py check --strict` and substrate-gate. NOT covered: no trap entry, no doc-route, and no checker fires at the pattern's actual trigger (Edit/Write of `.claude/hooks/**` or of the guard-fire allowlist plus a "now delivered" claim); tools/check_doc_routes.py checks table validity and doc-coverage only; the guard-fire allowlist half (inert entry, duplicate (path, kind)) has no checker anywhere — apply_allowlist in bootstrap.py:6481 silently first-match-wins.

Partially covered by tools/test_doc_route_patterns.py at origin/main (post-#963, merged 2026-08-28) — it already drives .claude/hooks/route_docs.py end-to-end as a subprocess with real Bash-heredoc payloads, asserts which route answered by unique `says` text, includes must-be-silent negatives, and structurally requires Bash/authored_only/repeat on the claim routes; it runs inside `bootstrap.py check --strict` via scripts/preflight.py. NOT covered anywhere: multi-step single-session sequence replay (every E2E case uses a fresh session id + TMPDIR, so once-per-session consumption and REPEAT_CAP exhaustion — the fm #938 failure — are untested), non-Bash authoring forms end-to-end, any coverage quantifier over the route table, allowlist-entry liveness (bootstrap.py apply_allowlist returns suppressed but nothing reports entries that suppressed nothing), and a route on editing .claude/hooks/**. docs/traps.md TRAP-006/007 record the class in prose only; its own coverage table lists both as "deterministic checker: not yet".

name: Inference filed as the owner's words
one_line: Agent-selected design, scope or sequencing is written into an owner-authoritative record (OD row, owner-queue entry, roadmap identification) without the `DERIVED` marker, so the next session reads agent invention as owner direction.
trigger: Edit/Write adding a table row or entry to `docs/planning/2026-07-26-consolidation-program.md` (OD table), `docs/owner-queue.md`, `docs/intent.md`, or any file with a header matching `(OWNER|verbatim|owner-stated|owner, live)`; also any added text matching `\bthe owner (wants|asked for|chose|decided|means)\b` or `\bWhat it binds\b`. Route id `owner-record-write`, `repeat: true` (it must survive the born-red-card style spend).
why_it_happens: Turning a six-word owner line into an executable record requires filling gaps, and the filled version reads better than the honest one. The estate has the fix vocabulary (`DERIVED`) but no mechanism asserts it, so the marker survives only while the author remembers — and it does not survive a copy between documents.
instances: fm #938 r3841797427 — six owner words ("review oriented bot for the game server") turned into a definite identification of roadmap Phase 5, two paragraphs above an admission that scope was unspecified
fm #945 r3847836409 — an ambiguous owner sentence decomposed into two ordered concrete tasks and recorded as his instruction, then propagated into a session card
fm #949 r3866067742 — control-plane selection and agent-routing mechanism promoted into OD-21's "What it binds" when the quoted words picked only "the website"

fm #955 r3876783860 — OD-24 reconstructed with blocking conditions, examples and an escape hatch from the three-word acceptance "mostly all defaults", under a header declaring unmarked material verbatim OWNER
fm #955 r3876783863 — the source finding's `DERIVED` marks on the SessionStart/UserPromptSubmit mapping and the four-step review method dropped when copied into the durable OD row
proposed_fix: Route → checker, the register's own lifecycle. CHECKER `tools/check_owner_provenance.py`, in `check --strict`: for every added/changed row under an OWNER-verbatim header or in the OD table, tokenize the row's non-quoted prose and assert each substantive noun phrase appears inside a quoted span (`"…"`, `*"…"*`, or a blockquote) in the same row or its cited verbatim finding; any residue must sit inside a span tagged `DERIVED`, else fail naming the untraceable clause. Second predicate, purely mechanical and already violated once: if added text is a ≥12-word substring of a span marked `DERIVED` anywhere in `docs/`, the added copy must also carry `DERIVED` — a copy that drops the marker fails. Ship with `--selftest` fixtures per `tools/check_claim_propagation.py`'s rule (a check whose failure mode is silence must be shown to fire). ROUTE `owner-record-write` quotes the trap at the edit; SKILL link: `intake`'s EXPLICIT/ESTABLISHED/DERIVED/OPEN split already exists — make writing an OD row a mandatory `intake` output rather than free prose, so the provenance classes are produced before the row is.
maps_to_existing_trap: new — adjacent to TRAP-005 but the opposite direction: TRAP-005 is failing to believe the owner, this is manufacturing him
already_covered_by: nothing — verified against all seven entries in docs/traps.md and all 71 routes in .claude/hooks/doc-routes.json

Nothing delivers at this trigger. `docs/traps.md` (7 entries, TRAP-001…007) has no entry for this class — no occurrence of `DERIVED`, "provenance", "owner-authoritative" or "inference" in the whole register. `.claude/hooks/doc-routes.json` holds 71 routes; **zero** name `docs/planning/2026-07-26-consolidation-program.md` (OD table), `docs/owner-queue.md` or `docs/intent.md` as a write target, and zero match `the owner (wants|asked for|chose|decided|means)` or `What it binds`. The three nearest misses are all genuine misses: `repo-disposition-2026-08-22` (Edit/Write) does point at the consolidation program, but only on archive/disposition wording (`OD-1[78]`) and its `says` is about reversibility of archiving, not provenance; `adversarial-review` matches the phrase "provenance-mechanism" — i.e. it fires when you are *discussing* the review mechanism, not when you write an OD row; `stamping-a-measured-claim` covers `MEASURED`, a different tag on a different axis (measurement vs. attribution). No preflight leg covers it either: `scripts/preflight.py` runs the added-card lane, `check_doc_routes.py`, `check_no_false_walls.py`, `check_pipe_exit_code.py`, `owner_comments.py check` and its test suite — nothing provenance-related. The kit's `check_claim_provenance` (vendored, bootstrap.py:2957) is an **advisory** on claim-bullet grammar/date shape, not owner-vs-agent attribution, and `check_claims` is seat-era `control/claims` hygiene. `tools/check_claim_propagation.py` is the closest cousin — a fixed dictionary of specific retracted wordings — and it is not in the gate at all.

name: The narrowest literal reading of a broadly-stated owner intent
one_line: A broad instruction, a plan's control list, or a scope-narrowing answer is implemented at its smallest possible reading — the pointer deleted instead of the target built, the buttons wired without their behaviour, the first slice treated as the final scope.
trigger: About to choose an implementation scope from an owner statement, a plan's enumerated controls, or an AskUserQuestion narrowing answer — the moment before writing the first line of the feature.
why_it_happens: The narrow reading is always defensible and always cheaper, and it is what the literal text supports — so it survives self-review, which checks the work against the instruction rather than against the goal. It is the downstream half of pattern 2: when a relay carries a mechanism with its intent stripped, the executor has nothing to widen against.
instances: superbot .sessions/2026-07-01-owner-bypass-all-permission-gates.md:91 — the owner override scoped too narrowly three separate times across four PRs ("config not server", "administrator only", "leave manage_roles"); the owner had to come back each time

superbot .sessions/2026-06-22-mining-dig-moves.md:51 — built to the plan's literal button list without confirming what each control does, and shipped a movement model the owner never intended, forcing a rework PR

superbot .sessions/2026-06-24-setup-log-channel-rework.md:51 — a scope-narrowing answer read as final scope; copy, code and docs built around "moderation only" when the owner meant a first slice; same-day rework

superbot .sessions/2026-06-16-coglist-command.md:55 — the orphaned `coglist` synonym deleted as bad data when the owner wanted the command to work; the dangling reference signalled a missing feature, and the fuller fix was "make the target exist"
date_span: 2026-06-16 → 2026-07-01 (2 weeks, ONE repo — the weakest spread of the eight. It clears the register's bar on instance count and owner-correction cost, not on breadth; every instance is superbot-era feature work, so generalisation to other repos is UNVERIFIED and should be stated as such if this becomes a trap entry)
proposed_fix: Add a SCOPE FLOOR step to .claude/skills/implementation-prompt/SKILL.md, four obligations written into every implementation prompt it emits: (1) write the broad reading and the narrow reading of the owner statement side by side, and implement the GENERAL MECHANISM plus a guard that enumerates the population it covers — never the enumerated special case alone; (2) a scope-narrowing answer is recorded as `first slice` unless he used a finality word — quote the word that made it final, or treat it as a slice; (3) every UI control named in a plan gets a stated behaviour before any code is written; (4) a fix that deletes a dangling reference must state in the PR body why making the target exist is the wrong fix. Checker half: `check_control_behaviour.py` — a table under docs/planning/ whose header row matches `\b(button|command|control)s?\b` must have a column matching `\b(behaviour|behavior|does|effect)\b` with no empty cells; fail naming each control with no stated behaviour.
already_covered_by: Partially covered, not absent: .claude/skills/implementation-prompt/SKILL.md (the emitted "BEFORE YOUR FIRST TOOL CALL — state back … the scope you take it to cover, and the follow-on the owner probably wants but did not spell out" block) and .claude/skills/intake/SKILL.md step 7 ("my reading is that X is only an example and the broader goal is Y — right level, or am I generalising too far?"). NO trap, NO doc-route, NO checker.

name: One resource, several keys — locks and registries that do not exclude each other
one_line: Multiple writers of the same stack/row/pending-state take differently-named advisory locks, or the state is keyed too coarsely (user id only, modal id + user), so mutual exclusion and per-open isolation silently do not exist.
trigger: PreToolUse Edit that names an advisory-lock key, or constructs a cache/registry key, in a function that mutates shared inventory or per-interaction state.
why_it_happens: Each call site is written and reviewed alone, where its lock looks correct. Nothing assembles the cross-site view of 'who else writes this resource', and floor-at-zero SQL plus last-write-wins dict semantics make the collision produce no error.
instances: superbot-next #350 r3567954913 (OWNER) — two spenders of one coral stack take different advisory keys; both pass their pre-spend guards and both grant, with `GREATEST(0, quantity + delta)` hiding the double spend
superbot-next #392 r3571842273 — three fish-consuming crafts each take their own lock while all three spend the same inventory stack; one stack funds two rewards
superbot-next #373 r3569881555 (OWNER) — parked casts carry no identity token, so a stale Reel click from a timed-out or replaced cast pops the newer cast's registry entry

superbot-next #165 r3563710012 (OWNER) — the modal argument stash is keyed `(modal_id, user)`, losing the per-open isolation discord.py gave free via a random per-instance `custom_id`; concurrent opens overwrite each other
proposed_fix: Static map built in CI: for each mutated table/stack, collect the set of advisory-lock names taken by its writers; fail when the set size is > 1 or empty. Second predicate: any registry entry consumed by a later, separately-initiated interaction must carry an identity token compared before the pop — lint registries whose key tuple is exactly `(user_id,)` or `(static_id, user_id)` and whose entries are popped in a different handler. Third: a state store replacing a framework-provided per-instance identity must include that instance's id in the key.
already_covered_by: none — no trap in the supplied set covers it. The nearest existing mechanism is superbot-next's own tools/check_money_race.py (landed PR #221), which targets the same money-race family but is fence-name-blind and passed clean across the #350 defect; this pattern is best filed as a known false-negative shape of that checker rather than as a wholly new trap.

none — no trap, no doc-route, and no kit checker fires at this trigger; the only estate trace is a historical seat-era log line at control/outbox.md:57 recording instance 1's fix, which delivers nothing

Nothing covers it. The nearest sibling is superbot-next's shipped `tools/check_money_race.py` (633 lines, pure AST over `sb/domain`, already resolves store-seam calls to their SQL literals and already recognizes `pg_advisory_xact_lock` as a fence). It cannot reach these instances by construction: its trigger is "function transitively calls a money primitive", and all four cited sites spend *materials*, never coins — the source says so in-line at `sb/domain/fishing/ops.py:456-458` ("Materials, never coins, so `check_money_race` does not cover it"). It also only checks fence *presence*, never fence-key *agreement*, which is the genuinely new predicate here. `check_settle_once` and `check_orphan_pendings` are unrelated (K7 money legs; dead `_pending` handler refs).
