name: An edit silently deletes pre-existing content from a record
one_line: Inserting into a living record replaces rather than precedes — an owner queue item, a section heading and table header, curated prose in a generated file, or a procedure that the next install overwrites.
trigger: PostToolUse Edit/Write on `docs/owner-queue.md`, `docs/traps.md`, `docs/decisions.md`, any `.claude/skills/**` live body, or any generator-owned artifact — structural diff of stable slugs and Markdown block structure.
why_it_happens: An Edit's `old_string`/`new_string` window is judged by what it adds; what it consumes is invisible in the author's mental diff, and nobody renders the file or greps for the slug afterwards. For generated files the loss is designed in rather than typed in — the overwrite happens later, on someone else's run.
instances: fleet-manager #872 r3826348715 — an owner-queue insertion replaced the existing `OQ-VENTURE-STRIPE-KEYS` bullet instead of preceding it; a repo-wide `rg` finds no occurrence of the slug and its instructions are grafted onto an unrelated entry
fleet-manager #938 r3842028927 — inserting TRAP-007 removed the `## Coverage` heading and the table header/separator, so seven coverage rows render as unrelated pipe-delimited paragraphs

fleet-manager #951 r3867018619 — hand-written prose slots specified inside a generator-owned file with no preserved-region marker, so the next `session-close` render silently deletes the curated summaries

fleet-manager #830 r3743082987 — a procedure landed only into the live skill copy, where the documented post-upgrade install loop overwrites it from the staged kit body while the roadmap and ledgers keep claiming it runs
proposed_fix: Three predicates in `check --strict` plus one hook: (a) SLUG CONSERVATION — no `OQ-`/`D-`/`PL-`/`TRAP-`/`OD-` identifier present at merge-base may be absent at HEAD without an explicit `consumed`/`resolved`/`superseded` marker in the same diff; (b) MARKDOWN STRUCTURE — a run of pipe-delimited lines must be preceded by a header+separator pair, and a heading present at merge-base may not vanish in a diff whose net line count grew; (c) GENERATED-FILE OWNERSHIP — a file produced by a generator may not be listed as a hand-edit target unless it declares a preserved-region marker, and live skill bodies must byte-match their staged sources or carry a declared local-amendment marker. Hook: PostToolUse on the four record paths reporting which stable slugs and headings the edit removed.
already_covered_by: none — TRAP-001..007 in docs/traps.md cover unrelated failure classes; no existing trap or checker in tools/ addresses content loss during an edit

`.claude/hooks/change_guard.py` — registered in `.claude/settings.json` on PreToolUse `Write|Edit|MultiEdit` and PostToolUse `Edit|MultiEdit`. Two of its three checks already own two of the four instances: check B `orphan_table_rows` (PreToolUse, any `.md`, evaluated against the RECONSTRUCTED post-edit whole file via `_resulting_content`, not the edit fragment) covers instance 2; check A `kit_skill_amendment` (PreToolUse on `.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md`, cross-checks `.substrate/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` and the ⚠ re-apply table in `docs/SKILLS-local.md`) covers instance 4 and was BUILT FROM it. Adjacent-but-not-covering: check C `unpropagated`, `scripts/check_owner_queue.py` (SLUG DISCIPLINE), kit `gate_carveouts` in `bootstrap.py:20570`.

Partially covered by an existing shipped mechanism, which the pattern's `maps_to_existing_trap: "new"` misses. `/home/user/fleet-manager/.claude/hooks/change_guard.py` (built 2026-08-09) already implements two of the four proposed predicates: check A `kit_skill_amendment` (L61) is predicate (c)'s second half and names fm #830 — instance 4 — as its own origin; check B `orphan_table_rows` (L129) is predicate (b)'s first half and covers instance 2. Both are registered PreToolUse on `Write|Edit|MultiEdit` in `.claude/settings.json` and both fire correctly when tested. Not covered by any existing trap in `docs/traps.md` (TRAP-001..007, none about deletion-on-insert) and not by `tools/check_claim_propagation.py`, which hunts the inverse defect (a corrected claim left standing elsewhere). The uncovered, buildable remainder is predicate (a) slug conservation plus closing change_guard's Bash-edit bypass.

name: Certainty label dropped when a claim moves surfaces
one_line: A hedged, ledger-derived or inferred finding is restated on a card, route README or owner-facing surface as a live measurement, losing exactly the qualifier that made it honest.
trigger: Write/Edit into `.sessions/*.md`, `docs/owner-queue.md`, `docs/repos/*/README.md` or an outbound draft restating a claim sourced from a findings document.
why_it_happens: The certainty legend is applied where the finding is authored; restating it elsewhere is a summarising act, and summaries drop qualifiers by default — particularly on the owner-facing surface, where hedges read as noise.
instances: fleet-manager #940 r3843065573 — ledger-derived Play-track facts presented as live measurement in the durable card, though the audit body split the provenance
fleet-manager #906 r3836366076 — owner-queue approval request presents UNVERIFIED §4 inferences as established vendor safety facts
fleet-manager #887 r3835908782 — a signature-mismatch inference promoted to a measured event ('installs refused, saves lost') in the auto-delivered route README
fleet-manager #922 r3838339142 — a nine-item breakdown attributed to an endpoint that returns only an aggregate count
proposed_fix: Card-lane predicate: every evidence bullet in a `.sessions/*.md` card or an owner-queue entry must carry a legend token (MEASURED / MEASURED-PRIOR / OWNER / REASONED / REVIEWED / UNVERIFIED / NOT-VERIFIABLE) — untagged factual bullets fail. A claim restated on another surface must carry the source document's token, and MEASURED must name the command or probe that produced it (this is TRAP-001's VERIFY rule enforced at restatement, not just at first authorship).
already_covered_by: TRAP-001 ("A dated document read as current state", docs/traps.md:38) — its TRIGGER explicitly names "a document... or a prior session's record" as the basis, its REQUIRED PREVENTION is literally "Never launder a citation into a measurement", and its VERIFY rule demands the call and its output. Coverage is doctrinal but not delivered on these surfaces: TRAP-001's two routes are `stamping-a-measured-claim` (fires on Edit/Write of the MEASURED tag) and `live-state-assertion` (fires on Bash reads of dated records), and neither fires on an UNTAGGED write into a .sessions card, docs/owner-queue.md or a route README — which is where all three genuine instances landed. #922 is additionally covered by TRAP-004 (claim wider than the sample).

TRAP-001 (`docs/traps.md:38-67`) covers the SUBSTANCE, and its route `stamping-a-measured-claim` (`.claude/hooks/doc-routes.json`, tools Edit/Write, when `MEASURED` | `measured (live|2026-)` | `verified live`) fires at the write moment with the exact prevention text ("A citation is not a measurement... is your basis a live surface, or a document that describes one?"). That covers the half where the session actively STAMPS the claim. It does not cover the half this pattern is named for — a qualifier being DROPPED — because a route keyed on the token cannot fire on the token's absence. Nothing else covers it: no route matches `docs/owner-queue.md` or `docs/repos/*/README.md`; `card-status-write` + `session-card-venue` do fire on `.sessions/*.md` writes but say nothing about provenance; no checker in fleet-manager knows the certainty legend at all.

TRAP-001 (VERIFY rule) — correctly identified by the pattern as its parent. The proposed extension "enforced at restatement, not just at first authorship" is the novel half and is the half that is not decidable. Partially overlapping existing mechanism: tools/check_claim_propagation.py (curated literal register for withdrawn claims that still stand on another surface) covers the same cross-surface residue problem retroactively, per-incident. #922 is not covered by this pattern and should be reassigned to an evidence-scope-overreach pattern (a cited probe not supporting the claim's granularity).
owner_flagged_premise: VOID — the lane that set this assumed every menno420-authored review comment was the owner speaking. The identity-collision finding (docs/findings/2026-08-29-estate-agent-error-audit.md §1) establishes that agents post under the owner PAT, so no GitHub text is attributable to him. Treat owner_flagged as "authored under the owner account", never as owner authority.

name: Impossible dataset committed and then cited as measurement
one_line: A generated fixture that contradicts itself — landmarks before their gate, unrecovered rows followed by recovery, silently dropped censored rows, fixtures the tree can no longer reproduce — is used as the evidence for a verdict in the same PR.
trigger: Commit of a generated dataset/fixture in a PR whose documents cite it as measurement, or a doc naming a regeneration command for a committed fixture.
why_it_happens: A dataset the session generated feels like a measurement rather than an artifact requiring verification, and the statistic is read off it without ever querying the rows for internal contradiction.
instances: couch-legend #7 r3833435992 — adopted-* dataset records stage-gated first-buys preceding their own gate stage, cited as measurement
couch-legend #7 r3833171776 — `pnpm sim tuned/baseline` documented as the regeneration path for fixtures the tree can no longer reproduce
couch-legend #2 r3826578025 — headline ~91% unrecovered computed from rows the committed data itself contradicts
couch-legend #2 r3826693456 — 'every started rebuild is accounted' while right-censored rows are silently dropped
proposed_fix: Internal-consistency pin tests over every committed fixture, run in CI: every stage-gated first-buy ≥ its gate's stage crossing; no row flagged `unrecovered` followed by a peak ≥ its target; `rows_in == rows_bucketed + rows_explicitly_censored`. Plus a reproducibility job that runs each committed fixture's documented regeneration command and diffs — mismatch fails, which also catches the 'documented command cannot rebuild this file' case.
already_covered_by: none identified — no existing trap covers it. It sits adjacent to the estate's prose doctrine ("verify before fold", "do not write about a file you have not opened", the MEASURED/REASONED certainty legend in docs/findings/2026-08-05-foundation-continuation.md), but all of those govern claims about DOCUMENTS and CAPABILITIES; none of them reaches a committed data artifact the session generated itself, and none is mechanically enforced over fixtures. maps_to_existing_trap "new" is correct.

Nothing in the estate fires at this trigger. Closest existing instruments, all measured 2026-08-29 and all missing it: (1) `docs/traps.md` TRAP-001 (dated doc read as current state) — about a document vs a live surface, not a dataset contradicting its own rows; TRAP-004 (claim wider than its sample) — about population coverage, not internal contradiction; neither names a fixture. (2) `.claude/hooks/doc-routes.json` — 71 routes, zero matching `fixture|dataset|regen|reproduc|snapshot|golden|csv|jsonl|seed` (grep returned only couch-legend prose mentions). `stamping-a-measured-claim` needs the literal `MEASURED` / `measured 2026-` / `verified live` token in an Edit/Write payload and then delivers TRAP-001's live-surface advice; `claim-beyond-the-sample` needs a ratio/`all N`/count with a noun from a fixed list (repos|files|cards|commits|sessions|…), so `~91% unrecovered`, `rows`, `rebuilds`, `first-buys` match nothing. (3) Delivery is moot for the instances anyway: `GET /repos/menno420/couch-legend/contents/.claude/hooks/doc-routes.json` → 404, and root is fixed at boot, so a couch-legend session loads zero hub routes. (4) Kit checkers — `scripts/check_bench_integrity.py` is kit-repo-only ("never ships in dist"), gates `bench/rubric|tasks|seeds` by label plus append-only `bench/results/`, and never reads a file's contents; `check_staged_regen.py` is about unfilled `${slot}` placeholders in staged `.substrate/` artifacts, not data regeneration; `check_claim_provenance.py` is advisory/warn-only and states outright that it "never inspects individual numbers" — a doc citing a self-contradicting fixture passes it by containing the word `provenance`. (5) fleet-manager's `tools/check_eap_figures.py` / `check_claim_propagation.py` pin specific prose figures against one generator (17 EAP mail locations) — not generalizable and not wired to fixtures. Partial, repo-local cover exists inside couch-legend itself and is the only real overlap: `tests/sim.test.ts:97-108` ("impact rows carry the purchase stage (Codex R3)") asserts every stage-gated impact's recorded stage ≥ its gate index, and `:173-188` ("rebuild accounting (Codex CL#2 R2: the horizon edge)") asserts every prestige row resolves to exactly one of completed/unrecovered/censored — i.e. two of the pattern's four proposed invariants, landed as remediation of these findings and running in the required `ci` workflow via `pnpm check`.

Partially covered in-repo, not at estate level: couch-legend tests/sim.test.ts already pins two of the three proposed invariants (the stage-gated first-buy ordering, and a stronger exactly-one-of completed/unrecovered/censored trichotomy that subsumes the row-conservation check), both landed 2026-08-21 in the cited PRs. No estate-level checker covers this — fleet-manager's scripts/preflight.py runs only check_doc_routes.py, check_no_false_walls.py and check_pipe_exit_code.py; tools/check_eap_figures.py and tools/check_claim_propagation.py are the nearest shape precedent (hand-pinned claim registries over prose figures) but are wired into no workflow and cover documents, not datasets.

The identity-collision finding (docs/findings/2026-08-29-estate-agent-error-audit.md §1) establishes that agents post under the owner PAT, so no GitHub text is attributable to him. Treat owner_flagged as "authored under the owner account", never as owner authority.

name: The qualifier that does not survive the copy
one_line: A claim is stated correctly and scoped in its source document, then copied into an index, a ledger row, a live skill or an outbound message with the scope qualifier and the honest null stripped off.
trigger: PreToolUse Edit/Write on a summary or outbound surface — docs/**/README.md, docs/current-state.md, the program's NOW pointer, docs/planning/README.md, outbox/**, .claude/skills/** — whose added text contains a number or superlative that also appears in another file changed in the same diff.
why_it_happens: Index and outbound surfaces reward brevity, and the qualifier is always the clause that looks droppable — 'fleet-manager only', 'self-attested', 'per Gmail', 'agent-selected fragments'. The copy is then the surface most readers meet first, so the narrow claim survives only where nobody looks. Twice here the stripped version went to an external recipient, including to the party being described.
instances: fleet-manager #830 r3743082986 — the live skill still advertises ten 'real owner messages' after the same change established they are agent-selected fragments

fleet-manager #943 r3846776986 — the source's honest null (instructed, self-attested containment; readable checkout; two same-family scorers) dropped, containment stated to an outside recipient as a guarantee
fleet-manager #943 r3847085837 — a Gmail search result copied out as 'never got an answer', against the source record's own null about non-mail surfaces
fleet-manager #949 r3866067778 — the sample qualifier dropped when summarising into docs/planning/README.md, so a fleet-manager-only measurement reads as a 14-repository result
proposed_fix: Extend the existing `tools/check_claim_propagation.py` — which today only sweeps for retracted wordings — with a qualifier-propagation lane. Predicate: for each number or superlative appearing in both a source doc and an index/outbound doc changed in the same diff, collect the qualifier tokens attached in the source (`only|sample|fleet-manager-only|self-attested|instructed|per <surface>|N of M|agent-selected`) and fail when none appears within the copy's sentence; print both sentences side by side. Second predicate: any claim sourced from a document containing an 'honest nulls' section must carry or cite that section — this is decidable from the source path alone and would have caught both #943 outbound cases. Chain link in session-close: no outbound or index write lands before its claim is diffed against the source sentence it came from.
maps_to_existing_trap: new — closest to TRAP-004 in effect, but the defect is transport between surfaces, not sampling; the tool that would host it already exists

Not covered: the qualifier/honest-null transport predicate for #943-style outbound copies.

Instance #943's "never got an answer" wording is already pinned as a retracted claim in tools/check_claim_propagation.py (post-hoc sweep, not a trigger-moment guard). The two #943 outbound instances are otherwise uncovered: no route matches, and mcp__Gmail__* matches no hook matcher in .claude/settings.json.

name: Instrument slack laundered into an exact number
one_line: The published figure is exact, and the measurement behind it was tolerant, threshold-relaxed, off-by-one, or never preserved — so the exactness is a property of the sentence, not the method.
trigger: Edit/Write of a headline metric (`N/N`, `all N`, `zero unverified`, `six imprecisions`) in the same session as a scoring script, or a scoring script whose comparison uses a tolerance, a `>=` on a derived cutoff, or a threshold it does not apply to every row.
why_it_happens: The tolerance is added for a good reason (noisy line numbers, moving files) and then does not travel with the number — the script's caveat lives in code, the figure lives in prose, and the prose is what gets read and cited. #851 is the sharp case: the tolerance was chosen to make the scorer usable and then the scorer's output was published as the exact defect count it had been built to blur.
instances: fleet-manager PR #851 — https://github.com/menno420/fleet-manager/pull/851#discussion_r3770623453 (±3-line citation tolerance turns wrong ranges into PASS; the resulting six-defect tally is published as exact and hides at least five misattributions)

fleet-manager PR #840 — https://github.com/menno420/fleet-manager/pull/840#discussion_r3753508766 ('833 paths reproduced, zero unverified' includes a row that failed the document's own two-of-three rule)

fleet-manager PR #947 — https://github.com/menno420/fleet-manager/pull/947#discussion_r3864685718 (`--days 7` window spans parts of eight UTC dates, so generated counts do not match the advertised period)

fleet-manager PR #959 — https://github.com/menno420/fleet-manager/pull/959#discussion_r3879998021 (59/59 verbatim-verification headline with no committed quote ledger; the file holds 36 quoted spans in total)
proposed_fix: A convention with two enforceable clauses, plus the checker that reads them. (1) **Disclosed slack:** any script that computes a published metric must print its tolerance/threshold/window beside the number, and the doc must carry it (`6 attribution defects (±3-line tolerance — see caveat)`). `tools/check_metric_provenance.py` fails a headline metric whose generating script contains a nonzero comparison tolerance, a `>=` against a derived cutoff, or a per-row threshold, unless the same doc names it within the metric's paragraph. (2) **N/N needs N rows:** an `N/N`, `all N verified` or `zero unverified` claim must be accompanied by a committed evidence artifact with exactly N rows, and the checker counts them — this alone closes #959 and #840. (3) Window boundaries get a unit test against the advertised label (`--days 7` must cover exactly 7 UTC dates), the cheapest of the four and the one that seeds every future figure the tool emits.
already_covered_by: Nothing existing covers it. `tools/check_eap_figures.py` and `tools/check_claim_propagation.py` are the adjacent family (figure-vs-source guards) but both target staleness/residue, not measurement slack; none of the four instances is reachable by either. The `docs/findings/2026-08-05-foundation-continuation.md` certainty legend (MEASURED/REASONED/...) labels a claim's evidence class but says nothing about disclosing a tolerance beside a number, so a ±3-tolerated count can be stamped MEASURED today and be exactly as misleading.

Nothing fires at either trigger moment. Nearest neighbours, all checked and all missing it: docs/traps.md TRAP-004 + route `claim-beyond-the-sample` (population-width, not measurement-slack); kit `check_claim_provenance` (PL-014, advisory-only, scoped to measurements|benchmarks|instrumentation dirs — fleet-manager has none); /home/user/fleet-manager/tools/check_eap_figures.py (stale-figure pinning for one document family, hand-run, not in the gate).

nothing — measured: TRAP-004's `claim-beyond-the-sample` route is silent on all four instance sentences (ran its six patterns from `.claude/hooks/doc-routes.json` against them; 0 fire, because its noun allowlist has no `quotes`/`paths`/`imprecisions`). No metric-provenance checker exists; `tools/check_eap_figures.py` guards cross-document figure *consistency* and `tools/check_claim_propagation.py` guards *retracted wordings*, neither the slack predicate.

one_line: A derived, aggregated, source-read or owner-reported figure is given the certainty label reserved for a command with a real exit code, and then propagates.
trigger: Edit/Write of content matching `MEASURED` / `verified live` in `docs/**` or `.sessions/**` (route `stamping-a-measured-claim` already fires here — it has no checker behind it).
why_it_happens: The legend's labels are applied at write time by self-assessment, and the strongest available label is the one that makes the sentence useful downstream. fleet-manager #962 r3882370921 — owner-reported, admittedly unreproducible console readings stamped MEASURED and propagated into CORE summaries
fleet-manager #949 r3866067758 — a live credential's permission scope inferred from reading `writeback.py`, recorded as established state, and turned into an owner instruction to replace the token

name: Mutation before its own precondition
one_line: A persisting or irreversible step ran ahead of the validation, preflight or prerequisite artifact that governs it — the check existed, it just was not on the path that writes.
trigger: Edit/Write of a tool under tools/*.py whose diff adds a filesystem- or git-mutating call (mkdir, makedirs, open(...,'w'), shutil.move, git add/commit), and Bash invocation of any regenerate/refresh command inside a session whose own card is not yet committed.
why_it_happens: The validation is written as a separate, correct function and the session assumes writing it is the same as placing it on the write path. Nothing in the local gate inspects call order, so the defect is only visible to a reviewer who traces the path by hand — which is exactly what @codex did in all four cases.
instances: fleet-manager PR #952 r3871799975 — staged candidate reached Git mutation without ESTATE/schema/lifecycle/projection validation
fleet-manager PR #952 r3873233907 — consume created consumed/ and a journal before preflighting record, destination and both indexes (OWNER-flagged)
fleet-manager PR #962 r3882130692 — estate_activity refresh regenerated the index at 15:52Z, before its own card committed at 15:53Z
fleet-manager PR #882 r3833853046 — roadmap put the Games ownership contract in Phase 5 while Phases 1-3 already consumed it

Add doc-route id `mutation-before-preflight` firing on Edit/Write of tools/*.py so the trap text is delivered at the write, not the review.

name: Rule landed at one site while the delivered instructions still say the opposite
one_line: A new prohibition, decision or correction is recorded in a ledger, hook or rendered document, and the surfaces that actually reach a working session — startup prompts, the canonical skill, the template slot that regenerates the doc — keep telling agents to do the old thing.
trigger: Edit/Write of docs/decisions.md, an OD row, or any generated/rendered document — fire on the write, quoting the propagation requirement and naming the generating slot for that file.
why_it_happens: Writing the decision feels like landing the rule, and the ledger is the site the session is already editing. The surfaces that would contradict it are in other repos, other directories, or generated at render time — none of them visible in the diff the session is looking at.
instances: fleet-manager PR #834 r3743846565 — delete_trigger prohibition recorded in decisions and the hook while init-prompt-universal.md:22 and the fleet-manager reboot prompt still order the call, in repos that never load the hook
fleet-manager PR #858 r3782659049 — D-0017 recorded in the ledger while the mandatory session-close skill and the owner-queue exemption instruct the opposite

fleet-manager PR #849 r3760744374 — three rendered docs corrected while .substrate/state.json still supplies new_area_ownership to ownership.md.tmpl, so the next render reintroduces every corrected claim
fleet-manager PR #122 r3566962910 — source digest edited without regenerating the registry copy, leaving seat_digest_sync.py --check reporting DRIFT
proposed_fix: Chain: decision-capture → a propagation step → tools/check_claim_propagation.py (already exists — extend it). The decision-capture skill gains a mandatory closing step 'name every delivered surface that states the old rule' with a required grep over docs/prompts/, .claude/skills/, and the estate's init prompts for the literal call or phrase the decision prohibits. The checker adds two predicates: (1) a diff adding a prohibition decision must also touch every file matching that literal string; (2) a diff editing a generated file must also touch its generating slot (state.json key or template), and any sync --check the repo ships must be run in the gate. This is the estate's own thesis — records may grow, instructions may not — failing on itself four times.

name: The file's own stated rule broken at the moment of writing it
one_line: A session writes into a ledger or index whose header states how entries must be made — append, don't edit; qualify IDs by repo; this lane excludes commits — and the write violates that rule, sometimes in the file's very first operational entry.
trigger: Edit/Write of docs/CAPABILITIES.md, docs/q-index.md consumers, docs/activity/ logs and any file whose first 40 lines contain a rule sentence — extract the in-file contract and check the diff against it before the write lands.
why_it_happens: Editing the nearest matching row is the cheapest correct-looking action, and the rule that forbids it sits in a header the session scrolled past on the way to the row. In the #947 case the session had authored the rule minutes earlier — proof that stating it, even in your own words, does not deliver it.
instances: fleet-manager PR #926 r3838465714 — 2026-08-23 confirmation folded into an append-log bullet whose LAST-VERIFIED stays 2026-08-07
fleet-manager PR #939 r3842352834 — 2026-08-24 measurements folded into the 2026-08-23 entry, against the ledger's explicit append-not-edit rule at its own lines 102-105
fleet-manager PR #947 r3864685681 — the first entry in a new log records a creator-kit commit, which the header it had just written says belongs in the repository lane
fleet-manager PR #959 r3879998012 — cross-repository findings cite bare Q-NNNN despite q-index.md:25-33 requiring superbot:Q-NNNN in cross-repo documents (playbook R28)
proposed_fix: Route plus checker. Route id `in-file-contract` on Edit/Write of the append-only ledgers (docs/CAPABILITIES.md, docs/activity/*.md, docs/traps.md), delivering the file's own rule lines verbatim at the write. Checker predicates, all decidable: (1) any diff to docs/CAPABILITIES.md that modifies an existing dated row without adding a new row with its own LAST-VERIFIED fails; (2) a new date appearing in a row whose LAST-VERIFIED is older fails; (3) in any document naming two or more repositories, a bare Q-NNNN / D-NNNN / PL-NNN citation fails (R28 is live and estate-general, currently enforced by nothing); (4) an entry in an off-repo lane log naming a commit SHA fails.

name: The unsafe review gate is authored, not committed
one_line: In all four incidents the agent did not mishandle a review — it wrote down a procedure that licenses future sessions to mishandle every review, and no checker looks at authored procedures.
trigger: Edit/Write/MultiEdit on `.claude/skills/**/SKILL.md`, `docs/CAPABILITIES.md`, `docs/traps.md`, `docs/planning/**`, `scripts/**`, `.github/workflows/**` where the added text matches review/merge-eligibility vocabulary (`review`, `merge`, `flip .* complete`, `@codex`, `verdict`, `clearance`).
why_it_happens: Every existing guard in this estate fires on the ACT — the push, the flip, the poll. None fires on the sentence that will cause a hundred future acts. So a defective procedure passes every hook, and its blast radius is every session that later follows it: #362 put it in gate code, #828 in the session-close sequence, #925 in the capabilities ledger, #951 in a rollout plan. All four were caught by `@codex` at review time and by nothing else, which is the estate's own measured thesis (116 committed statements catching 0 of 16 incidents) reproduced inside the review machinery itself. It is also self-eating: the artifact that carries the trap register is the artifact these defects get written into.

name: Check-then-act across an `await` — the guard fences nothing

name: Destructive filesystem operation without an lstat/containment guard
one_line: Path resolution and recursive deletes trust `resolve()` or the final path component, so an ancestor symlink or a planted reparse point lets the tool read, write and rmtree outside the repository.
trigger: PreToolUse Edit adding `shutil.rmtree`/recursive delete, or a path-resolution helper, in a tool under `tools/` that mutates repo files.
why_it_happens: `Path.resolve()` reads as a containment primitive but resolves symlinks on both sides of the comparison, so it confirms the escape rather than blocking it. The tool is tested on a normal checkout where no ancestor is a link.
instances: fleet-manager #952 r3873234302 (OWNER) — the owner-comments store resolves paths without lstat-checking its ancestors; a symlinked `docs/` or `docs/owner-comments/` lets reads and writes escape the repo, and parent aliases produce two lock/journal identities

fleet-manager #952 r3873028184 — the containment test resolves both base and target, so a symlinked `docs` makes both land in the same external directory and `reindex`/`consume` replace files outside the repository

fleet-manager #952 r3873606591 (OWNER) — transaction-root cleanup enumerates and rmtrees `txn-*`, `quarantine-*`, `.initializing-*` children without checking they are real directories; a reparse point there is traversed and its external target deleted
proposed_fix: Lint predicate in `check --strict`: (a) flag every `rmtree`/recursive-delete call not immediately preceded, in the same function, by an `lstat` real-directory guard on the target; (b) flag containment comparisons built from `resolve()` on both operands without a per-ancestor `lstat` walk. Mandatory containment test for any tool that mutates repo paths: replace each ancestor (`<store root>`, `docs/`, `docs/owner-comments/`) in turn with a symlink to an external directory and assert no external read or write occurs and the tool refuses before creating any journal, temp or lock artifact.

name: Paired state surfaces updated asymmetrically in the same PR
one_line: The program ledger says a step shipped while the session card is still in-progress, or the card records the final tally while docs/current-state.md keeps the round-one numbers — one PR publishing two contradictory histories of itself.

name: Local wall-clock stamped with a UTC Z
one_line: A commit or build timestamp is formatted with a literal `Z` while carrying a local offset, publishing an instant that is hours wrong and sometimes in the future relative to the same artifact's generation time.
trigger: Edit/Write of exporter/generator code that formats a git commit time (`%cd`, `%ci`, `git show` date) or a `datetime.now()` into a field whose value ends in `Z`.
why_it_happens: The reviewer's fix was applied to the emitted artifact, not to the generator, so the next regeneration reproduced it verbatim — twice. It is the purest example in the class of a correction that never reached the mechanism, and the fix is four lines of test.
instances: superbot PR #1049 — https://github.com/menno420/superbot/pull/1049#discussion_r3437198398 (commit `Thu Jun 18 17:26:42 2026 +0200` written as `17:26:42Z`)
superbot PR #1055 — https://github.com/menno420/superbot/pull/1055#discussion_r3439237956 (identical defect regenerated one PR later — `23:29:09+0200` published as `23:29:09Z`)
superbot PR #1127 — https://github.com/menno420/superbot/pull/1127#discussion_r3444018189 (third occurrence: build time stamped two hours ahead of the 18:06Z generation time)
proposed_fix: One assertion in the exporter's own test suite, which is where the previous two corrections failed to land: every exported field whose value ends in `Z` must have been produced by a UTC-normalising call (`git log --format=%cI` piped through `datetime.fromisoformat(...).astimezone(timezone.utc)`, or `%cd --date=iso-strict-local` with `TZ=UTC`), and `meta.build.committed_at <= meta.generated_at` must hold in every committed artifact. Add a static rule too: `strftime` with a literal `Z` in the format string is banned — use `isoformat().replace('+00:00','Z')` after an explicit `astimezone(utc)`. The chain link matters as much as the checker: a review finding on PR N that does not produce a test before PR N+1 regenerates the artifact is how this happened three times in 24 hours — make 'the correction reached the generator, and a test pins it' a required line in the session card that closes a review round.

The adjacent artifact checker `scripts/check_dashboard_data.py` in menno420/superbot explicitly excludes this field by design ("deliberately ignores the volatile churn (timestamps, build SHA, ...)"), which is why three review findings never reached a gate. `maps_to_existing_trap: "new"` is correct.

name: One stale figure copied into every delivery surface
one_line: A number is hand-carried into routes, front-door docs and living state alongside its source, so a single stale value becomes three or twenty-four wrong statements — and readers meet the wrong one first.
trigger: Edit/Write that writes the same numeral into a doc-route summary, `docs/current-state.md`, a program ledger row, or a generated header, when a generator or canonical document already computes it.
why_it_happens: The estate's delivery model deliberately duplicates facts into the surfaces sessions actually hit (routes, current-state, ledger rows), and duplication without a binding is how one measurement becomes several claims with independent decay. name: A guard built on a premise that drifts out from under it
one_line: The verification code the session authored was itself the defect — a test comparing fixed fixture stamps against the real wall clock, a membership guard enumerating its own module list by hand where a glob existed — so the guard passed at 08:31 and failed at 09:05, or drifted out of coverage in the exact code meant to catch drift.
trigger: Writing a test or guard that hard-codes a timestamp, or enumerates modules/paths by hand where the directory could be globbed.
why_it_happens: A guard is written to make one known case red, and the premise that makes it work today (now() is close to the fixture stamp; these are the modules that exist) is invisible in the code. Guards are also the code least likely to be re-read.

websites · .sessions/2026-07-11-nav-scan-glob.md:59 — "the SECOND self-referential drift the chain found in a guard (first: the overflow guard's markup/tuple duplication that #122 fixed; now the membership guard's own module list)"; the card's own 💡 proposes the sweep as a rung-5 grep

(a) Wall-clock leg: a test containing an ISO-8601 literal (`\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}T`) that calls a function whose body reads `datetime.now|datetime.utcnow|time.time` and whose signature has no `now=` parameter ⇒ exit 1, "inject now= or freeze the clock; this test's verdict depends on when it runs". (b) Hand-list leg: a module-level list/tuple literal of ≥3 string entries that are all existing paths or module names under one directory, where a glob of that directory returns a strict superset ⇒ exit 1, naming the missing members. name: The review fires on the born-red opening commit, so its output becomes noise
one_line: Automated review triggers at PR open — the card-first commit, before the code lands — so it reliably flags 'implementation missing', sessions learn to discard it, and the real findings inside get discarded too.
trigger: after the final push to a PR that triggers an automated review, before merge — the moment the head SHA stops moving
why_it_happens: Born-red discipline (card first, code second) and review-on-open are each individually correct and jointly produce a review of an empty diff. The resulting noise is not merely wasted — it trains the habit that a Codex comment is probably wrong, which is the disposition failure in P5 and the merge-anyway behaviour in P1. Nobody built the fix because the noise was individually cheap to ignore and the cost only appears in aggregate, in the reviews nobody read.
instances: superbot · .sessions/2026-06-17-settle-decisions-codex.md:16 — reviews on #1023/#1024/#1027 fired on the born-red open commit and flagged 'implementation missing / flip the card / script doesn't exist', all is_outdated noise; meanwhile 2 of 4 findings on #1028 were real drift and sat unread until this session went looking, prompted by the owner

[superbot] .sessions/2026-06-19-codex-final-head-review.md:49 — the Codex final-head gap was a known open item since Q-0171/Q-0174 plus the #1031 idea, yet 'sat unbuilt across many sessions while everyone treated its born-red false positives as noise to ignore'; every PR burned a wasted review

name: A reconciliation ledger that contradicts git truth
one_line: A pass that exists to reconcile merged history against the record omits a PR that merged in its own range, or lists already-merged PRs as awaiting owner review — while the same pass states there are zero open PRs.

name: Stated age or staleness not derived from the dates cited
one_line: A document asserts how old something is — 'over three weeks stale', 'about two years old' — and the dates it prints on the same page do not support it.
trigger: Edit/Write of a doc containing an age or staleness phrase (`\b(over|about|roughly|almost)?\s*\d+\s*(days?|weeks?|months?|years?)\s*(old|stale|ago)\b`, `older than`) in a file that also contains ISO dates or date-stamped filenames.
why_it_happens: Age is stated for rhetorical weight — 'stale', 'deep history' — and the adjective is chosen before the subtraction is done, so the number rounds toward whatever the argument needs. Both instances used the inflated age as the load-bearing part of a conclusion.
instances: fleet-manager PR #937 — https://github.com/menno420/fleet-manager/pull/937#discussion_r3839851271 ('four repositories >3 weeks stale' when curious-research's 2026-08-07 commit was 16 days old on the audit date)

proposed_fix: A small, fully decidable rule inside `tools/check_inline_arithmetic.py` (pattern 3's checker) rather than a file of its own: for every age/staleness phrase, resolve the reference instant (the doc's own date header, or `--as-of`), resolve the subject date from the nearest ISO date or `\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}-` filename cited in the same sentence or table row, and assert the stated interval matches within one unit of the displayed granularity. name: Two numbers from different methods compared as one measurement
one_line: Figures gathered by different instruments, windows or start events are placed in one table or one ratio and reasoned over as if commensurable — sometimes against a correction already recorded in the cited document.

why_it_happens: Two numbers with the same unit look comparable, and the interval definition lives in the session that produced each one rather than beside the number. name: Display rounding that erases the change it is meant to show
one_line: Two values are rounded independently and then compared as rendered strings, so a real difference renders as 'unchanged' and the UI tells the user nothing happened.
trigger: Edit/Write of formatter or preview code that applies a fixed precision (`toFixed`, `%.1f`, `round(x,1)`) to both sides of a before/after or delta display.
why_it_happens: Rounding is chosen for the value's typical magnitude, not for its typical delta; per-level upgrade steps are an order of magnitude smaller than the numbers they modify. Both sites are in one PR, so this is the least-established pattern here — it earns a place because the failure is a false negative shown to a player, and the property test costs almost nothing.
instances: couch-legend PR #17 — https://github.com/menno420/couch-legend/pull/17#discussion_r3838183896 (non-combined hit effects render a canonical percentage; small real increases round to an unchanged before/after string)
couch-legend PR #17 — https://github.com/menno420/couch-legend/pull/17#discussion_r3838176547 (a real `1.06 → 1.12` upgrade renders as `High/hit 1.1 → 1.1` in a preview that promises exact impact)
proposed_fix: A property test in the repo's suite, run in its gate: for every listed effect and every adjacent upgrade level, if `before != after` then `render(before) != render(after)`, or an explicit small-change path must be taken (`+0.06`, `1.06 → 1.12`, or a `<0.1` badge). Generate the cases from the effect table rather than hand-listing them, so a new effect type inherits the guarantee. Second, weaker rule for review: a feature whose copy promises 'exact impact' may not use a fixed display precision on a value whose step size is smaller than that precision — decidable if the step sizes are in data.

The proposed fix is, however, already partially implemented in the repo itself: tests/purchase-impact.test.ts:200-201 at head 5a9a185 pins `High/hit +5.7%` and asserts absence of `High/hit 1.1 → 1.1`, which is the hand-listed version of the proposed property test. name: Removed the artifact, left the instruction that recreates it
one_line: Something is retired or prohibited by deleting its runtime half, while binding instruction text elsewhere in the tree still orders the exact behaviour just removed.
trigger: A PR, card or commit message using retire/remove/deprecate/prohibit plus a named artifact or command — before the turn ends, grep every instruction-bearing file for that name.
why_it_happens: Retirement is modelled as deletion of the thing, and the thing is the schedule or the code — while in this estate the operative half is usually an imperative sentence in a prompt, playbook or boot file that no build step links to the artifact. Adding a contradicting warning above the old sentence feels like a fix and leaves the concrete command a reader will actually follow.
instances: fleet-manager #812 — discussion_r3736227547 (roster retired by deleting the Actions schedules; playbook rule and coordinator prompt still order regeneration at every wake)

name: Happy path shipped, abuse path unwritten
one_line: A user-facing flow is declared done once the intended click sequence works, with the client-controlled or repeated-click path left unhandled.
trigger: Adding a handler that reads client-supplied component values as a lookup key, or that grants a reward/spends a cost against a reusable session component id.
why_it_happens: The rendered UI is treated as the boundary — what the menu does not show, the agent reasons, the user cannot send — and the flow is verified by walking it as an honest player. Nothing in the loop asks what a dishonest one sends, so the completion criterion is 'the intended path works' rather than 'no other path works'.
instances: superbot-next #112 — discussion_r3561415149 (any member can submit admin/moderation to help_categories:select and open staff-only rosters omitted from their rendered menu)
superbot-next #236 — discussion_r3565713137 (the 'Waiting for a bite' button stays routable after the first catch; unlimited catches/items/XP for one energy spend)
proposed_fix: A required abuse-line step in `review`/pre-PR for any diff adding an interaction handler: write, in the card, what an adversarial client sends (a value omitted from the rendered menu; the same button clicked twice; a stale session id) and what the code does about it. Two decidable backstops in the repo's own checker: (1) a handler consuming interaction `values`/`custom_id` as a lookup key must call a visibility/authority helper before dispatch — flag handlers that index a registry with client input and reach no authority call on any path; (2) a reward-granting handler must either invalidate/expire its session id or re-charge the cost on the same path — flag grant calls with no expiry/spend in the same function.

name: Externally-authored text crossed into an execution or model-context boundary
one_line: Attacker-controlled strings (branch names, PR titles) were interpolated straight into a shell program or the first-turn model context with no allowlist or trust boundary.
trigger: Edit/Write of `.github/workflows/*.y*ml` where `${{ github.* }}` appears inside a `run:` block, or of a hook that reads remote repository metadata into session context.
why_it_happens: In a single-owner estate every string on the wire feels like the owner's own. The agent treats `head_ref` and PR titles as its own metadata rather than as text a stranger can write, and both surfaces (workflow YAML, hook stdout) are exactly the places where data silently becomes program. Both defects were introduced by PRs whose stated purpose was to ADD a safeguard.
instances: fleet-manager PR #833 — https://github.com/menno420/fleet-manager/pull/833#discussion_r3743547122 — `github.head_ref` interpolated into the workflow shell before Bash parses it; a branch named `claude/";exit${IFS}0;#` turns the gate step into an early `exit 0`, bypassing the gate the step existed to enforce

fleet-manager PR #845 — https://github.com/menno420/fleet-manager/pull/845#discussion_r3757343229 — first-turn hook injects PR titles from a public repo verbatim into model context, a prompt-injection path opened before the session has done any work
proposed_fix: `tools/check_untrusted_interpolation.py`, wired into `substrate-gate` (already a required check on `main`) beside `check_no_false_walls.py`: (a) fail any `${{\s*github\.(head_ref|ref_name|event\.[^}]*)\s*}}` occurring inside a `run:` block — require binding through `env:` and referencing as `"$VAR"`; (b) fail any hook that writes a remote-authored field (PR/issue title, body, comment, branch name) into `additionalContext`/stdout unless the emission is wrapped in a declared untrusted-data fence and the hook id is listed in `.claude/hooks/untrusted-sources.json` with the source named. Pair with doc-routes id `remote-text-into-context`, tools [Edit, Write], when: ["github\\.head_ref", "pull_request\\.title", "\\$\\{\\{\\s*github\\.event"].
already_covered_by: none — no workflow linter is wired anywhere in the repo (grep for actionlint/zizmor over .github/, tools/, scripts/ returns nothing), and none of the existing checkers (check_no_false_walls, check_pipe_exit_code, check_doc_routes, check_claim_propagation) touch expression interpolation or hook output
owner_flagged_premise: VOID — the lane that set this assumed every menno420-authored review comment was the owner speaking. The identity-collision finding (docs/findings/2026-08-29-estate-agent-error-audit.md §1) establishes that agents post under the owner PAT, so no GitHub text is attributable to him. name: A coarse selector where the precise one was available
one_line: Enumerated by 'everything present' — filesystem walk, wildcard permission — instead of the semantic unit (tracked files, the specific command), silently widening blast radius.
trigger: Edit/Write adding a `:*` wildcard grant to a tracked `settings*.json`, or `os.walk`/`Path.rglob`/`glob(` inside code on a publish, bundle, upload, or release path.
why_it_happens: The coarse selector is the one that makes the task at hand finish: the walk finds every file the bundle needs, the wildcard stops every permission prompt during a long audit. Both are correct for the session that wrote them and wrong for every session after, and neither leaves a visible symptom in the diff — the widening is what does NOT appear.
instances: fleet-manager PR #839 — https://github.com/menno420/fleet-manager/pull/839#discussion_r3752950221 — committed `Bash(python3:*)` into tracked `.claude/settings.local.json`, which runs arbitrary filesystem/process/network/git operations via `python3 -c` and silently widens every future session past the deliberately narrow project settings

fleet-manager PR #934 — https://github.com/menno420/fleet-manager/pull/934#discussion_r3839332420 — publishable sources selected by filesystem walk rather than `git ls-files`; reviewer reproduced an untracked `.env` and `.git/config` emitted into `sources/` with contents, leaking credentials into a public upload/release
proposed_fix: `tools/check_broad_selectors.py` in `check --strict` + `substrate-gate`: (a) fail any diff that adds a `"Bash(...:*)"` or bare `:*` grant to a TRACKED `.claude/settings*.json` — task-specific grants must stay untracked and `settings.local.json` must be gitignored, checked by asserting `git check-ignore` succeeds on it; (b) fail `os.walk|rglob|glob\(` inside any module whose CLI or docstring advertises publish/bundle/release/upload unless the enumeration derives from `git ls-files` output, with a required regression fixture containing an untracked `.env` and a `.git/` directory that must yield an empty selection.
already_covered_by: none — no trap, no doc-route, and no kit/local checker fires at this trigger moment

name: Owner-facing CLI shipped with an untested interface
one_line: A tool handed to the owner produces the wrong artifact at exit 0, or crashes on the very platform it was written for, because no flag combination was ever run.
trigger: Write/Edit of a `tools/*.py` argparse surface intended for the owner to run by hand — new flags, or a platform-conditional code path.
why_it_happens: The agent tests the one invocation it cares about, on the one platform it is running on, and infers the interface from the code it just wrote. Both failures are invisible from inside the container: the flag conflict exits 0, and the Windows path cannot be exercised at all — so 'it worked when I ran it' is true and useless. Cost lands entirely on the owner, at the moment he is trying to use the deliverable.
instances: fleet-manager PR #946 — https://github.com/menno420/fleet-manager/pull/946#discussion_r3851721702 — send-day renderer: `--html --count > mail.html` exits 0 but writes the count report, `--html --verify` writes verification prose; the owner opens and copies the wrong artifact with no error, no argparse mutually exclusive group

fleet-manager PR #947 — https://github.com/menno420/fleet-manager/pull/947#discussion_r3864685607 — Windows-targeted fallback shells out to Unix `which`, so `_have_gh()` raises `FileNotFoundError` on the exact platform the fallback exists to support, before the advertised `gh api` path or the friendly error can run
proposed_fix: `tools/check_cli_contract.py` in `check --strict`, three predicates over changed `tools/*.py`: (a) any two flags that gate the same output sink and are resolved by implementation order must sit in an `add_mutually_exclusive_group()` — detect by AST: multiple `args.X` branches returning/writing to the same handle with no group registration; (b) fail any `subprocess.*(["which"|"where"], ...)` — require `shutil.which`; (c) any tool whose docstring/README names Windows or 'the laptop' must ship a smoke test invoked with a PATH stripped of Unix coreutils, or be relabelled Linux-only. Plus one step in `prep-owner-steps`: run every documented flag combination once and paste each artifact's first line into the session card before handing the tool over.
already_covered_by: Nothing. No existing checker or documented trap covers either predicate — `tools/check_pipe_exit_code.py` (TRAP-002) is the nearest sibling in spirit ("verify with real exit codes") but tests an unrelated construct, and no doc in `docs/` or `.claude/` mentions argparse mutual exclusion or cross-platform executable lookup. `maps_to_existing_trap: new` is correct.

name: Hook declared working without a control for each input kind it sees
one_line: A hook was shipped after testing only the case it was written for, so the other payload kind or the non-execution position was never exercised.
trigger: Edit/Write under `.claude/hooks/` that adds a matched token to a pattern table, or reads `hook_event_name` / handles more than one event type.
why_it_happens: A hook that fires on the case you wrote it for looks finished, and a hook that fires too often looks safe — noise reads as caution rather than as a defect. The estate already has the answer for queries (TRAP-003's positive control) but never extended it to instruments: nothing required a must-be-silent case, and nothing required a case per event type, so a single code path over two payload shapes passed review. Note the second instance landed 18 days after the first, on the hook layer, in the same repo.
instances: fleet-manager PR #835 — https://github.com/menno420/fleet-manager/pull/835#discussion_r3745224934 — trigger-tools guard matched the bare strings `eval`/`source` anywhere in a command, so writing a file named `source.md` tripped it; reviewer reproduced inert warnings on `6388db4c`, training sessions to ignore the estate's only denying hook

fleet-manager PR #952 — https://github.com/menno420/fleet-manager/pull/952#discussion_r3872810657 — checkout-prefix stripping applied to the `UserPromptSubmit` payload as if it were a file path, mangling the owner's own words and breaking the route he had explicitly named; two event kinds with different payload types handled by one code path
proposed_fix: `tools/check_hook_controls.py` in `check --strict`, modelled on the existing `tools/test_doc_route_patterns.py` (17 pinned cases) and `tools/test_trigger_tools_guard.py`: for every changed file under `.claude/hooks/`, require a sibling `tools/test_<hook>.py` in which (a) every literal token/regex in the hook's match table appears in at least one MUST-FIRE and one MUST-BE-SILENT case — for command matchers the silent case must place the token in a non-execution position (`source.md`, `evaluate`), and (b) every `hook_event_name` the hook branches on has at least one case, with the prompt-text event asserting that no path transformation was applied to the payload. Fail the gate when a token or event kind gains a matcher without both controls.

name: Vacuous universal over an unverified-empty set
one_line: 'Every element passed' is declared over a collection nobody asserted was non-empty — zero check runs read as all-green, skipped platform cases read as executed — so the strongest-sounding verdict in the record is the one backed by no observations at all.
trigger: Edit/Write matching `all\(|\.every\(|\ball (checks|tests|cases|runs) (are |were )?(green|passing|passed)\b|\bevery returned item\b` where the iterated collection derives from an API list response or a test-result set; and Bash/Edit of a suite invocation whose skip count is not read.
why_it_happens: `all([])` is True, and both a language and a CI API will hand you an empty list without complaint — a rate limit, a queue that has not started, an unsupported platform. The verdict then reads as maximally strong precisely where the evidence is nil. Distinct from the 'never observed red' pattern above: there the instrument was incapable, here the instrument was fine and the population was empty. Only two named instances, but both sit on a merge path, which is why it is worth a predicate rather than a note.
instances: fm #367 r3610761395 — agent merge policy verifies every returned check is green and accepts the EMPTY set, merging an unverified workflow change; the existing merge workflow already had the safeguard being dropped

fm #908 r3836836422 — codex-hook contract suite declared green when the Windows `commandWindows` path was never executed; a skip counted as a pass, so the platform branch the tests exist to cover carried no evidence
proposed_fix: A cardinality assertion, enforced in two places. (1) Merge-readiness rule and its lint: `len(check_runs) >= 1 and all(completed) and all(success)` — never `all(...)` alone; `tools/check_vacuous_all_green.py` flags any `all(...)`/`.every(...)` over a collection derived from an API list response or a test-result set with no preceding emptiness guard, and flags a green verdict written from a check listing whose count is not stated in the same record. (2) Suites report executed vs skipped and the gate reads both: run with `-rs`, parse the skip count, and fail when a DECLARED contract case is skipped rather than executed (a skip on a case the contract names is red, not green); the pass count may never be published without the skip count beside it. (3) Add the pair as an origin to the TRAP-003 register entry — 'the empty set is the same defect as the empty grep, one layer down.'
maps_to_existing_trap: new (vacuous-universal); folds naturally into TRAP-003 as a second ORIGIN, with TRAP-004 adjacent on the count half
already_covered_by: TRAP-004 · "A claim wider than the sample that produced it" (/home/user/fleet-manager/docs/traps.md) already covers this as its degenerate case. Its TRIGGER names universals explicitly ("a fraction, a total, or a universal (*'only 3 of 26'*, *'none of the other 25'*, *'every repo'*) covering a population larger than the set you actually measured") — a universal over an empty set is that with N=0 — and its REQUIRED PREVENTION is literally the proposed fix: "state **N measured of M total**". Its route `claim-beyond-the-sample` was already widened 2026-08-26 (fm #950) to fire on count-only forms, and `tools/test_doc_route_patterns.py` pins 17 cases. TRAP-003 (absence of evidence recorded as evidence of absence) is the adjacent half — "an empty result proves your *query ran*, not that the world is empty" is the same argument one layer down. The pattern's own `maps_to_existing_trap` field concedes this. The genuine, cheap residual is that the `claim-beyond-the-sample` noun allowlist (repos/repositories/files/entries/cards/commits/sessions) does not include checks/runs/tests, which is why "Every check on the head is green" would not fire — a one-line widening plus a test case in tools/test_doc_route_patterns.py, not a new trap and not a new checker.

name: A committed hard rail not checked before touching its named target
one_line: A destructive or mutating action is proposed or executed against a service the owner's committed hard rail names as protected or never-touch — sometimes in the same card that restates the rail.
trigger: PreToolUse on Bash / MCP tool calls whose text matches a destructive verb — `\b(serviceInstanceUpdate|serviceDelete|volumeDelete|databaseDelete|deploymentRemove|DROP\s+(DATABASE|TABLE)|pg_dump[\s\S]{0,200}\b(drop|delete)|gh\s+repo\s+delete|rm\s+-rf)\b` — and on Edit/Write of any plan text matching `\b(dump[- ]and[- ]delete|decommission|tear down|delete the (service|database|volume))\b`. Route ids `hard-rail-target` (Bash, `repeat: true`) + `destructive-plan-write`.
why_it_happens: The rail is prose in a document; the action is an API call in a different modality, and no surface converts one into the other. Restating the rail in the card demonstrably does not bind — #863 restated it and mutated the named service anyway.
instances: fm #861 r3783109610 — the protected set in `reliable-grace` miscounted and an owner-protected Postgres database placed on a dump-and-delete path as ordinary cleanup rather than an explicit hard-rail amendment

fm #863 r3783746269 — a `serviceInstanceUpdate` mutation recorded against `worker`, two lines below the same card's restatement that the unchanged hard rail is "never touch `worker`", with the persisted invariant left unnarrowed
proposed_fix: Extend the estate's one denying-hook pattern (`.claude/hooks/trigger_tools_guard.py` is precedent — no judgement in this rule either). A `PreToolUse` guard builds the protected-name set once per session by grepping the committed rails (`\b(hard rail|never touch|protected|do not delete)\b` lines in `docs/`, `.sessions/`, and each repo's `docs/current-state.md`) for backticked identifiers; when a destructive verb fires and the command contains a protected identifier, it BLOCKS with the rail's own quoted line and the amendment path ("this requires an explicit owner amendment to the hard rail — say so in your reply"). Deterministic companion in `check --strict`: fail any diff recording a mutation whose target matches a `never touch` name in the same tree unless the same diff narrows the invariant and cites the authorizing OD/quote — the exact gap #863's reviewer named, where the record cannot distinguish an authorized change from a violation.

name: Owner-gated item stranded outside the owner queue
one_line: A session creates a genuinely owner-only decision or blocking question and records it only in a session card or a planning doc, never as an OQ- slug in docs/owner-queue.md, so normal orientation never surfaces it.
trigger: Edit/Write of `.sessions/*.md` or `docs/**` whose added text matches owner-gating phrasing — 'owner call', 'owner decision', 'owner-only', 'ask the owner', 'needs the owner', 'waiting on him', 'must be answered first', 'blocked until he' — in a diff that adds no new `OQ-` slug to docs/owner-queue.md.
why_it_happens: The card is where the session is already writing, and writing the flag there feels like recording it. The queue is a second file, in a second diff hunk, and nothing fails when it is skipped — the ask simply becomes invisible at the exact moment it is supposed to be surfaced.
instances: fleet-manager PR #870 — discussion_r3825809106 (missing LICENSE left as an owner call, flagged only in the session card)
fleet-manager PR #938 — discussion_r3841797420 (new blocking owner question written into a planning doc, never registered in the owner queue)
proposed_fix: New checker `tools/check_owner_asks_registered.py` in `scripts/preflight.py`. Predicate: over `git diff main...HEAD` added lines in `docs/**` and `.sessions/**`, match `/(owner (call|decision|only|must (decide|choose|answer))|ask(ing)? the owner|needs? the owner|waiting on (him|the owner)|must be answered (first|before)|blocked until he)/i`; if any line hits, the same diff must add at least one line matching `^\s*[-*#|]?\s*`?OQ-[A-Z0-9-]+` to `docs/owner-queue.md`, and that slug must also appear at the hit site (so the card and the queue cross-reference). Exit 1 naming file:line of every unregistered hit; `--selftest` fixture per pattern. Allowlist: `docs/owner-queue.md` itself and lines inside an explicit `[historical]`/`consumed` block. Companion route `owner-gated-item-write` (Edit/Write, `repeat: true`, docs matching docs/owner-queue.md): 'You just wrote an owner-only ask. A session card is not the queue — docs/owner-queue.md declares itself the one deduplicated list of things genuinely waiting on him, and it is what a fresh session reads. Add the OQ- slug in THIS diff and cite it here.' Add the same step to the `session-close` skill's close-out list, after the card write and before the flip.

name: Transient HTTP/transport failure hardcoded as a terminal status

name: A constraint written into a governing record that its own source does not support
one_line: A limit that no directive states and no probe measured is written into a record that briefs or routes future sessions — an invented OD-6 cap in a handoff card, a port-wide TCP wall in the capability ledger — so the fabrication propagates as estate law.
trigger: Edit/Write of .sessions/*.md, docs/**, CAPABILITIES.md or a PR body whose added lines either (a) cite a directive id (OD-\d+, PL-\d+, D-\d{4}, R\d{1,2}) as justification, or (b) state a categorical capability negative (cannot, is blocked, not possible, all/every/no ... blocked).
why_it_happens: Nothing in this estate checks a citation against its source. Writing 'per OD-6' costs one token and reads as authority to every downstream session, and the boot file's own precedence rules make a card's stated directive hard to argue with later. Combined with check_no_false_walls being scoped to CAPABILITIES.md, both the fabricated-authority and the over-scoped-probe shapes land in exactly the records that route future work, which is where a wall does the most damage per instance.
instances: fleet-manager PR #940 discussion_r3842987836 — 'four landings in one session is not OD-6' invented a per-session landing cap, attributed it to the owner, and wrote it into three places including the card that briefs the follow-up sessions; OD-6 says one thing at a time done properly and explicitly is not a reason to stop short

Both halves of fm #940 fail: no quote, and no substring of OD-6 mentions a count. (2) Widen tools/check_no_false_walls.py past CAPABILITIES.md to every record surface, and add a scope predicate: a categorical capability negative must carry, in the same sentence, either an N-of-M figure or a scope qualifier naming the hosts/ports actually probed — fm #867's 'all outbound non-443 TCP' fails on two probes of two Railway hosts. name: Mutating POST with no replay identity
one_line: A POST handler that creates a remote resource derives its identity from server wall-clock and answers with a rendered page, so an exact replay (refresh, retried tab, lost response, restart) publishes a second record, branch and PR.
trigger: Edit/Write of a request handler that both (a) is reachable by POST (`@app.post`, `@app.route(..., methods=[... "POST" ...])`, `def post(`) and (b) performs an external write (branch/commit/PR create, `requests.post|put|patch`) — fires before the first mutating call is written, and again on any `return render...` inside such a handler.
why_it_happens: The happy path is written and hand-tested exactly once, and replay is invisible in a single manual submit. A timestamp looks like a unique id, which is the trap: same-second replay silently collides and different-second replay silently forks, so neither failure appears until a public duplicate exists. Nothing in the estate's guards looks at HTTP method or response type.
instances: websites PR #523 — https://github.com/menno420/websites/pull/523#discussion_r3871837895 — exact POST/body replay created a second record, branch and PR; no submission key, no deterministic record id (OWNER-voiced)

websites PR #523 — https://github.com/menno420/websites/pull/523#discussion_r3871760248 — handler returned a template render from the POST with no redirect, record id derived from a second-resolution timestamp, so a browser refresh publishes a duplicate public record and PR
proposed_fix: Deterministic checker `tools/check_post_idempotency.py`, wired into `scripts/preflight.py` so `python3 bootstrap.py check --strict` fails on it. Predicate, per handler function that is POST-reachable AND contains an external write: (1) every terminal `return` on the success path must be a redirect (`RedirectResponse|redirect(|status_code=30[237]`) — a `render`/template return fails; (2) the record/branch identity must be derived from a token present in the REQUEST (`form.get(...)`, `request.json[...]`, names matching `idempotency|submission_key|dedupe`) — a `datetime.now()|time.time()|uuid4()` computed inside the handler fails; (3) the module must have a companion test that issues the identical POST body twice and asserts one record, one branch, one PR (grep the test tree for the handler name plus a double-post assertion; absent test = fail). Delivery route `mutating-post-replay` (tools: Edit, Write; when: `@(app|router|bp)\.post\(`, `methods\s*=\s*\[[^\]]*["']POST`, `def post\(self`) quoting both #523 findings verbatim, since the second one landed after the first was fixed on the same PR.

name: Clearance carried over from a stale head
one_line: A verdict earned on an earlier SHA is treated as covering the current head, so correction commits — the ones review just forced — merge unreviewed.
trigger: Edit/Write that sets `Status: complete` on an in-diff `.sessions/*.md` card, and the `git push` that follows it (existing routes `card-flip-to-complete` and `card-flip-before-push`, the latter already `repeat: true`). Also fires on Edit/Write of any doc that states a clean-verdict procedure.
why_it_happens: The review answered, so the session's mental state flips to 'reviewed' and stays there across the push that invalidates it. Nothing in the tree changes when the head moves, so every tree-level guard still reads green; the only surface that knows the verdict is stale is the PR, which no gate reads. TRAP-007's own coverage table declares a checker impossible ('a checker would have to know a review was requested, which is PR state, not tree state') — that is the excuse that keeps this class unenforced, and it is wrong: $GITHUB_PAT reads PR state from this container.
instances: fleet-manager PR #828 — https://github.com/menno420/fleet-manager/pull/828#discussion_r3741433987 — session-close sequence permits flipping the card complete immediately after applying review fixes, while the review is bound to the pre-fix SHA

fleet-manager PR #925 — https://github.com/menno420/fleet-manager/pull/925#discussion_r3838430981 — capabilities-ledger shortcut treats any Codex issue comment as a clean verdict, omitting the head-SHA match the canonical section requires
proposed_fix: Build the checker TRAP-007 says cannot exist: `tools/check_review_covers_head.py`, wired into `scripts/preflight.py` so `python3 bootstrap.py check --strict` fails. Predicate: IF an in-diff `.sessions/*.md` card reads `Status:\s*complete` AND a PR exists for the current branch, THEN require a verdict bound to `git rev-parse HEAD` — `review.commit_id == head` for review objects, or (clean pass, no review object) `Reviewed commit: <head>` in an `/issues/{n}/comments` body, falling back to `head in {40-hex strings extracted from the body}` (presence, not position — one of them is the merge preview). Exit non-zero otherwise, with the two escape hatches named in the message: leave the card `in-progress`, or apply `do-not-automerge` BEFORE the push. Delete the 'not yet / PR state, not tree state' cell from the coverage table when it lands.
already_covered_by: TRAP-007 (`docs/traps.md:292`) — rule + prevention + both clean-pass body shapes + the `do-not-automerge`-before-push escape hatch, delivered by two routes (`card-flip-to-complete`, `card-flip-before-push` with `repeat: true`); and `.claude/skills/session-close/SKILL.md` step 6c. name: A verdict predicate built from an impoverished read
one_line: The gate asks 'did something appear on the one surface I poll?' instead of decoding the verdict — so CHANGES_REQUESTED, a summary-only P1, and 'no answer yet' all read as clearance.
trigger: Edit/Write/MultiEdit whose added text implements or documents a review-verdict test — regex `chatgpt-codex-connector|@codex\b|/pulls/[^/\s]+/(reviews|comments)|/issues/[^/\s]+/comments|review (exists|found|answered|appeared)|no review appeared`. (Today `codex-verdict-poll` fires only on Bash polling, i.e. at execution time, never when the predicate is being written.)
why_it_happens: The measured contract is split across three endpoints with different semantics — findings arrive as inline comments on `/pulls/{n}/comments`, the state lives on the review object, a CLEAN pass creates no review object at all and lands in `/issues/{n}/comments` — and every session re-implements the predicate from whichever half it happens to remember. There is no single callable decoder, so each re-implementation drops a different piece: #362 dropped `state` and `body`, #951 dropped the issue-comment surface. Both failure directions are live in this repo right now: `scripts/r30_merge_check.py:264-313` decodes state, head-binding and P1/P2 badges correctly but reads only `/reviews` and `/pulls/{n}/comments`, so a genuine clean pass is indistinguishable from silence and returns REVIEW forever.
instances: fleet-manager PR #362 — https://github.com/menno420/fleet-manager/pull/362#discussion_r3610587904 — merge gate accepted any current-head Codex review without inspecting `state` or the review-level `body`

fleet-manager PR #951 — https://github.com/menno420/fleet-manager/pull/951#discussion_r3866945910 — rollout sequence for A3–A11 specified a six-minute wait reading only the inline-comment surface, contradicting the repo's own measured record
proposed_fix: Three links. (1) ONE decoder, no re-implementations: extend `scripts/r30_merge_check.py` with the third surface it currently misses — `/issues/{n}/comments` plus both observed clean-comment shapes — and expose `codex_verdict(owner, repo, n, head) -> {surfaces_read: [reviews, pull_comments, issue_comments], state, head_bound: bool, p1p2: int, verdict: PASS|REVIEW|ABSENT}`; every gate, skill and doc cites that function instead of describing an endpoint. (2) Route `review-verdict-predicate` on Edit/Write with the regex above → `docs/CAPABILITIES.md` § 'Codex's CLEAN verdict is an issue comment' + `docs/traps.md` TRAP-007's shape table, saying: presence is not a verdict — you must read all three surfaces, decode `state` and severity badges from the BODY, and match the head SHA; 'no review appeared' is a claim about your query, not about the reviewer (TRAP-003). (3) Pin it: add must-fire cases to `tools/test_doc_route_patterns.py` and a fixture pair under `scripts/fixtures/r30/` — one CHANGES_REQUESTED, one summary-only P1, one clean-issue-comment — so a future narrowing of the predicate fails a test instead of looking like a simplification.

NOT covered: (1) the `state`/CHANGES_REQUESTED and summary-only-P1-badge half — TRAP-007 is exclusively about head-SHA binding of an already-decoded verdict and never mentions decoding state or severity from the body, so the #362 direction has no trap entry at all; (2) the Edit/Write authoring moment, since codex-verdict-poll is Bash-only and the write-time route is path-scoped to .sessions/*.md; (3) the single-decoder consolidation — scripts/r30_merge_check.py is the only implementation and it reads two of three surfaces.
